title: [Fix/Kernel] Add JIT rmsnorm_hf kernel to fix transformers backend MMLU accuracy regression
author: Jiminator
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Commit `34ddf135fd` introduced `recursive_replace()` in `TransformersBase`, which replaced every HF `*RMSNorm` module with SGLang's `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm`. The two kernels differ in rounding order: `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm` multiplies the weight in fp32 then casts, while HF's `LlamaRMSNorm` casts the normalized output to the activation dtype first, then multiplies. Under int4wo-128 quantization this ~1-ULP difference compounds across 32 transformer layers and flips 3 borderline MMLU questions (0.703 → 0.656).  

#22435 introduced a naive fix which was reverting the change, but that led to a significant perf regression.
                                                  
This PR adds a JIT kernel (`rmsnorm_hf`) that replicates HF's cast-before-weight-multiply order exactly, recovering accuracy with less throughput regression.                     

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/rmsnorm_hf.cuh`** (new): 512-thread scalar-strided RMSNorm kernel with HF semantics. Caches input   
  values in per-thread registers between the two passes to halve global memory reads. Supports fp16/bf16, PDL (Hopper+).                             
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/rmsnorm_hf.py`** (new): Python wrapper using `cache_once` + `load_jit`. Supports `hidden_size` that is a multiple of 
  512 (covers all Llama/Qwen/Mistral models).                             
  - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_rmsnorm_hf.py`** (new): Correctness tests against PyTorch HF reference, out-param test, hidden-size
  predicate test. Registered for `stage-b-kernel-unit-1-gpu-large` and `nightly-kernel-1-gpu`.                                                       
  - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`**: When `cast_x_before_out_mul=True`, `forward_cuda` dispatches to `jit_kernel.rmsnorm_hf` (falls back
  to `forward_native` for unsupported hidden sizes or non-CUDA).          
  - **`python/sglang/srt/models/transformers.py`**: Sets `cast_x_before_out_mul=True` in `replace_rms_norm_class` for the non-Gemma path so the
  transformers backend uses HF rounding.    

## Accuracy Tests
On a H100:

After Fix: 0.703 (Accuracy fully recovered)

After Fix: 845.62 tok/s

title: [Pipeline Parallelism][Bug] Fix scheduler hang in pipeline parallelism setup
author: jonahbernard
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
There is a bug in SGLang servers that use pipeline parallelism. The bug causes the server to hang for prefill requests due to  `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` always returning `None` on every iteration of the main scheduler event loop.

I'll run through an example using `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` with `self.pp_size=2`:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
    --moe-runner-backend triton \
    --disable-cuda-graph \
    --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph \
    --chunked-prefill-size 64 \
    --max-running-requests 1 \
    --port 30004 \
    --pp-size 2
```

The bug occurs here in sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:

```python
        if (
            self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
            and self.chunked_req is not None
            and not self.enable_priority_preemption
        ):
            self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
            return None
```

In this SGLang server PP=2, so `get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((pp.max_micro_batch_size - running_bs), self.req_to_token_pool.available_size())`.

`pp.max_micro_batch_size = max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1)` so `pp.max_micro_batch_size = 1`.

`self.req_to_token_pool.available_size() = len(self.free_slots)` and the free slots are initialized to `self.free_slots = list(range(size))`.

In ou server's `req_to_token_pool`, `size = max_num_reqs` and `max_num_reqs = min(max_num_reqs // self.dp_size, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

`self.dp_size=1`, which gives us:

`max_num_reqs = min(max_num_reqs, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

This gives us `get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1) - running_bs), min(max_num_reqs, max(min(int(token_capacity / self.model_config.context_len * 512), 4096), 2048))`

We have `token_capacity = 4960064` and `self.model_config.context_len = 40960`, which gives us:

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1) - running_bs), min(max_num_reqs, 4096))`

`max_running_requests=1` so we get:

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((1 - running_bs), 1)` before any requests are sent, which will allow the first prefill batch to be returned by `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw`.

If a single large prompt is sent, it will be broken into chunks. The prompt's `Req` instance will be assigned to `self.chunked_req` and a req slot will be allocated in the req_to_token_pool, which started with 1 free slot so now it will have 0 free slots. Thus,

`get_num_allocatable_reqs = min((1 - running_bs), 0 (len(free_slots)) = 0` which means

```python
        if (
            self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
            and self.chunked_req is not None
            and not self.enable_priority_preemption
        ):
            self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
            return None
```

will evaluate to True on every iteration of the scheduler's event loop, and no new requests will make progress, nor will the current request. Thus, the server will hang for lots of users.

When pipeline parallelism was first added to SGLang (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/5724), this check actually always allowed the next chunk of a chunked prefill prompt to be returned in the new batch, and the check was `not self.chunked_req` instead of `self.chunked_req is not None`, which are logically opposite.

A bug was introduced in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14883 when that check was subtly inverted. The check went from `if not self.chunked_req` to `if self.chunked_req is not None`. 

## Modifications

Change `if self.chunked_req is not None` back to `if self.chunked_req is None`.

title: [LoRA] Fix EP + per-expert MoE LoRA illegal memory access
author: jybsuper
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs prevent `--tp N --ep M --enable-lora --lora-backend triton --moe-runner-backend triton` from running on any MoE model with per-expert LoRA adapters; both reliably crash in the first forward pass with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. This PR fixes both and adds unit coverage.

### Bug 1 — `LoRAMemoryPool` sizes per-expert buffers for the global expert count

`FusedMoEWithLoRA` allocates LoRA A/B buffers via `LoRAMemoryPool`, whose per-expert shape was `[num_loras, num_global_experts, ...]`. Under EP, however, `StandardDispatcher` remaps `topk_ids` from global → local IDs *before* the MoE kernel (see `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`), so both the base MoE weights and the LoRA delta kernels are indexed with IDs in `[0, num_local_experts)` plus a `-1` sentinel. A LoRA buffer sized `[..., 128, ...]` being indexed with local IDs `[0, 32)` therefore reads the wrong expert's weights (or, combined with bug #2, triggers the illegal access).

### Bug 2 — `moe_lora_align_block_size` doesn't filter the `-1` sentinel in one branch

`_count_and_sort_expert_tokens` only rejected `expert_id >= num_experts`:

```cpp
for (size_t i = tid; i < numel; i += stride) {
  int32_t expert_id = topk_ids[i];
  if (expert_id >= num_experts) { continue; }      // <-- no `< 0`
  ...
  int32_t rank_post_pad = atomicAdd(
    &cumsum_buffer[(model_offset * (num_experts + 1)) + expert_id], 1);
  sorted_token_ids[max_num_tokens_padded * model_offset + rank_post_pad] = i;
}
```

`-1` passes that guard and produces:
- `atomicAdd(&cumsum_buffer[model_offset * (num_experts+1) + (-1)], 1)` — OOB write (negative stride), and
- `sorted_token_ids[offset + rank_post_pad]` with a garbage `rank_post_pad`.

Both sibling call sites in the same file already guard `expert_id < 0 || expert_id >= num_experts`. This PR makes the third call site consistent.

## Changes

- **`python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py`**
  - Capture `(moe_ep_size, moe_ep_rank)` and `moe_use_local_expert_ids` at pool init. The latter is `True` iff `moe_ep_size > 1` **and** the active runner remaps to local IDs (Triton/DeepGEMM/Marlin) — the check is skipped for runners that keep global IDs (FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuteDSL / TRTLLM-routed), so their buffers stay globally-keyed.
  - Size per-expert LoRA buffers by `num_local_experts` (`get_lora_A_shape` / `get_lora_B_shape`).
  - Route all four per-expert load paths in `load_lora_weight_to_buffer` through a new `_iter_local_expert_weights(weights)` helper that filters and remaps global → local expert IDs for both `dict` and 3D-tensor inputs, then zeros unowned/unloaded slots.
  - No-op for pure TP and for runners that keep global IDs — verified by the TP-only LoRA unit tests, which still pass unchanged.

- **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu`**
  - Add `expert_id < 0` to the guard in `_count_and_sort_expert_tokens`, matching the two other call sites; adds a comment explaining the sentinel contract with `StandardDispatcher`.

- **`test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`** (new, 22 cases, hermetic CPU-only)
  - `_get_num_experts` covering `num_experts`, `num_local_experts`, `n_routed_experts`, and fallbacks.
  - `_get_num_local_experts` under no-EP / EP=1 / EP=4 and uneven splits.
  - `_global_to_local_expert_id` ownership filter.
  - `_iter_local_expert_weights` for dict and 3D-tensor inputs, with correct remapping under EP.
  - `LoRAMemoryPool.__init__` EP-context capture for no-EP, Triton+EP, and FlashInfer+EP.

## Compatibility

- **Pure TP (any `--tp`, no `--ep`)**: `moe_ep_size == 1` → `moe_use_local_expert_ids == False` → buffers and iteration are identical to pre-fix behavior. Verified end-to-end with `--tp 2` + LoRA.
- **Pure EP**: per-rank buffers and remapping via `_iter_local_expert_weights`.
- **Mixed TP + EP**: same as pure EP — TP slicing already happened when the base model loaded; the LoRA fix only affects the expert dimension.
- **FlashInfer CUTLASS / CuteDSL / TRTLLM-routed**: `_moe_runner_keeps_global_expert_ids()` returns `True`, `moe_use_local_expert_ids` stays `False` → buffers stay globally-keyed, matching what those runners expect.
- **Non-LoRA paths**: untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py` — 22 passed.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...`
- [x] End-to-end regression that originally reproduced the crash:
  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
    --tp 4 --ep 4 \
    --enable-lora --max-loras-per-batch 1 --max-lora-rank 32 \
    --lora-target-modules all --lora-paths lora_alpha=<per-expert adapter> \
    --lora-backend triton --moe-runner-backend triton
  # curl /v1/completions -> before: CUDA illegal memory access in first forward
  #                        after : returns a completion successfully
  ```
- [x] `--tp 4 --ep 4` base (no `--enable-lora`) still works.
- [x] `--tp 2` (no EP) + LoRA still works (regression for the non-EP path).

title: [diffusion] Fix --warmup-resolutions hang with --enable-cfg-parallel
author: mispa-ms
body:
## Summary

Fixes a 30-minute silent hang when SGLang-diffusion is launched with `--enable-cfg-parallel --warmup --warmup-resolutions <list>`. The synthesized warmup `Req`s were built with `Req(prompt="", negative_prompt="", ...)`, which auto-created a base `SamplingParams` with `guidance_scale=1.0`. `Req.validate()` left `do_classifier_free_guidance=False`, so in CFG-parallel mode rank 1 skipped the positive pass, returned `None` for `noise_pred`, and `scheduler.step()` crashed with:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'Tensor' and 'NoneType'
  at scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete.py:537
```

The exception was caught inside `GPUWorker`, `/health` kept returning 200, and the crash only surfaced as a 30-minute `gloo` broadcast timeout (`dist_timeout=3600`) when real requests arrived — turning a 7-second logic error into a half-hour silent hang.

## Root cause chain

1. `Scheduler.prepare_server_warmup_reqs` (`scheduler.py:238-258`) synthesizes `Req(prompt="", negative_prompt="")` with no `sampling_params` argument.
2. `Req.__init__` (`schedule_batch.py:169-182`) auto-creates a **base** `SamplingParams()` (not the model-specific subclass) on the first `setattr` of a SamplingParams field. Base defaults include `guidance_scale=1.0`.
3. `Req.validate` (`schedule_batch.py:270-285`) only sets `do_classifier_free_guidance=True` when `cfg_scale > 1.0 AND negative_prompt is not None`. With `cfg_scale=1.0`, the flag stays `False`.
4. `_predict_noise_with_cfg` (`denoising.py:1596-1621`) returns `noise_pred_cond=None` on `cfg_rank != 0` when `do_cfg=False`.
5. `scheduler.step(model_output=None)` crashes at `prev_sample = sample + dt * model_output` in `scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete.py:537`.

## Repro

```bash
sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 --num-gpus 2 \
    --enable-cfg-parallel --warmup --warmup-resolutions 512x512 1024x1024 \
    --enable-torch-compile --trust-remote-code
# Hangs ~30 min, then scheduler terminates with:
#   Error receiving requests in scheduler event loop (attempt 1/3):
#   [/pytorch/third_party/gloo/gloo/transport/tcp/unbound_buffer.cc:78]
#   Timed out waiting 1800000ms for recv operation to complete
```

## Before / After

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Warmup with `--warmup-resolutions --enable-cfg-parallel` | 30-min gloo timeout + rank-1 death | Works |
| Real request without CFG to cfg-parallel server | 30-min gloo timeout + rank-1 death | Instant `ValueError` |
| Real request with CFG (cfg-parallel on or off) | Works | Works (unchanged) |
| Warmup without `--enable-cfg-parallel` (image or text) | Works | Works (byte-identical `Req` kwargs) |

## Commits

1. **`[diffusion] scheduler: fix warmup Req synthesis under --enable-cfg-parallel`**
   `prepare_server_warmup_reqs` now builds the warmup `Req` via conditional kwargs. When `enable_cfg_parallel` is on, it sets `do_classifier_free_guidance=True` and `negative_prompt="warmup"` so rank 1 produces a valid `noise_pred_uncond` and `_combine_cfg_parallel`'s all-reduce succeeds. When cfg-parallel is off, the Req construction is byte-identical to the pre-fix behavior.

2. **`[diffusion] stages: reject non-CFG requests under --enable-cfg-parallel`**
   `InputValidationStage.forward` raises `ValueError` when the server was launched with `--enable-cfg-parallel` but the request has `do_classifier_free_guidance=False`. The error message distinguishes `negative_prompt` states (`not set` / `empty` / `set`) and notes that `negative_prompt_embeds` is also a valid way to enable CFG. Follows the existing per-request validation pattern (`input_validation.py:295-298`, `311-314`) and the server-args `_validate_cfg_parallel` at `server_args.py:1340-1343`. This is a defensive guard — not strictly required to fix the bug, but preempts the 30-min hang on any future misconfig or regression of commit 1.

3. **`[diffusion] test: add unit tests for --enable-cfg-parallel warmup fix`**
   Four CPU-only unit tests in `test/unit/test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` covering both commits (positive + regression for the scheduler fix; positive + negative for the input-validation guard).

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests pass locally (`pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` → 4/4 green).
- [x] Existing `test/unit/` suite still passes.
- [x] Full `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/` (excluding `server/` and `cli/`) → 154/155 passed, 1 pre-existing skip.
- [x] Integration validation: reran the failing Qwen-Image-2512 resolution sweep on 2x B200 with `--warmup-resolutions 512x512 1024x1024 --enable-cfg-parallel`. All cfg-parallel steps finish cleanly (previously all hung for 30 min).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The 30-min `gloo` broadcast timeout masks rank death — `/health` should reflect worker-process state, or the scheduler's recv loop should notice rank-1 termination faster.
- `Req.__init__` auto-creates a base `SamplingParams()` instead of the model-specific subclass when a caller omits the `sampling_params=` kwarg. Warmup is the only known affected caller today; an audit of all `Req(**kwargs)` construction sites is warranted.

title: [misc] CI hygiene: enforce __main__ entry, drop silent-skipped tests, fix rerun-test protoc
author: hnyls2002
body:
Misc CI hygiene bundle. Three independent changes:

## 1. Sanity check + streaming test fix

Pytest-style tests under `test/registered/` have been **silently skipping in CI**: the CI runner invokes each file via `python3 file.py -f` (not pytest), so files without an executable `if __name__ == "__main__":` block just import and exit zero. Every test function body has never run.

- **Sanity check** in `collect_tests`: every registered file with at least one enabled registry must have an executable `__main__` block (AST-verified). Files with all registries `disabled=...` (helpers, self-skipping multi-GPU benches) are exempt.
- **Streaming session unit test fix** (the immediate trigger): `_FakeReq.finished_len = None` (missing from fixture; real `Req` defaults to `None`) + proper `__main__` entry. Also dropped a stale test (`defers_tail_free`) whose intent was already superseded by #22897.

### Root cause (for context)

- `run_unittest_files` -> `subprocess.Popen(["python3", <file>, "-f"])` — assumes `unittest.main()` picks up `-f` as `--failfast`.
- Pytest-style files with no `unittest.main()` / no `__main__` block just import + exit 0. Zero tests executed, CI shows green.
- Easy to land silently during review, especially when migrating tests across directories.

### Kept files (6): `__main__` fix applied, tests now actually run

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_streaming_session_unit.py` — PR's immediate target (4 tests)
- `test/registered/debug_utils/comparator/test_preset.py`
- `test/registered/debug_utils/source_patcher/test_code_patcher.py`
- `test/registered/debug_utils/source_patcher/test_dumper_integration.py`
- `test/registered/debug_utils/source_patcher/test_source_editor.py`
- `test/registered/debug_utils/test_dump_comparator.py` — **also dropped `TestMainBasic` subset**: those 3 integration tests call `dump_comparator.main()` which hard-codes `x.cuda()` in `_load_tensor`, so they always raise `no NVIDIA driver` on the CPU suite they were registered in. Kept the 6 pure-CPU unit tests in the file. cc @fzyzcjy (originally added in #16285)

### Dropped files (9)

- `test/registered/quant/test_bnb.py` — cc @yhyang201
- `test/registered/quant/test_int4fp8_moe.py` — cc @fxmarty-amd (content #7392), @Ying1123 (framework #882)
- `test/registered/amd/test_zimage_turbo.py` — cc @michaelzhang-ai
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_dependency.py` — cc @DarkSharpness
- `test/registered/ops/test_repeat_interleave.py` — cc @yuan-luo
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_glm47_moe_detector.py` — cc @Leoyzen
- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_model_hooks.py` — cc @Carlomus
- `test/registered/rotary/test_mrope.py` — cc @yuan-luo (initial), @raayandhar (yarn feat #13313)
- `test/registered/vlm/test_patch_embed_perf.py` — perf assertion (linear-vs-conv3d speedup), prone to flakiness on shared GPU runners; silent-skip since day one. cc @yuan-luo

**If any original author wants a file revived**: reopen with a proper `__main__` block (see the pattern in `test_streaming_session_unit.py` at the bottom) so the file actually executes in CI.

## 2. Fix `rerun-test.yml` CPU job missing `protoc` / `rustup`

`rerun-test-cpu` (`.github/workflows/rerun-test.yml`) was `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` but missing the `Install protoc` + `Install Rust toolchain` steps that `pr-test.yml`'s `stage-a-test-cpu` has (at pr-test.yml:646-652). Installing `sglang` editable wheel compiles `sglang-grpc` Rust crate, whose `build.rs` needs `protoc` -> workflow fails in `Install dependencies` before pytest even starts.

Fix: mirror `pr-test.yml`'s setup — add the same two steps. Keeps rerun-test environment aligned with pr-test rather than forking into a docker-container approach.

title: [PD] Fix clip logic when state indices lens are mismatch
author: ShangmingCai
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Fix #18727.
In `MooncakeKVManager.maybe_send_extra`, the clip logic for SWA/NSA hybrid models only handled one direction of length mismatch between `prefill_state_indices` and `req.dst_state_indices`, and even that branch was effectively a no-op:
```python
if len(prefill_state_indices) < len(req.dst_state_indices):
    logger.warning(...)
    prefill_state_indices = prefill_state_indices[: len(req.dst_state_indices)]
```
Two issues:
1. When `prefill < dst`, slicing `prefill_state_indices` with an upper bound **larger than its own length** is a Python no-op: the list is returned unchanged, so the two sides remain mismatched.
2. The opposite case (`prefill > dst`) is not handled at all.
Whenever the two index arrays have different lengths, the downstream `_send_kvcache_generic` path calls `group_concurrent_contiguous`, which evaluates:
```python
brk = np.where((np.diff(src_indices) != 1) | (np.diff(dst_indices) != 1))[0] + 1
```
The bitwise-OR between two arrays of different shapes raises and causes the transfer to fail for SWA/NSA hybrid models under PD disaggregation.
## Modifications
`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py`:
- Handle both directions of length mismatch so the two index arrays always line up before being passed to `_send_kvcache_generic`:
  - `len(prefill) > len(dst)` → clip `prefill_state_indices` down to `len(dst)`.
  - `len(prefill) < len(dst)` → clip `dst_state_indices` down to `len(prefill)`.
- Introduce a local `dst_state_indices` variable instead of mutating `req.dst_state_indices` in place, so `TransferInfo` is not modified as a side effect of the clip.
- No behavioral change for the Mamba / MLA branches; only the SWA/NSA hybrid path is touched.

title: Fix /generate endpoint crash when sampling params contain null values
author: cctry
body:
## The bug
Fix `/generate` endpoint crash when sampling params contain null values (e.g., {"top_p": null}).                                                                  
   
Previously, None values passed via sampling_params would override the constructor defaults in SamplingParams.__init__, then crash in verify() with:
```                                                                                 
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'
```



### Reproduce
 
```
curl http://localhost:30000/generate -d '{"text":"Hello","sampling_params":{"top_p":null,"max_new_tokens":1}}'
```

## The fix
The fix handles None gracefully inside SamplingParams.__init__ itself. Each non-optional param falls back to its default when None is passed. The defaults match the existing constructor signature defaults.

title: [Intel GPU] Fix incorrect KV-cache page table for local attention when page_size > 1
author: ckvermaAI
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Fixes incorrect KV-cache page table values passed to `make_local_attention_virtual_batches` in the XPU (Intel GPU) attention backend when `page_size > 1` and local (chunked) attention is enabled. This bug caused incorrect/zeroed outputs from `flash_attn_with_kvcache`.

**Root Cause**

`make_local_attention_virtual_batches` expects a page-granularity block table where each column p stores the physical page index for logical page `p`. However, the raw `req_to_token` table is token-granularity (column `i` = KV slot for token`i`).

When `page_size > 1`, the un-strided token-granularity table was passed directly, causing `block_starts = k_seqstarts_absolute // page_size` to index incorrect physical page values.



## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

When `page_size > 1`, the page table is first converted to page-granularity by:

1. Striding: selecting every `page_size`-th column (`torch.arange(0, ..., page_size)`)
2. Dividing: integer-dividing values by `page_size` to convert KV slot indices to physical page indices
This mirrors the normalization already applied to `metadata.page_table` elsewhere in the backend.

**Changes**
`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: Add page table stride+divide normalization before passing to `make_local_attention_virtual_batches` when page_size > 1

title: [DeepSeek V4] Fix meaningless numbers in chat output by adding swiglu_limit clamp to DeepseekV2MLP
author: GaoYusong
body:
Fixes #23752

## Summary

DeepSeek-V4 chat output contains deterministic spurious tokens (e.g. plain `16`, `14:05`, `<｜end▁of▁file｜>` followed by training-data file paths and decode loops) at sentence-boundary positions. Reported in #23752 with this exemplar prompt:

> *"...Thiopentone is a barbiturate with anticonvulsant properties,**16** used sometimes in status epilepticus.  Propofol also has anticonvulsant effects and is**16** used in refractory status epilepticus..."*

The `16` tokens have IDs `[49, 54]` (ASCII `'1' '6'`) — they are plain text picked by argmax at `temperature=0`.

## Root cause

The routed-expert path already reads `config.swiglu_limit` and propagates it through `FusedMoE` → `MoeRunnerConfig.gemm1_clamp_limit` → triton/deepgemm kernels for SiLU clamping (see `deepseek_v2.py:485` → `layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:299` `_swiglu_silu_clamp_mul`). However, **the shared-expert path and the dense-MLP path use `DeepseekV2MLP` which never receives `swiglu_limit`**. `DeepseekV2MLP.forward` calls bare `SiluAndMul()` on `gate_up`, leaving SiLU output unbounded.

For DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints trained with `swiglu_limit=10.0` (e.g. V4-Pro / V4-Flash with the `2604B` submode, see `configs/config_backup_large.json`), the missing clamp causes shared-expert SiLU output to grow to **±2000+** during inference. This pollutes the residual stream via `final_hidden_states += shared_output`, propagates through `mhc_post`, and degrades `lm_head` logits at sentence-boundary positions, producing the spurious tokens reported in #23752.

A `mhc_post` debug hook on V4-Pro (multiple layers, contributed by @xu-yfei) shows the magnitude:

```
hc_post #0 return: min=-1368 max=2576 mean=0.369627 nan=0 inf=0
hc_post #9 return: min=-2240 max=2224 mean=0.243731 nan=0 inf=0
hc_post #N return: min/max ±1000 to ±2576, mean ~0.1
```

`mhc_post`'s output formula is `post * x + sum(comb * residual, dim=1)` where `post ∈ [0, 2]` (sigmoid-bounded) and `comb` is Sinkhorn-normalized to a doubly-stochastic matrix with elements in `[0, 1]`. Neither of these can blow up the output by themselves, so the ±2000+ values trace back to the `residual` / `x` inputs being poisoned by unclamped shared-expert SiLU output.

The 2604B-specific comment at `deepseek_v4.py:1432-1433` already flagged the issue:
```python
disable_reason = "2604B checkpoint requires different clamping for shared and routed experts"
```
Disabling shared-expert fusion was implemented but the corresponding clamp on the unfused `DeepseekV2MLP` path was missing. This PR closes that gap.

## Fix

Three minimal edits to `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`:

1. **`DeepseekV2MLP.__init__`**: add `swiglu_limit: Optional[float] = None` kwarg, store as `self.swiglu_limit`.

2. **`DeepseekV2MLP.forward`**: clamp `gate_up` chunks before `SiluAndMul` if `self.swiglu_limit` is set. Mirrors `_swiglu_silu_clamp_mul` semantics in the routed-expert kernel:
   ```python
   if self.swiglu_limit is not None:
       _g, _u = gate_up.chunk(2, dim=-1)
       _lim = float(self.swiglu_limit)
       gate_up = torch.cat(
           [_g.clamp(max=_lim), _u.clamp(min=-_lim, max=_lim)], dim=-1
       )
   ```

3. **Both call sites** (`shared_experts` at L530, dense-MLP `self.mlp` at L2589) pass `swiglu_limit=getattr(config, "swiglu_limit", None)` — same pattern already used at L485 for routed experts.

No env vars introduced; behavior is gated entirely on `config.swiglu_limit`. Models that don't set this (e.g. plain V2/V3) retain current behavior (no clamp).

## Verification

- Anaesthesia MCQ from #23752 reproduction: spurious `16` tokens **eliminated** at all 3 positions.
- Multi-prompt smoke test (medical / dialog / long-form explanation / code / math): **0 leaks** across all prompts (without patch, multiple `16` interjections and a `the16 the16 ...` decode loop in the long-form case).
- Tested on `97d1a672` of the `deepseek_v4` branch.

## Backwards compatibility

`swiglu_limit=None` is the existing implicit behavior; adding the kwarg with default `None` is non-breaking. Models without `config.swiglu_limit` see no behavioral change.

title: [Bug Fix] Reject pp_max_micro_batch_size=0 to prevent silent deadlock on generate()
author: ppraneth
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation


`pp_max_micro_batch_size` is an `Optional[int]` CLI argument that defaults to `None`. When `None`, `Scheduler.__init__` auto-computes a safe value via `max(self.max_running_requests // self.pp_size, 1)` — always ≥ 1.

Passing an explicit `0` bypassed the `is None` guard in `scheduler.py`, leaving `pp_max_micro_batch_size = 0` throughout execution. `Scheduler.get_num_allocatable_reqs` then returns `0 - running_bs ≤ 0` on every scheduler tick, so no request ever transitions from waiting → running. The first `engine.generate()` call hangs indefinitely — with no assertion, no exception, no watchdog fire, and no stderr output past the CUDA-graph capture phase.

Found and fixed. Same family as the `prefill_max_requests=0` silent deadlock.

- **`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`** — Added an assertion in `check_server_args`
  that rejects `pp_max_micro_batch_size <= 0` at startup with a clear error message: AssertionError: pp_max_micro_batch_size     must be a positive integer or None (for auto-compute). Got: 0 This fails fast before any model loading or CUDA graph capture occurs.

- **`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`** — Broadened the auto-compute guard from `is None` to `not pp_max_micro_batch_size`, so `0` also falls through to the safe auto-compute path as defense-in-depth (e.g. when `Engine()` is called programmatically, bypassing CLI validation).

title: [BugFix] Fix rid_to_state leak for aborted queued requests
author: guoyuhong
body: Fix a bug where `rid_to_state` entries are not cleaned up when queued requests are aborted, causing `Duplicate request ID detected` errors on resubmission. ## Motivation When aborting all requests (e.g., during weight updates or pause/resume), queued requests that were waiting in the scheduler are aborted and an `AbortReq` is sent back to the `TokenizerManager` via `_handle_abort_req`. However, this handler never called `del self.rid_to_state[rid]`, leaving stale entries behind. The root cause is that **running** and **queued** requests follow completely different abort paths, and the queued path was missing cleanup: **Running request abort** — goes through the normal forward → output pipeline: ```text scheduler: req.to_finish = FINISH_ABORT() → next forward pass finishes normally → stream_output() sends BatchStrOutput → detokenizer forwards to tokenizer_manager → _handle_batch_output() → del self.rid_to_state[rid] ✅ cleaned up ``` **Queued request abort** — never enters forward, scheduler sends `AbortReq` directly: ```text scheduler: waiting_queue.pop(i) → sends AbortReq back to tokenizer_manager → _handle_abort_req() → state.finished = True → state.event.set() → ❌ missing del self.rid_to_state[rid] ``` Because the two abort paths produce different message types (`BatchStrOutput` vs `AbortReq`), they are dispatched to different handlers. `_handle_batch_output` has the cleanup, but `_handle_abort_req` does not. When the same request ID is resubmitted, a `ValueError` raises: `raise ValueError(f"Duplicate request ID detected: {rid}")` This pattern of aborting all requests is especially common in **Reinforcement Learning training workflows**, where weight updates or rollout synchronization frequently trigger global request drains and resubmissions. In such cases, queued rollout requests that haven't started decoding yet are particularly susceptible to this leak, causing the next training step to fail with duplicate RID errors. ## Modifications Add `del self.rid_to_state[recv_obj.rid]` in `_handle_abort_req` before signaling the event, consistent with how `_handle_batch_output` handles finished requests. ## Accuracy Tests - Added a reproduction UT `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`. The tests mock TokenizerManager and can reproduce the "Duplicate request ID detected" errors. - **Without this fix:** Resubmission fails with `ValueError: Duplicate request ID detected: resubmit_after_abort_rid`. - **With this fix, all tests succeed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: Fix mega-MoE crash on idle DP-attention ranks under tvm-ffi DeepGEMM
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary
- On idle DP-attention ranks (num_tokens == 0), `_run_mega_routed` allocates `y = torch.empty((0, H), ...)`, whose CUDA storage is empty so `data_ptr()` is `nullptr`.
- DeepGEMM's tvm-ffi binding (introduced upstream in commit `ffb3d29`, "support tvm ffi interfaces") reconstructs a `torch::Tensor` from the `tvm::ffi::TensorView` via `from_blob(data_ptr, ...)`, which calls `getDeviceFromPtr(data_ptr)` and rejects nullptr with `tvm.error.InternalError: The specified pointer resides on host memory and is not registered with any CUDA device.`
- Mega-MoE is collective on the EP symmetric buffer, so the rank can't skip the call. Fix: allocate `y` with at least 1 row to guarantee a valid CUDA pointer, then truncate back to `num_tokens` before return — caller-visible behavior is unchanged.

## Repro
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 NVSHMEM_DISABLE_IB=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1 SGLANG_OPT_FIX_HASH_MEGA_MOE=1 \
  SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \
  SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \
  sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 --max-running-requests 256 \
    --deepep-config '{"normal_dispatch":{"num_sms":96},"normal_combine":{"num_sms":96}}' \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```
Sending any request crashes the scheduler with the `tvm.error.InternalError` above (origin frame: `deep_gemm::convert_to_torch_tensor` → `from_blob` → `getDeviceFromPtr`).

## Test plan
- [x] B200, DeepGEMM `2e21741`: server boots and `sgldev acc send-one` returns a valid 512-token response (108 tok/s) with no scheduler exception.

title: Re-land #23109: rebase-required mode + fix for grep-no-match abort
author: alisonshao
body:
Re-lands #23109 (which was reverted in #24179) with a fix for the bug that caused the original revert.

## Why #23109 was reverted

The `check-maintenance` action's `MIN_BASE_SHA` parser piped through `grep`, which exits 1 when no line matches. With `shell: bash` composite steps defaulting to `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`, the 1 propagates via pipefail and aborts the whole script before any further check runs. Result: when the issue body had no `MIN_BASE_SHA` directive (the normal case), every job's `check-maintenance` step exited 1 in 0 seconds, falsely blocking all PR CI.

Reproduces locally:

```bash
bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail -c '
  A=$(echo "" | grep "x" | head -n1)
  echo after
'
# -> exits 1, never prints "after"
```

## Fix

Wrap `grep` in a brace group with `|| true` so an empty match falls through to `head`/`sed`/`awk` cleanly. Verified locally with both empty-body and directive-present inputs.

```diff
-        MIN_BASE_SHA=$(printf '%s' "$ISSUE_BODY" | tr -d '\r' | grep -iE '...' | head -n1 | sed -E '...' | awk '{print $1}')
+        MIN_BASE_SHA=$(
+          { printf '%s' "$ISSUE_BODY" | tr -d '\r' | grep -iE '...' || true; } \
+            | head -n1 | sed -E '...' | awk '{print $1}'
+        )
```

## Original feature (from #23109)

Adds a rebase-required mode to `check-maintenance`. Issue #21065's body can include a `MIN_BASE_SHA: <sha>` directive — when present, CI runs only for PRs whose branch already contains `<sha>` (verified via GitHub compare API, status `ahead`/`identical` passes, `behind`/`diverged` blocks). The directive is enforced regardless of whether the issue is open or closed; the existing full-pause maintenance gate (issue OPEN, no SHA) still works as before. The `bypass-maintenance` label still bypasses both gates. API errors fail-open.

## Behavior matrix

| Issue #21065 | `MIN_BASE_SHA` in body | PR contains SHA | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Closed | absent | — | CI runs (the case that was broken before this fix) |
| Closed | present | yes | CI runs |
| Closed | present | no | Blocked: Rebase Required |
| Open | absent | — | Full pause |
| Open | present | yes | Full pause (rebase OK, but issue still pauses) |
| Open | present | no | Blocked: Rebase Required |

## Test plan

- [x] Bash repro of the no-match bug confirmed locally
- [x] Fix verified locally for both empty-body and directive-present inputs
- [ ] Verify on this PR's own CI (issue #21065 body has no `MIN_BASE_SHA` currently, so the empty-body code path is the one we're exercising — it should pass `check-maintenance` cleanly)
- [ ] Verify rebase-required mode end-to-end on this PR's own CI (set `MIN_BASE_SHA: <sha-PR-contains>` for pass, then `<sha-PR-doesn't-contain>` for block) — same procedure used to verify #23109 before merge

title: fix: STANDALONE spec-decode hidden-size mismatch crash
author: brian030128
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Fixes #24215. Reporter saw STANDALONE spec-decode crash on Llama-3.1-8B (target, hidden=4096) + Llama-3.2-1B (draft, hidden=2048) at `EagleDraftInput.merge_batch.torch.cat`:

```
RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0.
Expected size 4096 but got size 2048
```

## Diagnosis

`spec_info.hidden_states` has two canonical shapes, switched at phase boundaries:

| Phase | Producer | Wire shape |
|-------|----------|------------|
| decode | draft model output, re-written by `capture_for_decode` and the draft loop (`eagle_worker.py:875`, `:1234`) | **draft** |
| extend | target verify output (`eagle_worker.py:959`), carried by `EagleDraftExtendInput` from `eagle_info.py:547`/`:617` | **target** |

`capture_for_decode` at the end of `forward_draft_extend` (`eagle_worker.py:1115`) normalizes the batch back to draft shape before it leaves the worker, so the scheduler always sees draft shape.

The reporter's 0.5.9 crash is no longer reachable on current main — the `capture_for_decode` normalization (added 2025-03-05) already handles the cross-phase shape switch.

## Changes

Two extend-phase wiring sites aligned to target (the producer for extend):

1. **`eagle_worker.py:1117`** — `forward_draft_extend_after_decode`'s idle fallback sizes the `EagleDraftExtendInput` placeholder from `target_worker.model_runner.model_config`.
2. **`eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py:154-163`** — the extend cuda graph buffer is sized from the target config.

Both are hygiene fixes: pre-PR the extend wiring used draft shape, which was latent because (a) the idle fallback path requires `enable_dp_attention=True` to be reachable (`eagle_worker.py:499-504`), and (b) the extend cuda graph runner has a shape-guard at `:486-492` that silently skips `copy_` on mismatch.

Decode-phase wiring is left at draft shape (the pre-PR state). Flipping it to target — as the initial hypothesis suggested — would actively produce the exact `Expected 4096 got 2048` crash by giving the scheduler a target-shaped idle batch to cat against a draft-shaped running batch.

Per #21058 task 1 (PR #21434), STANDALONE should not carry `hidden_states` at all on the spec v1 path. Once that lands, both sites become dead code.

## Motivation
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19746 introduces radix tree on pd-decode side;

title: [docker] Fix silently-masked cubin download failure; skip prebuilt cubins on aarch64
author: mispa-ms
body:
## Motivation

Fix two compounded issues in `framework_final` of `docker/Dockerfile` that have been silently breaking aarch64 nightly Docker builds since #22160 (2026-04-09):

1. **Silent-failure bug.** The cubin-download retry block ends with `... || true` (intended only to guard the trailing `find` cleanup), but bash's left-associative `&&`/`||` precedence makes that swallow the entire chain — including the `[ "$success" = "1" ]` fail-fast check that #22322 added the same day. When `kernels download python` fails permanently, the RUN reports `DONE 0`, the subsequent `mkdir -p /root/.cache/sglang && mv python/kernels.lock` steps are skipped, and the runtime stage's `COPY --from=framework_final /root/.cache/sglang /root/.cache/sglang` then fails with a misleading `"not found"` two stages later.

2. **No aarch64 cubin variants.** `kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3` (pinned via `[tool.kernels.dependencies]` in `python/pyproject.toml`) only publishes `x86_64-linux` build variants. On aarch64 hosts (e.g., Grace Blackwell builds), all 3 retries always fail; the silent-failure bug above hides this inside a `DONE 0` layer.

This affects every aarch64 build of this Dockerfile — observed in NVIDIA-internal nightly pipelines for several weeks. x86_64 builds are unaffected (they find a matching prebuilt cubin variant).

## Modifications

In `docker/Dockerfile`, the `framework_final` editable-install RUN block:

- **Scope `|| true` to the cleanup find only.** Wrap the trailing `find ... -exec rm -rf {} +` in a subshell so the `|| true` no longer swallows earlier failures in the `&&` chain. This is the actual silent-failure fix; it makes future regressions in the retry/install chain fail loudly at the right step, not three stages later in `COPY`.
- **Skip the cubin download on aarch64** with an explicit log message naming `kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3`. JIT compilation handles the kernels at runtime (which the silent-failure path was implicitly already doing). A short reference comment marks the branch for removal once arm cubins are published upstream.
- **Defensive `mkdir -p /root/.cache/huggingface /root/.cache/sglang`.** `/root/.cache/huggingface` was previously created as a side effect of `kernels download python` (HF Hub cache). With that call skipped on aarch64, the adjacent `COPY --from=framework_final /root/.cache/huggingface ...` in the runtime stage would fail the same way `/root/.cache/sglang` did. Eliminating this class of silent-skip-then-COPY-fails bug in one place.
- **Replace `[ -f kernels.lock ] && mv ... || true` with `if [ -f ... ]; then mv ...; fi`.** Loud-fails on real `mv` errors (filesystem, permissions) rather than masking them — consistent with the silent-failure lesson of this very fix.

`python/pyproject.toml` is intentionally untouched: removing `kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3` from `[tool.kernels.dependencies]` would also break x86, which can use the prebuilt cubins. Selective skip in the Dockerfile is the right scope.

Diff size: `1 file changed, 18 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — Dockerfile-only build fix. No model output, no kernel/forward changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — Dockerfile-only build fix. The functional behavior on aarch64 is unchanged from the prior silent-failure path: cubins were not actually being installed (the retry was failing every time), so kernels were already being JIT-compiled at runtime. This PR just makes that explicit and removes the misleading `COPY: not found` failure mode.

## Verification

### Before (representative aarch64 nightly run, sglang `bcb34da9f`)
```
#71 [framework_final 4/8] RUN ... kernels download python && success=1 && break ...
#71 21.45 Cannot find a build variant for this system in
          kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3 (revision: b73eb6a16dea3a785f3c491f4d174d339684c4a3).
          Available variants: torch211-cxx11-cu130-x86_64-linux,
                              torch210-cxx11-cu128-x86_64-linux,
                              torch29-cxx11-cu129-x86_64-linux,
                              torch29-cxx11-cu128-x86_64-linux,
                              torch211-cxx11-cu128-x86_64-linux,
                              torch210-cxx11-cu130-x86_64-linux,
                              torch29-cxx11-cu130-x86_64-linux
... (3 attempts, all fail with same message) ...
#71 DONE 115.4s         <-- RUN reports success despite all failures
...
#81 [runtime 10/16] COPY --from=framework_final /root/.cache/sglang /root/.cache/sglang
#81 ERROR: failed to calculate checksum ... "/root/.cache/sglang": not found
ERROR: failed to build: ...
```

### After (expected)
On aarch64:
```
#71 [framework_final 4/8] RUN ...
Skipping kernels-community/sgl-flash-attn3 cubin download on aarch64
(no variants published upstream); kernels will be JIT-compiled at runtime
#71 DONE ~5s
...
[runtime 10/16] COPY --from=framework_final /root/.cache/sglang /root/.cache/sglang
... build completes
```

On x86_64: behavior unchanged — retry loop runs as before, fail-fast on permanent download error preserved.

I will attach links to a green NVIDIA-internal aarch64 nightly Docker build run once the patched build cycle completes.

author: yhyang201
body:
Fix `--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel` crash on `dsv4-rebase`.

`dsv4-rebase` introduced `_ATTN_CP` process group via `attn_cp_size`, but CP operations still used `get_attention_tp_*` (pointing to `_ATTN_TP` which shrinks to size 1 when CP is active). This caused shape mismatches in metadata, compressor allgather, and indexer.

author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

Improve LTX-2 / LTX-2.3 diffusion accuracy against official-generated outputs, especially for multi-GPU CI cases and the LTX-2.3 HQ two-stage path.

The previous LTX-2.3 multi-GPU CI settings had weak consistency thresholds for some cases and could use parallelism modes that were either slower or less aligned with the official output. The HQ path also regressed on the PR #23366 SpongeBob repro.

Transformer fp8-cast is intentionally **not** included in this PR. It did not materially help this PR's target CI paths, and any future precision branch can keep or reintroduce it as a separate opt-in change.

## Modifications

- Tighten LTX consistency coverage:

  - tighten thresholds for `ltx_2.3_one_stage_ti2v`, `ltx_2.3_two_stage_t2v_2gpus`, and `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus`.

title: Fix NCCL deadlock in Ulysses SP when sequence length has remainder
author: storyicon
body:
## Motivation
The issue is a deadlock that occurs in Ulysses sequence-parallel (SP) mode when the audio/video sequence length is not evenly divisible by `sp_world_size`.

`_build_ltx2_sp_padding_mask` returns `None` when a rank has no padding tokens (`valid >= seq_len`), but returns a mask `Tensor` for ranks that do have padding. Since `USPAttention.forward` branches on `attn_mask is not None`, different ranks execute different sets of NCCL collective operations:

- **No-padding ranks** (mask=None): skip `all_gather(mask)`, go directly to local attention then `all-to-all output`
- **Padding rank** (mask=Tensor): call `all_gather(mask)` first, then attend, then `all-to-all output`

The padding rank blocks on `all_gather(mask)` waiting for the other ranks to join, while those ranks never call it. This causes a deadlock.

## Modifications
Remove the `valid >= seq_len → None` early return in `_build_ltx2_sp_padding_mask`. When there is no padding, return an all-ones mask Tensor instead of `None`, so all ranks take the same masked-attention path through `USPAttention`.

The all-ones mask is semantically equivalent to `None` (no tokens are masked out), so this change has no effect on model output. It only ensures NCCL collective operations are consistent across ranks.

## Accuracy Tests
No accuracy impact. The all-ones mask is semantically equivalent to `None`, no tokens are masked out.

title: fix(cuda_graph): zero out_cache_loc_swa on pad and use int32 (hybrid-SWA accuracy fix)
author: JoyFuture
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

  PR #23552 added a pre-computed `out_cache_loc_swa` buffer in `DecodeInputBuffers` so the captured decode graph can hit
  `set_kv_buffer`'s fast path on hybrid-SWA models (Gemma, MiMoV2, DeepSeek V4, …). On the main `CudaGraphRunner`, the main correctness issue is that `out_cache_loc_swa` is not cleared on padding, which can silently corrupt the SWA KV cache when decode cuda graphs are enabled. While touching this path, this patch also fixes a related dtype mismatch.                                                                                                                                                                 

  The user-visible symptom we hit is a measurable accuracy regression on **MiMoV2.5 Pro** (which is registered as hybrid SWA via `MIMO_V2_MODEL_ARCHS` in `model_config.py`). With the same checkpoint and identical eval workload:                                                                                                                                                                              

  | Benchmark      | Before | After   | Δ      |                                                                                                                                                            
  | -------------- | ------ | ------- | ------ |                                                                                                                                                            
  | aime24_25      | 80.3   | 90.3    | +10.0  |                                                                                                                                                            
  | cmmlu          | 87.6   | 90.1    | +2.5   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | minerva_math   | 89.4   | 93.6    | +4.2   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | mmlu-pro       | 82.6   | 85.1    | +2.5   |                                                                                                                                                            
  | mmlu_redux     | 93.1   | 94.97   | +1.87  |                                                                                                                                                            
  | supergpqa      | 59.1   | 62.4    | +3.3   |                                                                                                                                                            

  The regression is reproducible only when decode cuda graphs are enabled **and** the served batch size is small enough to be padded to a `capture_bs` bucket — which is exactly the common decode steady-state. 

## Root cause                                                                                                                                                                                             

  ### 1. Stale padding indices corrupt the SWA KV cache                                                                                                                                                     

  In `populate_from_forward_batch` (the main `CudaGraphRunner`), when `bs != raw_bs` only `out_cache_loc` is zeroed before the per-tensor copy. `out_cache_loc_swa` is not — and the subsequent copy only writes the first `raw_num_token` entries:                                                                                                                                                                        

  ```python                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  if bs != raw_bs:                                          
      self.seq_lens.fill_(seq_len_fill_value)                                                                                                                                                               
      self.out_cache_loc.zero_()                                                                                                                                                                            
      # out_cache_loc_swa is NOT zeroed                                                                                                                                                                     
      ...                                                                                                                                                                                                   

  if (                                                                                                                                                                                                      
      self.out_cache_loc_swa is not None                                                                                                                                                                    
      and forward_batch.out_cache_loc_swa is not None       
  ):                                                                                                                                                                                                        
      dsts.append(self.out_cache_loc_swa[:raw_num_token])
      srcs.append(forward_batch.out_cache_loc_swa[:raw_num_token])                                                                                                                                          
  ```

  The captured graph, however, runs set_kv_buffer over the full buffers.out_cache_loc_swa[:num_tokens] slice. The padded region [raw_num_token : num_tokens] keeps real SWA indices from the previous replay, so padded tokens write their junk KV into live SWA slots belonging to previously active requests. The pre-#23552 fallback path  (translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(out_cache_loc) per layer) didn't have this problem because out_cache_loc is zeroed on pad, so padded positions translate to the SWA sentinel.                                                                                                                                                                  

  The piecewise runner already does the right thing — it zeroes the buffer on pad in piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py:654-655. The fix brings the main runner in line with that.                                                                                                                                                                 

  ### 2. Dtype mismatch with translate_loc_from_full_to_swa                                                                                                                                                     

  out_cache_loc_swa was allocated as torch.int64, but both SWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa (swa_memory_pool.py:170) and the DSV4 equivalent (deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:482) return torch.int32. The populate_from_forward_batch copy then implicitly  widens int32 → int64 and the captured graph hands an int64 index tensor to SWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer. This was flagged in the #23552 review and deferred; it's cheap to fix here alongside the correctness issue.

title: [Mamba] Fix extra_buffer overlap schedule races
author: hanming-lu
body:
## Summary
Goal: move all mamba state operations to forward stream to avoid scheduler <-> forward stream data manipulation races
1. Fix `cache_unfinished_req`'s copy mamba state races with forward stream:  cache unfinished donate the index to the radix cache instead of copying, then alloc a new one for next iteration
2. prefix match copy-on-write (cow) and mamba state clear both happen during init metadata instead of scheduler stream.

## Testing
- CI coverage is sufficient
- Verified race-free fix with 0kl RL testing, context: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24221#issuecomment-4424945325

































<!-- pr-states:start -->

title: Fix DenoisingStage to respect dit_precision config instead of hardcoded bfloat16
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

In `DenoisingStage`, `target_dtype` was hardcoded to `torch.bfloat16`, ignoring the user-configured `pipeline_config.dit_precision` setting. This is inconsistent with other stages (e.g., `helios_denoising`, `mova`) that correctly use `PRECISION_TO_TYPE[server_args.pipeline_config.dit_precision]` to determine the target dtype.

This bug means that even if a user explicitly sets `dit_precision` to `fp16` or `fp32`, the denoising stage would still forcefully cast tensors to `bfloat16`, causing precision loss and potentially degrading generation quality — especially for models that are trained or fine-tuned in `fp16` or `fp32`.

## Modifications

- Changed `target_dtype` in `DenoisingStage` from hardcoded `torch.bfloat16` to `PRECISION_TO_TYPE[server_args.pipeline_config.dit_precision]`, making it consistent with other stages (e.g., `helios_denoising`, `mova`).

## Accuracy Tests

- **Fix**: Previously, when `dit_precision` was set to `fp16` or `fp32`, the denoising stage would still run in `bfloat16`, introducing unintended precision loss (e.g., `fp32` → `bfloat16` truncation). After this fix, the stage correctly respects the configured precision, preserving numerical accuracy for models that require higher or different precision.
- When `dit_precision` is set to `bfloat16` (the common default), behavior is identical to before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- No performance impact. This is a one-line config lookup replacing a hardcoded constant.

title: [perf] fix kimi tokenizer to improve ttft
author: Qiaolin-Yu
body: ## Problem https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5/blob/main/tokenization_kimi.py warning in server log `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts` calls the tokenizer via `__call__`, which forces tiktoken-derived tokenizers (Kimi-K2.5) through `PreTrainedTokenizer`'s slow Python pipeline. Its native tiktoken fast path is only reachable via `.encode()` with no kwargs. Microbench on Kimi-K2.5, 80k tokens, single text: | Call | Time | |---|---:| | `tok.encode(text)` (tiktoken native) | **47 ms** | | `tok([text])` (`__call__`, what SGLang did) | 308 ms | That's a fixed **~260 ms / request** overhead for any tiktoken-derived tokenizer on long inputs. | Tokenizer | bs=1 | bs≥2 | |---|---|---| | Slow (Kimi / tiktoken-derived) | `.encode()` ← fix | `.encode()` loop ← fix | | Fast (Llama / Qwen / BERT) | `.encode()` (equivalent) | `tokenizer(...)` (keep `tokenizers`-crate rayon batch) | | Cross-encoder (BGE-reranker, …) | `tokenizer(...)` | `tokenizer(...)` (needs `token_type_ids`) | Microbench (`.encode()` loop / `tokenizer(...)` batch ratio — >1 means loop wins, <1 means batch wins): | Tokenizer | bs=1 | bs=2 | bs=16 | bs=100 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Kimi-K2.5 | 6.6× | 7.6× | 6.7× | 7.1× | | Llama-3.1-8B | 1.0× | 0.43× | 0.14× | 0.08× | | Qwen2.5-7B | 1.0× | 0.38× | 0.13× | ~0.08× | For Kimi `.encode()` always wins; for fast tokenizers rayon batch wins from bs≥2. The branch condition lands exactly on this boundary. ## E2E `bench_serving --random-input-len 80000 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1` on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 (B200×4, TP=4, EAGLE3): | | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | |---|---:|---:| | Baseline | 2948 ms | 3151 ms | | Patched | **2791 ms** | **2932 ms** | **~157 ms** / request saving (~5–7%).

title: [Disagg] Fix MegaMoE topk_ids dtype mismatch and FakeKVManager missing kv_args
author: JoeLee314
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

When serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MegaMoE enabled (`SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1`) and disaggregation decode mode (`--disaggregation-transfer-backend fake --ep-dispatch-algorithm fake`), the server crashes during initialization with two independent errors:

**Bug 1 — dtype mismatch in `mega_moe_pre_dispatch`:**
```
tvm.error.InternalError: Tensor match failed for Tensor<32, 6>[strides=<6, 1>, dtype=int64, device=cuda:0]
  at mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh:150
- Root cause: Dtype value [int64] not in the allowed options: [int32]
```
The `topk_output.topk_ids` is `int64` with `-ep-dispatch-algorithm fake`, but the JIT-compiled `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` kernel only accepts `int32`.
Here is the analys:

1. When `--ep-dispatch-algorithm` is not set, `ExpertLocationDispatchInfo.init_new()` returns None (`expert_location_dispatch.py:50`), so `topk_ids_logical_to_physical()` returns `topk_ids` as-is — `int32` is preserved.
3. When `--ep-dispatch-algorithm fake` is set, it routes to `_topk_ids_logical_to_physical_dynamic()` (`expert_location_dispatch.py:93`), which does:                             
  `topk_ids = info.partial_logical_to_all_physical_map[topk_ids, chosen_dispatch_index]`
4. `partial_logical_to_all_physical_map` is created via `torch.tensor()` without an explicit dtype, defaulting to `int64` (`expert_location_dispatch.py:422`). In PyTorch, tensor indexing result dtype follows the source tensor, not the index tensor — so `int64_tensor[int32_idx]` returns `int64`, silently undoing the earlier `.to(torch.int32)` cast.
6. The `int64` `topk_ids` then flows into `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` which only accepts `int32`, triggering the TVM dtype check error.


**Bug 2 — `FakeKVManager` missing `kv_args` attribute:**
```
AttributeError: 'FakeKVManager' object has no attribute 'kv_args'
```
`FakeKVManager` inherits from `BaseKVManager` but does not store the `args` parameter as `self.kv_args`, unlike `CommonKVManager`. The disaggregation decode event loop accesses `self.kv_manager.kv_args.state_types`, which crashes at runtime.

Both bugs are hit when running:
```bash
SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_FIX_HASH_MEGA_MOE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_FIX_NEXTN_MEGA_MOE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320 \
SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 \
sglang serve \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
    --disaggregation-mode decode \
    --ep-dispatch-algorithm fake \
    --disaggregation-transfer-backend fake \
    --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:30435 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001
```

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py`** — `_run_mega_routed`:
- Cast `topk_ids` to `int32` before passing to `mega_moe_pre_dispatch`, since the kernel only accepts `int32` tensors. The `else` branch already creates an `int32` empty tensor, so this makes the two branches consistent.
The alternative would be fixing _topk_ids_logical_to_physical_dynamic() or the map dtype in expert_location_dispatch.py. However, casting at the MegaMoE entry point (mega_moe.py) is a more robust choice because:
  - It makes MegaMoE self-contained — the kernel's contract (int32 input) is enforced at its own boundary regardless of upstream dtype changes.  
  - Multiple topk paths (grouped, biased, fused, custom) converge here; fixing any single upstream path would miss others.
  - It avoids risking regressions in non-MegaMoE paths where int64 topk_ids may be used by other kernels without issue.

**`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/fake/conn.py`** — `FakeKVManager.__init__`:
- Add `self.kv_args = args`, matching the pattern already used in `CommonKVManager`. This is needed because the decode event loop accesses `self.kv_manager.kv_args.state_types` during preallocation.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — the first fix is a dtype cast that preserves values (int64→int32 is safe since expert indices are small), and the second fix stores a reference that was already being accessed at runtime.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — both fixes are one-line changes with no impact on the forward compute path. The `.to(torch.int32)` cast is a no-op when the tensor is already on GPU and the values fit in int32.

Verified that the server starts successfully and prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` with the above command on 8× NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Bug] Fix V4-Pro NaN on Blackwell by converting fp8_einsum input scale to ue8m0
author: yhyang201
body:
## Summary

- Fix DeepSeek-V4-Pro producing garbage text during autoregressive decode on Blackwell GPUs (B300/B200)
- Root cause: `deep_gemm`'s `transpose_and_pack_fp32_into_ue8m0` CUDA kernel has a packing bug — it doesn't mask mantissa bits when extracting fp32 exponent, so non-power-of-2 scale values get corrupted. This causes `fp8_einsum` to produce NaN at batch=1 (single-token decode)
- Fix: add `ceil_to_ue8m0()` on the activation scale before passing to `fp8_einsum`, ensuring mantissa bits are zero before packing
- The scale tensor is tiny (e.g. shape `(2, 32)`), so the overhead is negligible
- Detailed analysis: https://gist.github.com/yhyang201/2fce5750e44970af419f9669e10e994c

title: [Bug][Mamba] Fix LRU list reference cycle leak in mamba_radix_cache
author: zjd0112
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Fix memory leak in `LRUList._remove_node` that causes scheduler RSS to grow linearly under sustained load on hybrid Mamba models (e.g., Qwen3-Next).

In our test (Qwen3-Next on RTX 5090 TP=2), RSS grows at ~3.7 GB/h.

Related: #21535

### Root cause

`LRUList._remove_node` updates the neighbors to skip the removed node but does not clear the removed node's own `prev` / `next` pointers:

```python
def _remove_node(self, node):
    setattr(getattr(node, self.prv), self.nxt, getattr(node, self.nxt))
    setattr(getattr(node, self.nxt), self.prv, getattr(node, self.prv))
    # ⚠️ node.prev / node.next still dangling
```
When multiple nodes are evicted in the same batch (common case in evict_full / evict_mamba / _iteratively_delete_tombstone_leaf), the dangling LRU pointers between evicted nodes form 2-element reference cycles that Python's reference counting cannot reclaim. They wait for gen-2 GC, which is too infrequent under sustained load.

### Diagnostic evidence

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| malloc_trim() | Releases only 0.3%, not glibc fragmentation |
| flush_cache | Releases only 0.1%, not cache occupancy |
| gc.collect() | Releases 1.9 GB instantly, reference cycles confirmed |
| gc.set_debug(DEBUG_SAVEALL) | 17270 TreeNode + 17270 RadixKey + 17270 list + 17194 defaultdict in cycles |
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
Clear the removed node's own prev / next pointers in LRUList._remove_node so reference counting can reclaim it immediately, without waiting for gen-2 GC.

```python
 def _remove_node(self, node):
     """Helper to remove node from linked list"""
     setattr(getattr(node, self.prv), self.nxt, getattr(node, self.nxt))
     setattr(getattr(node, self.nxt), self.prv, getattr(node, self.prv))
+    # Clear self pointers to break reference cycles among evicted nodes.
+    setattr(node, self.prv, None)
+    setattr(node, self.nxt, None)
```

title: [diffusion][bugfix] Fix Wan channels_last_3d VAE decode corruption
author: IPostYellow
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Fix visual corruption in Wan VAE decoding when Conv3d weights are stored in `channels_last_3d` memory format.

This PR makes Wan causal Conv3d inputs match the memory format of the Conv3d weights before running the convolution, and restores the output back to contiguous format afterward to keep the downstream tensor layout unchanged.

When serving Wan2.2 I2V with 8 GPUs and offload disabled, the generated video could become visually corrupted / garbled on current main.

Reproduction command:

```bash
sglang serve \
    --model-path /home/admin/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers \
    --dit-cpu-offload false \
    --dit-layerwise-offload false \
    --text-encoder-cpu-offload false \
    --image-encoder-cpu-offload false \
    --vae-cpu-offload false \
    --pin-cpu-memory false \
    --num-gpus 8 \
    --port 3000
```
```
import requests
import time

title: Fix stale forward_metadata leak in DP attn unpadded idle batch
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26157 added a debug canary on the SWA `full→swa` mapping_stack and exposed a pre-existing race in DSv4 disaggregation with DP-attention. The canary fires `mapping_stack[full_slot] == (producer=0, canary=SENTINEL)` — i.e. a full-slot is being gathered after `free_swa` has already written the sentinel into the mapping.

After narrowing the trigger surface (EAGLE off, PD off, write_through_selective off, one at a time), the race reproduces **iff DP-attention is enabled**. None of EAGLE / PD-disagg / write_through_selective is necessary or sufficient.

## Root cause

DP-attention requires every rank to enter `forward` for the MLP all-gather, so a rank with no local work executes `ModelRunner.forward_idle`. In the **unpadded** case (`batch_size == 0`, MLP-sync doesn't pad this rank), `forward_idle` skipped `init_forward_metadata` entirely. That leaves `attn_backend.forward_metadata` holding the **previous forward's stale `DSV4RawDecodeMetadata`** — e.g. warmup-A's last decode at `req_pool_indices=[1]`, `seq_lens=[13]`, `out_cache_loc=[268]`.

`DeepseekV4Model.forward` then runs this **unconditional** pre-layer call (`deepseek_v4.py:1270`):

```python
# Upgrade lazy raw metadata on the main stream once before any layer
# forks alt-streams; later per-layer calls become no-ops.
get_attn_backend()._maybe_upgrade_forward_metadata()
```

The call lives outside any per-layer module, so the existing `self_attn.forward` `x.shape[0] == 0` early-return does **not** protect it. With stale `DSV4RawDecodeMetadata` still attached, the upgrade proceeds and `make_forward_metadata_from_raw_decode(rpi=[1], seq_lens=[13])`:

1. Re-reads `req_to_token[1, :13]` — still holds full-slots `[256..268]` (`req_to_token` is not cleared on `free`).
2. Calls `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(...)` on those slots.
3. Warmup-A's `free_swa` has already written `(producer=0, canary=SENTINEL)` into `mapping_stack[256..268]`.
4. Canary fires; in production this is a silent cross-rank use-after-free once the freed slots are reallocated to another request.

This is the chain that drives the gsm8k regression observed in disagg + DP-attention runs.

## Modifications

Drop the stale `forward_metadata` in the unpadded IDLE branch of `ModelRunner.forward_idle`:

```python
if forward_batch.batch_size > 0:
    self.attn_backend.init_forward_metadata(forward_batch)
else:
    self.attn_backend.forward_metadata = None
```

`_maybe_upgrade_forward_metadata` already no-ops on `None` (both `isinstance(None, DSV4RawDecodeMetadata / DSV4Metadata)` branches fail), so no backend-side guard is needed. The padded IDLE path (`batch_size > 0`, e.g. DSA Indexer that needs a real batch_size view) is unchanged.

For non-DSv4 backends this is also safe: `AttentionBackend.forward` early-returns on `forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle()` before touching `forward_metadata` (`base_attn_backend.py:101`), so a `None` value is never dereferenced.

## Accuracy

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, disagg + DP-attention + EAGLE, 8×H200, gsm8k via `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py`:

main (with the #26157 canary instrumented):
```
Accuracy: 0.010
Latency: 142.31 s
```

this PR (same canary instrumented, never fires):
```
Accuracy: 0.975
Latency:  14.12 s
```

5/5 reproduction iterations: canary fires on main, zero fires on this branch.

title: [PD] Fix cross-rank queue divergence by gating metadata readiness before all-reduce
author: ShangmingCai
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

  When `poll_and_all_reduce` returns `KVPoll.Success`, it only confirms KV cache transfer completion. The data written via a separate RDMA op may not have landed on all ranks yet. If one rank sees metadata ready and removes the request from its queue while another rank keeps it, the queues diverge across TP ranks. Subsequent all-reduce calls operate on misaligned tensors, causing hangs or silent corruption.

## Modifications
  - Add `_apply_metadata_gate()` helper that downgrades `Success → Transferring` for requests whose `bootstrap_room` field is still zero (the "not yet written" sentinel) on the decode side, no need to allreduce the metadata checksum
  - Call it inside `poll_and_all_reduce` and `poll_and_all_reduce_with_staging` (opt-in via new optional params) before the single all-reduce

title: [Bug Fix] Fix activation.cuh JIT compilation failure on CUDA 13 due to template type/value mismatch
author: 256256mjw
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

  Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25487

  On CUDA 13.0, the JIT compilation of `activation.cuh` fails during CUDA graph capture, crashing the server process. The root cause is a C++ template type/value mismatch in the `select_kernel` trailing return type:

  activation.cuh:95:52: error: type/value mismatch at argument 1 in template parameter list
    note: expected a type, got 'ActivationKind::kSiLU'

  CUDA 13's stricter `nvcc` cannot correctly parse `decltype(ActivationKernel::template activation_kernel<ActivationKind::kSiLU, kFilterExpert>)` in a dependent context (trailing return type with an outer template parameter `kFilterExpert`). It
   misinterprets the non-type enum value `ActivationKind::kSiLU` as a type argument. Older CUDA versions (11/12) silently accepted this.

  ## Modifications

  - Introduced an explicit `kernel_fn_t` type alias via `decltype(&act_and_mul_kernel<...>)` on the global function template (avoids the problematic variable template parsing path).
  - Replaced `auto` with `kernel_fn_t` for the `activation_kernel` variable template.
  - Removed the `decltype`-based trailing return type from `select_kernel`, using `kernel_fn_t` directly.
  - Removed unnecessary `ActivationKernel::template` qualification inside the class body.
  - Added `static_cast<uint32_t>()` for `hidden_size` to fix a signed-to-unsigned narrowing conversion warning.

  All changes are compile-time only — no runtime behavior or performance change. Compatible with CUDA 11, 12, 13, and ROCm/HIP.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  N/A — This is a compile-time fix only. No changes to kernel logic, numerical computation, or model output.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

  N/A — No runtime behavior change. The generated PTX/SASS is identical since the function pointer type and kernel code are unchanged.
