title: Fix _GenerationStreamAccumulator logprob_end off-by-one under retract
author: shenxiul
body:
## Summary

Fix an output-logprob cursor off-by-one when overlap scheduling retracts an in-flight request before its prefill result is processed.

The fix is deliberately retraction-specific. Non-retracted prefill-only requests with `max_new_tokens=0` retain the existing behavior of returning their first logprob.

## Root cause

Under overlap scheduling and retraction:

1. A prefill forward pass is launched.
2. The request is retracted while that pass is in flight, setting `req.is_retracted = True`.
3. `process_batch_result_prefill` skips appending the sampled token for that request, but still passes the full batch to the output streamer.
4. For a non-streaming request with no output IDs, the forced-stream condition is true because `0 % DEFAULT_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL == 0`.
5. `max(len(output_ids_), 1)` advances `send_output_token_logprobs_offset` to 1 while `send_token_offset` remains 0.

Every later output is therefore shifted by one logprob, and the final response has one fewer output logprob than output token.

## Fix

```python
logprob_end = (
    len(output_ids_) if req.is_retracted else max(len(output_ids_), 1)
)
```

For a retracted request with no output IDs, both cursors stay at zero. For a legitimate non-retracted prefill-only request, the existing first-logprob behavior remains intact.

## Tests

- Added CPU unit coverage that verifies a retracted empty-output request does not advance its logprob cursor.
- Added CPU unit coverage that verifies a non-retracted `max_new_tokens=0` request still returns its first logprob.
- Kept the end-to-end forced-retraction regression and registered it in CUDA `base-b` and AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` CI.
- Ran all pre-commit hooks on the changed files successfully.
- Ran Python syntax compilation successfully.
- The focused runtime unit test was not run locally because this bare checkout lacks SGLang runtime dependencies; it is registered with CPU CI.

The original end-to-end reproduction produced 2/32 mismatched responses in five consecutive pre-fix trials and 0/32 in eight consecutive post-fix trials.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add regression coverage.
- [x] Preserve prefill-only logprob behavior raised in review.
- [x] Rebase onto current upstream `main`.

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'max_n_routed_experts'. Did you mean: 'n_routed_experts'?
```

## Modification

Add `max_n_routed_experts=2` to the test's fake config so it mirrors the real `NemotronHConfig`, where the property equals `n_routed_experts`. Production code is unchanged — the bug was purely in the test fixture.

title: Fix TokenizerManager crash on top_logprobs with tensor values
author: kflansburg
body:
## Motivation

`detokenize_top_logprobs_tokens` checked `if token_logprobs_val[i]:` to skip
empty positions. When `token_logprobs_val[i]` is a multi-element `torch.Tensor`
(instead of the annotated `List[float]`), Python evaluates the truthiness of the
tensor and raises:

```
RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous.
```

This propagates out of the detokenization handler and is caught by
`print_exception_wrapper`, which calls
`kill_process_tree(os.getpid(), include_parent=True)` and SIGKILLs the whole
prefill process (exit code -9). In disaggregated PD deployments this manifests
as a prefill restart storm whenever clients send requests with
`top_logprobs > 0`.

## Modifications

- Replace the truthiness check with an explicit `is not None` test in
  `detokenize_top_logprobs_tokens`. This matches the actual sentinel used to
  mark skipped positions and works for both lists and tensors.
- Add a CPU unit test
  (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_top_logprobs_tensor.py`)
  that reproduces the crash with a multi-element tensor value and verifies the
  None-sentinel and plain-list paths.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — this is an error-path correctness fix. It does not touch kernels or model
forward code and does not change model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no impact on inference speed.

title: Fix multi-tokenizer batch request output routing (health stuck at 503)
author: whybeyoung
body:
In multi-http-worker mode (--tokenizer-worker-num > 1), generate_request called _init_req_state(obj) before _attach_multi_http_worker_info(obj).

For a batch request, _init_req_state accesses obj[i], and GenerateReqInput.__getitem__ builds and CACHES the per-index sub-objects (in _sub_obj_cache), copying the parent's http_worker_ipc at that moment. Since the attach step ran afterwards, the parent's http_worker_ipc was still None when the sub-objects were cached, so every cached sub-object kept http_worker_ipc=None. Attaching later only stamped the parent.

As a result the tokenized batch items carried http_worker_ipc=None, the scheduler built each Req with http_worker_ipc=None, and the streamed BatchStrOutput had http_worker_ipcs=[None, ...]. MultiTokenizerRouter then dropped those outputs ('IPC name is None ... skipping'), so the PD prefill warmup POST never received a response, server_status stayed at Starting, and /health returned 503 forever. Single-tokenizer mode and non-batch requests were unaffected.

Fix: attach the multi-http-worker info before _init_req_state so the parent's http_worker_ipc is set before sub-objects are built and cached.

CC @hnyls2002

title: [AMD] Fix GPT-OSS MXFP4 accuracy on ROCm AITER path
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
CO-OWNER: @bingxche 

## Motivation

On ROCm AITER, the GPT-OSS MXFP4 fused-MoE path was producing silently wrong outputs. With these server flags on MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache --port 8000
```

the AITER dispatcher was selecting `module_moe_ck2stages_b16_fp4x2_preshuffle_off_b16_swiglu_per_1x32_mulWeightStage2`, a `preshuffle_off` codegen kernel. But the weights had already been preshuffled by `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, so the kernel interpreted shuffled bytes as un-shuffled and the model emitted nonsense. lm_eval gsm8k `flexible-extract` dropped from ~0.88 to ~0.21.

There were two root causes:

1. **Wrong shuffle layout.** The old path used `shuffle_weight_a16w4(..., 16, True)` / `shuffle_scale_a16w4(...)`, which produce the **gate/up-interleaved** tile layout (`is_guinterleave=True`). The AITER MXFP4 fused-MoE kernels tuned for GPT-OSS — both the FlyDSL `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` entries in `gptoss_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` (which have `gate_mode="separated"`) and the CK `module_moe_ck2stages_*_preshuffle_on_*` fallback — expect the **separated** (`is_guinterleave=False`) layout, identical to what ATOM uses on the same hardware.

2. **`is_shuffled` flag never set.** `shuffle_weight_a16w4` returns a tensor with `.is_shuffled=True`, but the call site did `layer.w13_weight.data = shuffle_weight_a16w4(...)`. Assigning to `.data` does not copy custom Python attributes, so `layer.w13_weight.is_shuffled` stayed unset. `aiter.fused_moe` reads this via `getattr(w1, "is_shuffled", False)` and, seeing `False`, dispatches the `preshuffle_off` codegen — which assumes the weight bytes are *not* shuffled. With actually-shuffled bytes, this gives garbage output.

The two bugs interact: even if the layout had been correct, the missing `is_shuffled` flag would still have routed to the wrong codegen branch.

## Modifications

- **`Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` (`_use_aiter` branch)** — replace `shuffle_weight_a16w4` / `shuffle_scale_a16w4` with `shuffle_weight(..., is_guinterleave=False, gate_up=...)` / `shuffle_scale(..., is_guinterleave=False, gate_up=...)`. This matches the layout `gptoss_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` flydsl entries (e.g. `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_t32x128x256_w2`) were tuned against, and the same layout ATOM produces. Set `layer.w13_weight.is_shuffled = True` and `layer.w2_weight.is_shuffled = True` after shuffling so AITER picks the `preshuffle_on` codegen.

- **`Mxfp4MoEMethod.apply` (`_use_aiter` branch)** — after `layer.w13_weight.view(torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2)`, re-tag the new view with `is_shuffled = True` (the `.view()` produces a fresh tensor that drops Python attributes). Also forward `swiglu_limit=self.moe_runner_config.swiglu_limit or 0.0` to `AiterMoeQuantInfo` so the OAI swiglu clamp gets through to AITER.

- **`AiterRunnerCore.run`** — gate the `GateMode.INTERLEAVE` selection behind a new env var `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV` and default to `GateMode.SEPARATED`. The default matches the new weight layout and the gptoss_fp4 tuned config; the env var is only for the rare case where someone shuffles weights into the gate/up-interleaved layout on purpose.

- **`environ.py`** — register `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV = EnvBool(False)` in the AMD & ROCm section.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified with `lm_eval gsm8k --num_fewshot 3` on gpt-oss-120b @ MI355X:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=/path/to/gpt-oss-120b/,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=65,max_retries=3,max_gen_toks=2048,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 3
```

| Filter | Before this PR (SGLang) | After this PR (SGLang) | ATOM baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flexible-extract` | ~0.21 (broken) | **0.8810 ± 0.0089** | 0.8825 ± 0.0089 |
| `strict-match` | — | **0.3541 ± 0.0132** | 0.3487 ± 0.0131 |

Both post-fix numbers are within one standard error of ATOM, the working baseline on the same hardware / aiter commit. To cross-check that the fused-MoE inputs really are bit-identical between the two stacks after the fix, I instrumented `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe_` to dump byte-level signatures of `w1`, `w2`, `w1_scale`, `w2_scale`, `bias1`, `bias2`, `is_shuffled`, etc. for the first two MoE calls per process, and ran both ATOM (`./run_gpt-oss.sh`) and SGLang back-to-back with the same model. Layer 0 and layer 1 produced identical `bytesum` and `head8` for every weight/scale/bias tensor between the two, and `is_shuffled=True` on both sides.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf regression expected — this PR only changes the *layout* of the MXFP4 weights produced at load time and the `is_shuffled` flag carried into AITER. The kernels picked at runtime are the same family (`flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` for `M >= 256`, CK `module_moe_ck2stages_*_preshuffle_on_*` for small-M decode), only now they receive correctly-laid-out inputs. No new ops, no extra copies.

Sample kernel selection from a server log on MI355X (gfx950, `--max-running-requests 128`):

```
[fused_moe] using 2stage (kernelName1='flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_t64x128x256_w4_bnt0',
  kernelName2='flydsl_moe2_afp4_wfp4_bf16_t64x128x256_atomic') for (256, 16384, 3072, 3072, 128, 4, Swiglu, bf16, fp4x2, fp4x2, per_1x32, True, False)
[fused_moe] using 2stage default for (256, <small M>, 3072, 3072, 128, 4, Swiglu, bf16, bf16, fp4x2, per_1x32, True, False)
```

title: [Spec] Fix Gemma 4 MTP with `trtllm_mha` crash issue
author: kpham-sgl
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`trtllm_mha` + FROZEN_KV MTP (NEXTN) on hybrid-SWA models (e.g. Gemma-4) crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access once the SWA pool fills past the SWA-vs-full layer ratio (issue [#26957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26957), prior attempt [#26531](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26531)). `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` cached its SWA state at `__init__` from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool`. On the draft worker that is the draft's own non-SWA pool, so `use_sliding_window_kv_pool` was `False` and the SWA→full page-index translation became dead code — SWA layers then got raw full-pool indices and read the smaller SWA k-cache out of bounds.

## Modifications

- Resolve the SWA pool from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool_allocator` (`get_kvcache()`) instead of `token_to_kv_pool`. In FrozenKVMTP the draft's `token_to_kv_pool` is swapped to the target's `SWAKVPool` per forward call, but `token_to_kv_pool_allocator` is set once at init and is stable — the correct source of truth.
- Mirrors FlashInfer, which already gates SWA eligibility on the allocator (`isinstance(token_to_kv_pool_allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator)`, `flashinfer_backend.py:1027`).
- Not registering the Gemma-4 draft as hybrid-SWA: the draft owns no KV (frozen), so its own `SWAKVPool` would be keyed by draft layer ids while attention runs on remapped target layer ids (KeyError + wasted alloc); the allocator already points at the correct target pool.

## Accuracy Tests

Reproduced end-to-end on B200 (SM100) with [repro_26957_e2e.py](https://gist.github.com/kpham-sgl/d696a3b8c2fdc959c940f7a8afdd9c9b): crashes before the fix (CUDA illegal memory access), passes after.

title: fix(disagg): correct DSA/SWA state-page transfer mismatch in PD disaggregation
author: kflansburg
body:
# fix(disagg): correct DSA/SWA state-page transfer mismatch in PD disaggregation

## Motivation

On a disaggregated (PD) deployment of a DSA (sparse-attention, formerly NSA)
model — observed with GLM/DSA-FP8, `page_size=64`, mooncake transfer backend —
the prefill transfer worker can crash while sending the hybrid "state/extra"
pool to decode:

```
File ".../disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py", in _send_kvcache_generic
    prefill_kv_blocks, dst_kv_blocks = group_concurrent_contiguous(...)
File ".../disaggregation/common/utils.py", in group_concurrent_contiguous
    brk = np.where((np.diff(src_indices) != 1) | (np.diff(dst_indices) != 1))[0] + 1
ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (2,) (0,)
```

There are two layered problems:

1. **Root cause (length mismatch).** On the last chunk, the prefill side
   enumerates its DSA/SWA state-page list over `seq_len = len(req.fill_ids)`. By
   send time `fill_ids` already includes the token sampled during prefill
   (`output_ids` is appended before `send_kv_chunk(last_chunk=True)`), so it is
   longer than the prompt. But the decode side registers its destination state
   pages over `len(origin_input_ids)` (`DecodePreallocQueue`), and the main
   KV-pool transfer is already clamped to
   `min(len(fill_ids), len(origin_input_ids))`. When the sampled token crosses a
   page boundary, prefill emits one extra state page that decode never
   registered, so the prefill (src) and decode (dst) index arrays differ in
   length.

2. **Fragile helper.** `group_concurrent_contiguous` only early-returns when the
   *source* is empty and otherwise assumes equal-length inputs. Unequal lengths
   either raise a cryptic NumPy broadcast error (non-broadcastable shapes) or
   silently produce wrong groupings (broadcastable shapes).

## Modifications

- `disaggregation/prefill.py` (`SchedulerDisaggregationPrefillMixin.send_kv_chunk`):
  compute the last-chunk state `seq_len` as
  `min(len(req.fill_ids), len(req.origin_input_ids))`, matching the decode-side
  registration and the clamped main-pool transfer range. The value is shared by
  `_dsa_payload` and `_swa_payload`, so both hybrid-state paths are corrected.
- `disaggregation/common/utils.py` (`group_concurrent_contiguous`): early-return
  `[], []` when *either* index array is empty, and raise a descriptive
  `ValueError` when both are non-empty but of unequal length — converting a
  cryptic broadcast error / silent mis-grouping into a clean no-op or a clear
  failure. Defense-in-depth in case other callers pass mismatched arrays.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py`: add CPU unit
  tests for `group_concurrent_contiguous` covering contiguous/discontiguous
  grouping, both-empty, empty-src, the empty-dst regression, and the
  mismatched-length error.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-forward changes. The prefill `seq_len` fix equals the previous
`len(fill_ids)` in the common case (no page-boundary crossing), so behaviour is
unchanged; it only removes the over-enumerated trailing state page. The helper
change is unchanged for equal-length inputs. End-to-end validation on a DSA
PD-disaggregated deployment is recommended.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact (two size checks; one `min()`).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit (black/isort/ruff pass).
- [x] Add unit tests.

title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
author: stepinto
body:
## Motivation

When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash.  The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607.

## Modifications

This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue.  I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1.

1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads.  pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch.  PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues.  This prevents divergence.

2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads.  Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN).  This behavior is consistent with TP.

This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works.  Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted.  However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread.  This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead.

## Accuracy Tests

Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`.

I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model.

I ran two groups:

- Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled.  Resolved 356/500.
- Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled.  Resolved 353/500.

I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B.  The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. 

Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test.  Hints to make L3 are in-use:
- Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests.
- Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2.

```sh
# Group A
sglang serve \
    --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp-size 8 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --disable-cuda-graph \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
```

title: [hicache] Fix UnifiedRadixCache write-back load_back / eviction crashes
author: libertyeagle
body:
## Summary
Fixes two write-back HiCache crashes in `UnifiedRadixCache`.

## 1. `_evict_device_leaf` triggers host eviction even if `write_backup` fails with host page allocation.
The current logic of `_evict_device_leaf` is:
```python
# unified_radix_cache.py
        if not node.backuped:
            if (
                self.cache_controller is not None
                and self.cache_controller.write_policy == "write_back"
            ):
                self.write_backup(node, write_back=True)
                self.writing_check(write_back=True)
                self._evict_to_host(node, tracker)
                return
```
where `self.write_backup` may fails due to host allocation fails, e.g., if most host pages are locked and host page allocation fails at `host_indices = self.cache_controller.write(...)`. `self.write_backup` returns 0. In this case, we cannot treat the node as backed up and cannot do `self._evict_to_host(...)`. In `hiradix_cache.py`:
```python
# hiradix_cache.py
def evict(self, params: EvictParams):
       ...
       if not x.backuped:
                if self.cache_controller.write_policy == "write_back":
                    # write to host if the node is not backuped
                    written = self.write_backup(x, write_back=True)
                    num_evicted += written
                    if written > 0:
                        write_back_nodes.append(x)
      ...

        if self.cache_controller.write_policy == "write_back":
            self.writing_check(write_back=True)
            for node in write_back_nodes:
                assert node.backuped
                self._evict_backuped(node)
```
For the nodes that fails backup, they will not be evicted. To match this logic, we can do:
```python
            if (
                self.cache_controller is not None
                and self.cache_controller.write_policy == "write_back"
            ):
                written = self.write_backup(node, write_back=True)
                if written == 0:
                    return
                self.writing_check(write_back=True)
                self._evict_to_host(node, tracker)
                return
```
Or alternatively, we can just drop the device node without backing it up.

Without the fix, we will trigger:
```
assert node.backuped                                  # _evict_to_host
```

## 2. `load_back` does not lock the host value of the nodes to load back, causing device eviction's `write_backup` evicting the host values.

In `load_back`, if there is not enough device KV pages, a device eviction will trigger to release enough pages.
```python
        if avail < kv_tokens:
            needed = kv_tokens - avail
            result = self.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=needed))
            if result.num_tokens_evicted < needed:
                self.dec_lock_ref(best_match_node, ancestor_lock_params)
                return False
```
However, during the evict, evicted device nodes will trigger `self.write_backup`, potentially causing host eviction. The nodes to be loaded back's host values must be protected. `hiradix_cache.py` does not have this problem because 
```
# hiradix_cache.py
    def load_back(
        self, node: TreeNode, mem_quota: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:

        # protect the ancestor nodes from eviction
        result = self.inc_lock_ref(ancester_node)
        delta = result.delta

    def inc_lock_ref(self, node: TreeNode) -> IncLockRefResult:
        if self.disable:
            return IncLockRefResult(delta=0)

        delta = 0
        while node != self.root_node:
            if node.lock_ref == 0:
                self.evictable_size_ -= len(node.key)
                self.protected_size_ += len(node.key)
                delta -= len(node.key)
            node.lock_ref += 1
            self._update_leaf_status(node)
            self._update_host_leaf_status(node)
            node = node.parent
        return IncLockRefResult(delta=delta)
```

`inc_lock_ref` protects the nodes whether it has device values or not (whether it's in device or host). In the unified radix cache, since there is SWA, `acquire_component_lock` adds an mechanism to skip nodes without device values, and it is also applied on full_component:
```python
# unified_cache_components/full_component.py
    def acquire_component_lock(
        self,
        node: UnifiedTreeNode,
        result: IncLockRefResult,
        lock_host: bool = False,
    ) -> IncLockRefResult:

        # Skip the bottom evicted segment
        while cur is not root and cur.component_data[ct].value is None:
            result.skip_lock_node_ids.setdefault(ct, set()).add(cur.id)
            cur = cur.parent
```
Hence, I think we need to lock the host values of the load back nodes, preventing them from eviction. This would happens when, e.g., we have 2 long requests. One request is fresh in GPU, while the other in host. Once the host side request is hit again, during its load back the device side request is evicted, `write_backup` triggered, and host pages need to be freed to accommodate it. 

We can directly use `inc_host_lock_ref` and `dec_host_lock_ref` for this.

Without the fix, we will trigger:
```
                assert cd.host_value is not None    # build_hicache_transfers in full_component.py
```

## Tests
Adds two unit tests in
`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`
(run across the FULL / FULL+SWA / FULL+Mamba configs):
- a host-locked leaf survives a host-eviction sweep that frees an unlocked one,
  and the lock is correctly released;
- `_evict_device_leaf` leaves the node on device when `write_backup` returns 0
  (with a negative control asserting `_evict_to_host` would otherwise raise).

## Original commits
- `032756d33`
- `e7147dd8e`

title: [NPU][Bugfix] fix MTP accuracy regression on Qwen3 hybrid models
author: AndyLi429
body:
## Motivation
When running Qwen3.6-35B-A3 (w4a8, MTP enabled) on Ascend NPU with `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`, ceval accuracy was below the expected baseline, and **enabling thinking mode made it worse** — accuracy dropped *and* the model produced repeated / looping reasoning content. **Three** bugs in the NPU hybrid-linear attention graph-mode verify path, the post-verify mamba state tracking, and the EAGLE speculative top-k selection are responsible.

After the fix:
- thinking **off**: ceval ~87.5% → **89.75%**
- thinking **on**: ceval ~86% → **90.71%**, and the repeated-reasoning regression is gone.

## Modifications

- **`ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` — SSM state index aliasing fix**:   During graph-mode target verify, `ssm_state_indices` was constructed over only   `(bs - num_padding) * draft_token_num` entries, with the padded tail zero-filled.   This made every padded-row verify write alias real request 0's intermediate   scratch slot; the post-verify state restore (`move_intermediate_cache`) then read   back corrupted data, producing garbage output or token repetition. Fix: construct   the indices over the full graph bucket `bs * draft_token_num` so each padded row   has its own unique scratch slot. The buffer is sized exactly `bs * draft_token_num`   (`init_cuda_graph_state`), so the full-buffer `copy_` is shape-safe, and the padded   scratch slots are never read back by the real-request restore.

- **`ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` — mamba state tracking after MTP verify**:   Implement the `mamba_track_indices` / `mamba_steps_to_track` scatter in   `update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify` that the CUDA path already has   (`hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`). When `mamba_track_indices` is set (mamba prefix   reuse — which long, thinking-mode sequences trigger), the verify-time SSM   intermediate state is scattered into the persistent track slots via
  `move_intermediate_cache`. Conv state needs NPU-specific handling: unlike CUDA,   NPU keeps **no** per-step `intermediate_conv_window` cache, so the tracked conv   state is reconstructed by copying the working slot's *pre-rollback* conv state into   the track slot, then independently rolling back both the working slots and the   track slots by their respective step counts (`conv_state_rollback`). Without this,   prefix reuse restored a **stale** SSM/conv state, which is what produced the   repeated reasoning content and the thinking-mode accuracy drop.

- **`eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` / `eagle_worker_v2.py` — NPU top-k fast-path guard**:   The `topk == 1` argmax fast-path was already gated to exclude ROCm with   `not _is_hip` (ROCm guard, added in #26358). NPU's argmax tie-break similarly   diverges from the full `softmax + topk` path on certain logit distributions,   corrupting MTP draft selection. Add `not _is_npu` to the same guard at all three   call sites so NPU takes the numerically-consistent `softmax → fast_topk` path.   (The NPU draft-extend graph runner inherits `run_once` from the CUDA runner, so  the guard in eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` is live for NPU.)

## Implementation note (NPU conv-state tracking)

Unlike the CUDA path — which scatters the tracked conv state directly from the per-step intermediate_conv_window_cache` — NPU has no per-step conv intermediate. The tracked conv state is therefore reconstructed from the working slot *before* its rollback, then rolled back independently to the desired step. This relies on track slots and working slots being disjoint and on `conv_state_rollback` reproducing the per-step window; both are exercised by the thinking-mode ceval run in Result 2 below (which is the configuration that actually drives `mamba_track_indices` to be non-`None`).

## Accuracy Tests

Model: **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8**, MTP enabled, Ascend NPU.
Eval: evalscope, dataset = ceval, 1346 samples.

**Launch command:**
```bash
GDN_ATTN_BACKEND_TRITON=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1 nohup python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path ${workspace}/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/ \
--stream-response-default-include-usage \
--attention-backend ascend \
--device npu \
--tp-size 2 \
--chunked-prefill-size 20480 \
--max-prefill-tokens 20480 \
--trust-remote-code \
--host 0.0.0.0 \
--mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
--port 9811 \
--enable-prefill-delayer \
--prefill-delayer-max-delay-passes 30 \
--cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 6 8 10 16 20 24 \
--max-running-request 24 \
--context-length 262144 \
--mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
--max-mamba-cache-size 80 \
--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
--reasoning-parser qwen3 \
--enable-metrics \
--enable-multimodal \
--limit-mm-data-per-request '{"video": 0, "audio": 0}' \
--dtype bfloat16 \
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \
--speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
--speculative-num-steps 3 \
--speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4  > sglang.log 2>&1 &
```

**Eval command** (the two results below differ only in
`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`):
```bash
evalscope eval --model ${workspace}/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/ --api-url http://127.0.0.1:9811/v1 --api-key EMPTY --eval-type openai_api --generation-config '{
      "max_tokens": 20000,
      "seed": 3407,
      "top_p":0.8,
      "top_k":20,
      "temperature": 0.6,
      "n":1,
      "timeout": 60,
      "stream": true,
      "extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}}' --datasets ceval --dataset-hub Local --dataset-args '{"ceval": {"local_path": "${workspace}/dataset_eval"}}' --eval-batch-size 24 --ignore-errors
```

**Summary:**

| Version | Thinking | Dataset | Samples | mean_acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| This PR (fixed) | off | ceval | 1346 | **0.8975** (89.75%) |
| main (buggy MTP) | off | ceval | 1346 | ~0.875 (87.5%) |
| This PR (fixed) | on | ceval | 1346 | **0.9071** (90.71%) |
| main (buggy MTP) | on | ceval | 1346 | ~0.86 (86%), + repeated reasoning content |

title: [HiCache] Fix crash when using PP + HiCache L2
author: stepinto
body:
## Motivation

HiCache does not work well with PP.  It leads to server crash. 

I have tried to solve the PP + HiCache L2+ L3 in a single patch #27010.  But that patch became larger and larger when I try to deal with `UnifiedRadixCache` and `HybridCacheController`.  Let me divide that patch into smaller ones.

This patch fixes PP + L2 only, leaving L3 unsolved.

## Modifications

The reason to server crash is due to lack of synchronization beteeen scheduler threads of PP0 and PP1.  The details are discussed in #22607. 

This patch introduced a new synchrnoization mechanism called **pp_sync** for scheduler threads.  

PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the exact same number of events from its queues. This prevents divergence.

## Tests

### Reproduce

A minimal reproduce step for "PP + L2 => crash" issue:

```sh
sglang serve \
  --model-path=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \
  --pp-size=2 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
  --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024))

python -m sglang.bench_serving --num-prompts 1000

Got this error:
RuntimeError: shape '[3013, -1, 128]' is invalid for input of size 8192000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
```

This patch fixes that crash.

### Effectiveness of L2 cache

I tested Qwen3-32B the following configuration:
- pp-size=4
- tp-size=2
- \#tokens in L1 = 256K
- \#tokens in L2 = 512K

title: [HiCache] Fix SWA L3 cache miss due to a prefetch/hit len mismatch
author: vladnosiv
body:
## Motivation

Currently, such a test does not work with SWA + HiCache L3.:
1) Make a prefill of N tokens (N % page_size == 0)
2) /flush_cache
3) Make a prefill of the same N tokens, see the >= N - page_size cache hit

Prefetch N tokens from storage with a full cache hit due to SWA creates the following tree `(host_len, swa_host_len)`:

```
(N - page_size, null) --> (page_size, page_size)
```

But then after the prefetch, the correction for logprobs is used during the match:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8e836e7dc9b8ff48987c21fdcf6bcd65b16a9837/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1143-L1148

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8e836e7dc9b8ff48987c21fdcf6bcd65b16a9837/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1082

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8e836e7dc9b8ff48987c21fdcf6bcd65b16a9837/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1093-L1096

Due to the correction, the match does not see a leaf of the tree and as a result, there is no entry into the cache, because we did not prefetch the necessary SWA.

For non-SWA models, this is ok, because we can use the father of the leaf.

## Modifications

We align the match in the prefetch with the subsequent match.

After the fix after prefetch tree looks like:
```
(N - 2 * page_size, null) --> (page_size, page_size)
```
And we can hit `(N - page_size) / (N - 1)` tokens

title: fix(fa3): no NaN embeddings with fa_skip_kv_cache under piecewise CUDA graph
author: jasperjiaguo
body:
## Summary

Fixes NaN embeddings emitted by the `fa_skip_kv_cache` embedding fast path (added in #21971) when **piecewise CUDA graph** is enabled. ~40% of **short** embedding inputs came back as fully-NaN vectors; long inputs were unaffected.

## Root cause

`fa_skip_kv_cache` serves attention with `flash_attn_varlen_func` on raw K/V. Under a piecewise CUDA graph the model forward runs at a **padded token-bucket size**, so the query tensor `q` has more rows (`B`) than `cu_seqlens_q` covers (`N`, the real token count).

`flash_attn_varlen_func` requires `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]`. With `N < B` that contract is violated, and the boundary query block corrupts the **last real token's** output. Embedding models use LAST-token pooling, so that corrupted row *is* the returned embedding → NaN.

Only short inputs are affected: long inputs fill the top bucket (no padding / the boundary lands harmlessly), while short inputs get padded into a small bucket, placing the last real token right at the corrupting boundary. It reproduces only with the FA3 backend (the flashinfer backend is already piecewise-padding-aware), and is independent of `--prefill-only-disable-kv-cache` (it is gated on the embedding config, not that flag).

## Fix

Append the padded tail `[N, B)` as a **dummy, self-attending segment** so `cu_seqlens = [0, …, N, B]` and `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]` holds again. The real-token segments are untouched (their attention is unchanged), and the padding rows get valid, isolated self-attention instead of reading uninitialized memory. This mirrors how the flashinfer backend reserves a dummy request for piecewise padding.

## Validation

H100, Qwen3-0.6B embedding model (fp16), fa3 + piecewise:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| previously-NaN short inputs | 81/81 NaN | **0** |
| overall NaN | ~40% of short | **0/1000** |
| cosine vs non-piecewise (correct) path | — | **mean 0.9999987, min 0.9999946** (all 1000 ≥ 0.99999) |

So the fix removes the NaN *and* leaves correct embeddings bit-for-bit equivalent.

## Test

Adds `test/registered/prefill_only/test_fa_skip_kv_cache_piecewise_nan.py`:
- `test_no_nan_with_piecewise` — short inputs (~1–150 tokens) through fa3 + piecewise + `fa_skip_kv_cache`, asserts no embedding is NaN.
- `test_matches_non_piecewise` — asserts cosine > 0.99 vs the non-piecewise path.

Reproducing requires the production piecewise config (`piecewise_cuda_graph_max_tokens`, i.e. `ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH`) and **batch size 1** (one request per forward): when requests are batched, only each batch's tail request abuts the padding boundary, which masks the per-request failure rate.

title: [Bug] Fix out-of-range token id crashing tp=1 `VocabParallelEmbedding`
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- `gen_radix_tree` builds requests with `random.randint(0, 32000)` (inclusive), which can emit token id `32000` -- out of range for a 32000-vocab model (valid `0..31999`)
- At `tp=1`, `VocabParallelEmbedding.forward` does not mask input ids, so the bad id reaches `F.embedding` and crashes with a `vectorized_gather_kernel` device-side assert
- Flaky (single-GPU only; the generator is unseeded, ~1.2% of runs); surfaces in CI as a GPU coredump in `TestEagleLlama2Retract.test_radix_attention`

## Fix
- `gen_radix_tree`: `random.randint(0, 31999)` -- fix the off-by-one
- `VocabParallelEmbedding.forward`: gated `maybe_detect_oob` on the input ids, so an out-of-range or negative (unmasked sentinel) id surfaces as a located assert instead of a silent OOB / coredump
- `maybe_detect_oob`: assert lower and upper bounds separately so the message names which one failed

title: Fix TP deadlock in unified radix cache writing_check / loading_check
author: ispobock
body:
## Motivation

A permanent TP deadlock has been observed in `UnifiedRadixCache.writing_check` after a long run with HiCache enabled. py-spy fingerprint:

- TP0: `all_reduce → writing_check → check_hicache_events → get_new_batch_prefill_raw → event_loop_overlap`
- TP1-3: `broadcast → broadcast_pyobj → recv_requests → event_loop_overlap` (next iteration)

TP0 entered the all_reduce in `writing_check` while TP1-3 took the early-return path on empty `ongoing_write_through` and advanced to the next event-loop iteration's `recv_requests` broadcast. Mismatched collectives → 300s watchdog → process kill.

`loading_check` has the same anti-pattern (early-return on empty `ongoing_load_back` before an all_reduce) and is fixed alongside.

## Fix

Always enter the all_reduce regardless of local queue state. An empty local queue contributes 0 to the MIN-reduce; the `while finish_count > 0` loop becomes a no-op. Cheap and collective-safe.

## Tradeoff

Removing the early-return does not address the underlying source of cross-rank `ongoing_write_through` divergence (e.g. `write_backup` returning 0 on a subset of ranks when host-pool alloc or aux-pool alloc fails). With this fix the process no longer deadlocks, but the divergent entries can be left undrained — manifesting as slow host-pool / lock-ref leak rather than a hard hang. A follow-up will make `write_backup` enqueue decisions themselves collective-consistent.

title: [AMD] Fix DeepSeek V4 Pro c128 state tensor dtype mismatch error and c4_sparse_raw_indices attribute error in cuda graph phase
author: At1a8
body: ## Motivation coworked with @yctseng0211，https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27525 The compress JIT kernel (c128_v2.cuh) requires `kv_score_buffer`/ `kv_score_input`/ `ape` to have same dtype. So before feeding the kernel, we need unify all three to the same dtype. Otherwise, the mismatch crashes outright `dtype=float32 not in allowed [bfloat16]`. similar error on jit norm when enable `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM` c4_sparse_raw_indices attribute error ## Modifications - template the C128 / C4 compress kernel on per-tensor dtypes `BufFloat` / `InFloat` / `ApeFloat` / `OutFloat` (cast each input to fp32 at load; no host-side `.to()`) in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/c128_v2.cuh` and `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/c4_v2.cuh` - template the fused norm+rope kernel on a separate `WeightFloat` for the fp32 RMSNorm weight in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/fused_norm_rope_v2.cuh` - pass the per-tensor dtypes when building the JIT modules (`_jit_compress_module`, `_jit_compress_norm_rope_module`) in `python/sglang/jit_kernel/dsv4/compress.py` - add `c4_sparse_raw_indices` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` ## title: Fix NaN in triton EAGLE spec-v2 draft-extend CUDA graph at topk>1 (wrong qo_indptr stride)
author: hnyls2002
body:
The draft-extend CUDA-graph metadata built `qo_indptr` with a per-req stride of `num_steps+1`, but the runner lays out `num_draft_tokens` tokens/req. For topk>1 these differ, so at bs>1 each req's queries read from the wrong offset -> NaN (bs==1 and eager are unaffected). Use `num_draft_tokens` for the v2 draft-extend path.

title: [NPU][Bugfix] Fix accuracy issue in no-graph with MTP
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

Fix MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding accuracy regression on NPU with `--disable-cuda-graph`. Three places unconditionally called `mark_forward_metadata_ready()`, which prevented attention metadata from being properly initialized on the non-cuda-graph (eager) path for NPU backends.

## Modifications

- `eagle_info_v2.py` ( `prepare_for_extend_to_fill_draft_kvcache` ): Only mark metadata ready on the cuda-graph path. On NPU non-graph, `init_forward_metadata` runs pre-padding and produces wrong block_table shapes after `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads the batch.
- `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` ( `verify` ): Only mark metadata ready on the cuda-graph path. NPU non-graph verify needs forward_extend to init metadata post-padding.
- `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` ( `_draft_extend_for_decode` ): Only mark metadata ready on the cuda-graph path. The batch-level marker was blocking `draft_runner_list[1+]` from initializing their own per-runner attention metadata.
- `npu_graph_runner.py`: Replace hardcoded `self.attr_name[AttentionArch.MLA]` with `self._get_update_attr_name()` in graph replay. The old code always used `"actual_seq_lengths_kv"`, which is incorrect for MiMoV2 models — they require `"actual_seq_kvlen"`. The dynamic selector returns the correct attr_name per model architecture. This caused graph-mode-only accuracy regression (gibberish output) when cuda graph was enabled without MTP.

## Accuracy Tests

```

export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \

    --device npu \

    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
```

title: Fix Mistral GSM8K chat eval
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

Move the nightly text-model GSM8K eval from the hand-rolled 5-shot chat-API scorer to `sgl-eval` (zero-shot chat, `\boxed{}` answer, `math_verify` grading), fill in real thresholds for every nightly model, and fix the CI install-order bug that blocked the sgl-eval path.

## Root cause

`nightly-test-text-accuracy-2-gpu-h100` was red on Mistral-family models (e.g. `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` 0.414 vs 0.47 threshold). Reproduced on a devbox: the model generates correctly with `finish_reason=stop` and no runaway — it is not a serving regression. The old scorer wraps a completion-style 5-shot `Question:/Answer:` prompt in Mistral's `[INST]` chat template, which breaks the few-shot context for Mistral-family models; last-number extraction then occasionally grabs the wrong number when the response continues into another Q/A block.

## What this PR does

1. **Switch the nightly eval to `sgl-eval`** (`api="sgl_eval"` in `test_text_models_gsm8k_eval.py`). sgl-eval is a black-box subprocess running zero-shot chat with `\boxed{}` formatting and `math_verify` grading, which avoids the few-shot/chat-template interaction.
2. **Make sgl-eval opt-in**: only the nightly correctness eval sets `api='sgl_eval'`. Every other gsm8k caller keeps the hand-rolled 5-shot completion scorer unchanged.
3. **Fill real thresholds** for all 15 nightly models, baselined on H100 2-GPU over the full 1319-example split (measured_score − 0.05).
4. **Fix the antlr4 install-order bug** (below).

## The CI install-order bug

sgl-eval's `latex2sympy2_extended` requires `antlr4-python3-runtime` 4.9.3 / 4.11 / 4.13.2 and raises `ImportError: Unsupported ANTLR version 4.7.2` on 4.7.x. The `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.9.3` pin in `python/pyproject.toml [test]` was not enough — CI still loaded 4.7.2:

```
install_sglang        # [dev]→[test] → sgl-eval → latex2sympy2_extended (needs antlr4 4.9.3) ✓
install_extra_deps    # uv pip install -e lmms-eval/ → lmms-eval v0.5 → latex2sympy2 1.9.1
                      #   hard-pins antlr4==4.7.2, clobbering 4.9.3 ✗
install_test_tools    # does not restore antlr4
```

The clobber comes from `latex2sympy2==1.9.1` (a transitive dep of `lmms-eval`, distinct from `latex2sympy2_extended`), which hard-pins `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.7.2`.

Fix: in `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`, right after the `lmms-eval` install, force it back:
```bash
$PIP_CMD install "antlr4-python3-runtime==4.9.3" --force-reinstall --no-deps $PIP_INSTALL_SUFFIX
```

## Thresholds (H100 2-GPU, full 1319 split, sgl-eval zero-shot)

| model | measured | threshold |
|---|---|---|
| meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 0.81 | 0.77 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B | 0.81 | 0.76 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-4B | 0.82 | 0.77 |
| meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct | 0.95 | 0.90 |
| mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 | 0.44 | 0.39 |
| Qwen/Qwen2-57B-A14B-Instruct | 0.51 | 0.46 |
| neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 | 0.82 | 0.77 |
| neuralmagic/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8 | 0.28 | 0.23 |
| neuralmagic/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 | 0.85 | 0.80 |
| zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 | 0.77 | 0.73 |
| neuralmagic/gemma-2-2b-it-FP8 | 0.07 | 0.02 |
| neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8 | 0.94 | 0.89 |
| neuralmagic/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8 | 0.40 | 0.35 |
| neuralmagic/Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8 | 0.88 | 0.83 |
| neuralmagic/Qwen2-57B-A14B-Instruct-FP8 | 0.45 | 0.40 |

Low scorers (`gemma-2-2b-it-FP8` 0.07, `Mistral-7B-v0.3-FP8` 0.28) are genuine — verified on a devbox that the model emits `\boxed{}` correctly and the grader extracts the answer (no format issue, no `no_answer`). GSM8K is a numeric answer task, so these reflect weak zero-shot reasoning on small/older-instruct models, not an eval bug.

## Validation

- `/rerun-test test/registered/eval/test_text_models_gsm8k_eval.py` on 2-gpu-h100 — all 15 models pass: [run 28645576771](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28645576771) ✅
- Prior rerun [28642161462](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28642161462) failed with the antlr4 clobber on all models — fixed here.

title: [Metrics] Fix `fwd_occupancy` reading NaN on every decode log line; probe-free `base-a`
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary
- `update_device_timer` clobbered the `fwd_occupancy` gauge with NaN at every device-timer window start. The window counter advances on all batch results while the decode-log cadence counts decode batches only, so each prefill shifts their phase and the phase freezes during pure decode -- a workload can land every decode log line exactly on the NaN tick and report `fwd occupancy: nan` indefinitely. Concurrent eval workloads (e.g. the ngram spec CI tests) hit this constantly because prefills keep stepping the phase across the bad slot.
- Fix: keep the last published value at window start; NaN is still published when the value is truly stale (idle reset).
- Guard the occupancy division against `cpu_time <= 0` (hold last value), so a non-advancing timer cannot crash the scheduler loop.
- Disable `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT` for the `base-a` CI stage only: it runs the fwd-occupancy sanity kit, and the async-assert probes add GPU work that skews the measurement. Other stages keep the probes on.
- Raise `fwd_occupancy_threshold`: vanilla sanity 97 -> 99, EAGLE3 sanity 97 -> 98 (CUDA; AMD stays 80) -- with NaN-free sampling and probe-free `base-a`, the threshold can sit right under the ~99 measured median so occupancy regressions surface earlier.

All computed occupancy values are bit-identical to before; the fix only changes what is published on ticks that have no new sample.

## Verification
Qwen3-8B + `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`, `--decode-log-interval 10`, H200. Sustained concurrent load (40 rolling requests):

| | decode-line `fwd occupancy: nan` | prefill-line nan |
|---|---|---|
| main | 11 / 268 prints, in consecutive bursts | 30 (idle stale marker) |
| this PR | 2 / 279 prints, isolated, only on the first decode print right after an idle reset (intended stale semantics) | 30 (unchanged, intended) |

title: [Fix][MTP][MM] Fix EAGLE v2 chunked-prefill next-token chain crash on multimodal models due to placeholder tokens
author: litmei
body: ## Motivation An error was triggered when running a multimodal model with multimodal requests and enabling SpecV2. After enabling `ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, I observed that the crash occurred within the embedding layer.Upon debugging, I found that this regression was introduced by PR #26800. Specifically, the `_compute_chunked_req_next_prompt_token` method does not account for multimodal scenarios. In multimodal contexts, `input_ids` can contain placeholder/padding values that far exceed the vocab_size, leading to the subsequent error in the embedding layer. ## Modifications Fix `_compute_chunked_req_next_prompt_token` by validating against `vocab_size`. title: fix(moe): make FlashInfer A2A robust to collapsed global_num_tokens (moe_dense_tp_size NaN)
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer` with `--enable-dp-attention` silently produces NaN/inf logits (gsm8k ~0, or a `probability tensor contains inf/nan` device-side assert under sampling) when `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` is set. The FlashInfer CuteDSL/Cutlass MoE kernels are correct on their own; the corruption comes from per-rank A2A dispatch sizing.

Root cause: `moe_dense_tp_size` set makes `require_mlp_tp_gather()` return `False`, so the scheduler stores only the local rank count in `batch.global_num_tokens` instead of the all-gathered list (see the existing `TODO: handle the case when moe_dense_tp_size != 1` in `scheduler_components/dp_attn.py`). `FlashinferDispatcher.dispatch()` then sees `len(dp_global) > 1 == False` and takes the `else` branch (intended for `dp_size=1` / SP), setting `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank = x.shape[0]`. Under EP this local count differs across ranks, so the fixed-geometry `MoeAlltoAll` (combine reshapes to `[ep_size, runtime_max_tokens_per_rank, hidden]`) disagrees across ranks and reads/writes mismatched slots, producing NaN.

Only the FlashInfer dispatcher reads `get_dp_global_num_tokens()`; DeepEP / Mooncake / MoRI / NIXL size dispatch from a static `num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank` and are unaffected (so `moe_dense_tp_size=1` already works with them, e.g. DeepSeek).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py`: in `dispatch()`, when `ep_size > 1` and `moe_dense_tp_size` is set (the exact condition that collapses `global_num_tokens`), fall back to `self.max_num_tokens` (the static per-rank dispatch capacity, identical on every rank and bounding the workspace) instead of the per-rank-inconsistent `x.shape[0]`. CUDA-graph safe (fixed at init, no device sync). The normal multi-rank path (`max(dp_global)`) and the `dp_size=1` / SP path are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, 4x Blackwell, `tp4 / dp4 / ep4` + dp-attention + `flashinfer_cutedsl` + flashinfer A2A, full gsm8k (1319 examples, 8-shot):

| Config | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` | crash (`probability tensor contains inf/nan`) / 0.0 | **0.977** |

Reproduce:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp 4 --dp 4 --ep-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --disable-radix-cache --disable-flashinfer-autotune

python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --num-shots 8
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact on existing paths. The fallback triggers only for the previously-broken `moe_dense_tp_size=1` case.

## Checklist

- [x] Provided accuracy results above.
- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests.

title: fix(multimodal): return 400 for corrupt image inputs
author: Sunt-ing
body:
## Motivation

Corrupt, truncated, or non-image bytes in an OpenAI-compatible VLM request are client input errors, but the CPU PIL fallback currently can surface them as HTTP 500. `_load_image` returns a lazy `Image.open(...)` result without forcing decode or translating PIL decode failures; when that failure reaches the multimodal loader, the fast and legacy paths wrap it as `RuntimeError`, which serving treats as internal.

SGLang #27451 already keeps malformed base64 as a 400 in `_load_single_item`; this patch closes the remaining corrupt image-byte path. It also complements #26995: that PR proposes eager decode for throughput, but it does not translate PIL decode errors into `ValueError` or preserve them through the fast and legacy aggregation paths. The behavior matches vllm-project/vllm#38253.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: force `image.load()` in `_load_image`, then translate `OSError` / `SyntaxError` / `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError` into `ValueError("Failed to load image: ...")`.
- `python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`: let `ValueError` propagate through `fast_load_mm_data` and `legacy_load_mm_data` before the generic `Exception -> RuntimeError` wrapping.
- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`: add one CPU-registered test method that covers valid, garbage, empty, truncated-PNG, and broken-PNG-chunk inputs.

Serving already maps `ValueError` to 400. The forced decode does not add a new happy-path decode; valid images are decoded by preprocessing anyway, and this just moves the failure point before the heavier path runs.

## Testing

Real server E2E on A800-80GB with `Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct`, baseline without the fix vs fixed:

| input | baseline | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| valid PNG, valid JPEG, two valid images | 200 | 200 |
| non-image bytes | 500 | 400 `Failed to load image: cannot identify image file` |
| truncated PNG | 500 | 400 `Failed to load image: image file is truncated` |
| truncated JPEG | 500 | 400 `Failed to load image: Truncated File Read` |
| garbage bytes | 500 | 400 |
| two images, one corrupt | 500 | 400 |
| 12 concurrent, 6 valid and 6 corrupt | 6x200 + 6x500 | 6x200 + 6x400 |

Valid requests are unaffected, and `/health` stays 200 after the corrupt-input burst. The same matrix was also reproduced across six processor families covering both loader paths: `Qwen2.5-VL-3B`, `InternVL2-1B`, `Gemma-3-4B`, `GLM-4.1V-9B`, `Pixtral-12B` on the fast path and `MiniCPM-V-2_6` on the legacy path.

The GPU nvJPEG fast path stays correct. A truncated JPEG without the trailing marker does not enter `decode_jpeg`; a marker-valid but corrupt JPEG makes `decode_jpeg` raise, falls back to the CPU path, and returns 400 after this fix.

Current `upstream/main` branch checks:

- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=9 python -m pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py::TestLoadImage::test_corrupt_image_bytes_raise_value_error -q`: 1 passed, 4 subtests passed.
- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=9 python -m pytest test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py -q`: 1 passed, 2 skipped, 4 subtests passed.
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`: passed.
- `python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

<details><summary>repro command and client</summary>

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --port 30000 --trust-remote-code \
  --sampling-backend pytorch --attention-backend triton \
  --disable-cuda-graph --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --dtype bfloat16

# base64("not an image") = bm90IGFuIGltYWdl
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"x","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[
        {"type":"text","text":"describe"},
        {"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/jpeg;base64,bm90IGFuIGltYWdl"}}]}],
       "max_tokens":4}'
```

The server E2E above was run in the release-pinned validation environment (`sglang==0.5.12.post1`) before adapting the same fix onto current `upstream/main`. The current-main branch passes the focused unit and pre-commit checks listed above.
</details>

title: fix(precision): do not promote failed runs to the comparison baseline
author: JustinTong0323
body:
Follow-up to #26902 (nightly precision regression test).

## Problem

`_select_latest_run` selects the comparison baseline purely by recency (`push_index`) and ignores `pass_label`. The FAILED branch of the nightly test uploads the regressed tensors to the HF store with `pass_label="failed"` (intended only to preserve the diagnostic diff). Because the next night's `_maybe_hf_fetch` → `fetch_latest_baseline` → `_select_latest_run` picks the most-recent row regardless of label, a failed run becomes the next night's reference baseline.

This **masks persistent regressions after a single night**:

| Night | Event | Result |
|-------|-------|--------|
| N-1 | good baseline | PASS (green) |
| N | regression introduced → today(regressed) vs good baseline | **FAIL** → uploads regressed tensors as `pass_label="failed"` |
| N+1 | baseline = N's failed regressed run → today(still regressed) vs regressed | **PASS** ❌ |
| N+2+ | baseline already regressed | green forever |

CI shows red on night N then green from N+1 onward, making an unfixed regression look self-resolved. This defeats the test's core purpose (continuous regression detection). It manifests in the nominal HF-driven / cross-runner operating mode — i.e. exactly the case the HF store was built for (cold local baseline on a fresh/rotated runner).

This is distinct from the documented "rolling baseline" known-limitation, which covers *gradual* cumulative drift. Here a *sharp* single-night regression — and any persistent regression — is absorbed in one step via failed-run promotion, which also contradicts the FAILED-branch comment's stated intent ("so the diagnostic diff survives on HF").

## Fix

`_select_latest_run` now prefers the most-recent **non-failed** row, falling back to the most-recent failed row only when every candidate failed. Rows missing `pass_label` (legacy) remain usable (`!= "failed"`), preserving backward compatibility.

After the fix:
- Persistent regression: baseline stays pinned to the last good run → the regression is caught *every* night until fixed.
- Once fixed: baseline advances to the newest passed run.

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/$(true)/python/sglang/test/precision_baseline_store.py

## Testing

Added 4 unit tests to `TestSelectLatestRun` (`test/registered/unit/test_precision_baseline_store.py`):
- `test_prefers_older_passed_over_newer_failed`
- `test_prefers_baseline_established_over_newer_failed`
- `test_falls_back_to_failed_when_only_failed`
- `test_missing_pass_label_treated_as_usable` (legacy backward compat)

All existing `TestSelectLatestRun` cases still pass (no behavior change when no `failed` rows are present). Verified `_select_latest_run` against the full existing + new assertion set plus end-to-end masking scenarios (persistent-regression pinned to last good; baseline advances after fix).

`pre-commit` clean (isort / ruff / black / codespell / CI-registry validation).

title: Fix EagleDraftExtendInput missing kv_indptr crash with triton/DP attention
author: yctseng0211
body: ## Motivation pr-#24860 ("[Spec] Install `EagleDraftExtendInput` as the V2 draft-extend `spec_info`") changed the draft-extend `spec_info` from `EagleDraftInput` to the new `EagleDraftExtendInput`. However, several attention backends read `spec_info.kv_indptr` directly in `init_forward_metadata` for the decode/idle path, and `EagleDraftExtendInput` does not define that attribute. With EAGLE3 + DP attention, an idle DP rank goes through `forward_idle` -> `init_forward_metadata`, hitting: ``` File ".../layers/attention/triton_backend.py", line 570, in init_forward_metadata if spec_info is None or spec_info.kv_indptr is None: AttributeError: 'EagleDraftExtendInput' object has no attribute 'kv_indptr' ``` This crashes the scheduler and fails `test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_dp_attention.py`. It surfaces in AMD CI because that lane uses `--attention-backend triton`, while the CUDA lane uses `fa3` (the only backend that doesn't access `spec_info.kv_indptr`). The same crash would occur on any platform using the `triton`, `flashinfer`, `flashinfer_mla`, `aiter`, or `wave` backends. When it is `None` (the draft-extend idle batch case), the attention backends fall back to rebuilding plain metadata from `seq_lens`, matching the pre-a52ccd2 behavior. title: [Tokenizer] Fix abort racing server crash when large amount of aborts
author: hanming-lu
body:
An AbortReq echoed back from the scheduler can race the request's normal completion in the TokenizerManager handle_loop: a batch output may have already finished the request and deleted its rid_to_state entry before the abort echo is processed. Indexing rid_to_state directly then raises KeyError, which propagates out of handle_loop and is treated as fatal (the process is killed), taking down the whole server over a benign race.

This is common under mass client disconnects, and is amplified by the scheduler matching rids by prefix / abort_all, which fans a single abort out into many echoed AbortReqs.

Use dict.get() and return early when the state is already gone — there is nothing left to abort since the completion path already resolved the request.

title: [AMD] Fix Always mask padded topk_ids on HIP to prevent garbage MoE routing (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 accuracy regression)
author: kangwangamd
body:
## Motivation

`test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_8gpu.py` (`stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x`) was failing with a catastrophic GSM8K accuracy drop:

```
AssertionError: 0.1379833206974981 not greater than 0.94
```

i.e. accuracy collapsed from **>0.94 to ~0.09–0.14** on `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview` (MI35x, TP=8).

**Root cause:** commit `63df86f5` (PR #28188, *"Skip eplb bookkeeping and topk remap when EPLB is not in use on mori-ep / HIP"*) accidentally moved the padded-region masking **inside** the `_eplb_remap_enabled()` guard in `_post_process_topk_ids`:

```python
# After #28188 (broken for models without EPLB):
elif _is_hip:
    if _eplb_remap_enabled():                                  # False for MXFP4
        _mask_topk_ids_padded_region(topk_ids, ..., fill_value=0)   # never runs!
        topk_ids = topk_ids_logical_to_physical(...)
    _zero_topk_weights_padded_region(topk_weights, ...)
```

For models that do **not** use EPLB (the common case, including DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4), `_eplb_remap_enabled()` returns `False`, so `_mask_topk_ids_padded_region` is **never called**. The padded slots of `topk_ids` keep garbage/out-of-range expert IDs from the kernel. Although routing weights are zeroed, the aiter MoE / MXFP4 indexer kernels read `topk_ids` directly to index expert weight tables **before** the weighted sum, so the garbage IDs corrupt the computation and wreck accuracy.

## Modifications

- In `_post_process_topk_ids` (HIP branch), call `_mask_topk_ids_padded_region(topk_ids, num_token_non_padded, fill_value=0)` **unconditionally**, so padded tokens always get a valid in-range expert id (`0`; aiter cannot handle `-1`).
- Keep only the logical→physical remap (`topk_ids_logical_to_physical`) inside the `_eplb_remap_enabled()` guard — that part of #28188's intent is correct.
- `_zero_topk_weights_padded_region` remains unconditional (unchanged), so padded tokens still contribute nothing to the hidden state.

Net diff is small (+9 / −8 in `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`).

## Accuracy Tests

Validated end-to-end on **AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP=8** via the registered test (CI run [27598431399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27598431399)):

```
TestDeepseekR1MXFP4.test_a_gsm8k       -> Accuracy: 0.950   [PASS]   (was ~0.09)
TestDeepseekR1MXFP4.test_bs_1_speed    -> speed=152.01      [PASS]
TestDeepseekR1MXFP4MTP.test_a_gsm8k    -> Accuracy: 0.950 / 0.960   [PASS]
```

The masking logic was also unit-tested directly on MI355X: padded `topk_ids` are correctly clamped to `0`, real tokens are untouched, and the pre-fix garbage behavior is reproduced.

> **Note — one unrelated MTP failure remains:** `TestDeepseekR1MXFP4MTP` reports `avg_spec_accept_length=1.45 (<2.04)`. This is **not** caused by this PR (accuracy is a perfect 0.95, and this change only touches padded tokens). It is the cross-stream race fixed by #28410 — the MTP test enables `SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM`, which triggers the `predict.to(torch.int64)` plan-stream race introduced by #28043. This PR will be rebased and re-validated once #28410 lands.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact: the change only adds an unconditional in-place mask of the padded region (which the original pre-#28188 code already did). `test_bs_1_speed` is green at **152.01 token/s**.

title: [Bugfix] Fix MTP acceptance regression on plan stream by moving int64 cast before plan stream context
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation
Closes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28406.
PR #28043 fixed a DeepSeek-V4 DP dtype mismatch hang by normalizing predict to torch.int64 inside prepare_for_draft_extend . However, when the overlap plan stream is enabled, this cast executes on the plan stream while predict is produced on the main stream, creating a cross-stream data race that silently corrupts draft token ids and drops MTP acceptance to nearly zero.

## Modifications
- eagle_worker_v2.py : Move the predict.to(torch.int64) cast from inside prepare_for_draft_extend to _draft_extend_for_decode , before entering the plan stream context. The cast now runs on the main stream with correct synchronization.
- base_spec_worker.py : Update the comment in prepare_for_draft_extend to explain why dtype normalization must NOT be done inside this function, and that the caller should cast before entering the plan stream.

## Accuracy Tests
No impact on model output — the int64 cast preserves all token id values. The fix only changes where the cast executes (main stream vs. plan stream).

```

export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1

        --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \

        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
        --cuda-graph-bs 8 12 16 20 24 32 40 48 56 64 \
```

```
│ Model           │ Dataset   │ Metric   │ Subset   │   Num │   Score │ Cat.0   │
```

title: Fix Qwen MoE precision issue with PP and all-reduce fusion
author: 1e4ves
body: ## Motivation Fixes #27744 This is a small patch to fix the Qwen MoE precision issue when pipeline parallelism is used together with tensor parallelism and FlashInfer all-reduce fusion. When all-reduce fusion is enabled, the post-expert all-reduce can be deferred and fused into the next layer's prepare_attn path. This deferred reduction is tracked by _sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion, and the marker is normally consumed by the next layer. However, at a PP boundary, hidden states are wrapped into PProxyTensors and sent to the next pipeline stage. The Python-side fusion marker is not preserved across this boundary. As a result, one pending post-expert all-reduce can be skipped entirely, which leads to larger KL drift in PP+TP runs. ## Modification This patch simply flushes the pending MoE all-reduce before returning PPProxyTensors at the PP boundary, so the deferred reduction is completed before the tensor is handed to the next PP stage. The same issue can also happen with EP, because EP also requires a post-expert all-reduce. This patch handles that case as well by flushing the pending EP all-reduce at the PP boundary. ## Testing ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [PD] Fix data race in NixlKVManager for NIXL backend
author: nvjullin
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

In `NixlKVManager.__init__`,

```py
        if self.disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL:
            # ...
            for i, queue in enumerate(self.transfer_queues):
                # ...
                threading.Thread(
                    target=self.transfer_worker,
                    args=(queue, staging_buffer),
                    daemon=True,
                ).start()
            self._start_bootstrap_thread()
```
`transfer_worker` runs `self.agent.check_xfer_state` and `_start_bootstrap_thread` runs `self.agent.add_remote_agent`. The two functions run with released GIL and race on `std::unordered_map<std::string, nixlRemoteSection> remoteSections_;` in NIXL `src/core/agent_data.h`.

There is a lock protecting `remoteSections_`, but it requires configuring the agent to use the lock
```cpp
nixlAgentData::nixlAgentData(const std::string &name, const nixlAgentConfig &config)
    : name_(name),
      config_(config),
      useEtcd_(detectEtcd()),
      needsCommThread_(useEtcd_ || config.useListenThread),
      lock(effectiveSyncMode(config.syncMode, needsCommThread_)) {
```
where the `lock` argument decides whether to actually lock. The current config is to set `syncMode` to none, meaning no locking. This results in a data race, which is hard to hit unless you have a large disagg setup. When you do, it may manifest as a segfault
```
!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in PyCode_Addr2Line
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in _Py_DumpTracebackThreads
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in std::_Hashtable<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> >, std::pair<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const, nixlRemoteSection>, std::allocator<std::pair<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const, nixlRemoteSection> >, std::__detail::_Select1st, std::equal_to<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > >, std::hash<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > >, std::__detail::_Mod_range_hashing, std::__detail::_Default_ranged_hash, std::__detail::_Prime_rehash_policy, std::__detail::_Hashtable_traits<true, false, true> >::find(std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&) const
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlAgent::getXferStatus(nixlXferReqH*) const
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in pybind11::cpp_function::initialize<pybind11_init__bindings(pybind11::module_&)::{lambda(nixlAgent&, unsigned long)#36}, nixl_status_t, nixlAgent&, unsigned long, pybind11::name, pybind11::is_method, pybind11::sibling, pybind11::call_guard<pybind11::gil_scoped_release> >(pybind11_init__bindings(pybind11::module_&)::{lambda(nixlAgent&, unsigned long)#36}&&, nixl_status_t (*)(nixlAgent&, unsigned long), pybind11::name const&, pybind11::is_method const&, pybind11::sibling const&, pybind11::call_guard<pybind11::gil_scoped_release> const&)::{lambda(pybind11::detail::function_call&)#3}::_FUN(pybind11::detail::function_call&)

```

## Modifications

Always use `syncMode = NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT`.

title: fix(nightly-precision): pin flashinfer allreduce-fusion backend for TP-partial capture contract
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Problem

The nightly precision regression test (`test_nightly_precision_regression`, suite `nightly-precision-8-gpu-h200`) has been failing on `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` since 2026-06-17:

```
FAILED - tensor=non_intrusive__model.layers.8.inputs.1 rel_diff=0.7537
```

30/33 captured layers fail, all with `rel_diff` in `[0.7497, 0.7839]`. Only layer 0 passes.

## Root cause

Bisected to #23402 (`32685874f3`, "Reenable MNNVL backend for FlashInfer allreduce fusion"). That PR correctly dropped SM90 from the fusion auto-enable list (SM90 mnnvl needs an NVLink multicast fabric H200 nodes do not reliably have), changing the gate on H200 from `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion` (auto True for GLM-family) to `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend is not None` (None on H200).

The nightly serve flags pass no fusion flag, so fusion is now OFF where it used to be ON. This flips the dumper capture contract:

- fusion ON (#23402 before): the previous MLP layer skips `postprocess_layer` and tags the tensor for deferred allreduce, so the dumper pre-hook at the next layer entry captures a TP-partial sum (ranks differ).
- fusion OFF (#23402 after): the previous layer allreduces immediately, so the dumper captures an identical full sum on every rank.

The comparator compares with `--override-dims "...:bs h[tp:partial]"`, whose `tp:partial` is a ReduceSum (`torch.stack(ranks).sum(0)`). Summing 8 identical full-sum tensors yields 8x the baseline (partial-sum) magnitude — abs_mean 0.00556 -> 0.04443, exactly 8x — and `rel_diff = 1 - 16/65 = 0.7538`, matching the observed 0.7537.

Layer 0 passes because `inputs.1` of layer 0 is the embedding output, before any MLP allreduce.

## Fix

- Pin `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=trtllm` in the nightly serve flags so the dumper captures TP-partial sums again (the comparator contract). Explicit `trtllm`, not `auto`, because `auto` resolves to `mnnvl` on SM90 single-node.
- Include the fusion backend in the capture signature so a future change to the fusion default re-establishes the baseline (first run) instead of silently mismatching partial vs full tensors.

This is a test-infra capture-contract fix, not a forward-precision change: the model forward is unchanged, only which tensor (partial vs full) the dumper records. The fused H200 GLM path is what the existing baselines and comparator dims were built for.

## Verification

E2E on an H200 devbox (8xH200, TP8, main worktree, GLM-5.1-FP8):

- Served with the nightly flags + `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=trtllm`. Chat returned 200; dumper captured 1872 tensors (78 layers x 8 ranks x 3 steps).
- Ran the nightly comparator against the 2026-06-16 HF baseline (run-2dd449c, pre-#23402 partial-sum): **33/33 passed, max_rel_diff=0.000000** — bit-exact match. This confirms the fix restores the pre-#23402 capture contract (TP-partial), so the existing baseline is reusable.
- Causal chain confirmed: with the flag, `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend` resolves to `trtllm` and `apply_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion(bs)` returns `True`; without it, the backend is `None` and it returns `False`.
- Historical HF baseline data corroborates the regression: 2026-06-16 (pre-#23402) baseline layer 8 abs_mean=0.00556 (partial); 2026-06-17/22 target abs_mean=0.04443 = 8x, rel_diff=0.7537.
- `pre-commit` (black/isort/ruff/clang-format) passes; `py_compile` passes.

## Related

- #28190 fixes `_select_latest_run` to not promote failed runs to the comparison baseline. That bug caused 2026-06-20/21 to pass falsely (the 06-19 failed full-sum run became the baseline). It is independent of this fix but should land together so failed runs can no longer mask this class of regression.

title: [LoRA] BF16 support + EP cuda-graph crash fix for experimental_sgl_trtllm MoE-LoRA
author: jybsuper
body:
## Summary

Two changes on the `experimental_sgl_trtllm` MoE-LoRA fast path:

1. **BF16 support** for the path (previously FP8 / NVFP4 only), plus `experts_shared_outer` LoRA.
2. **Stability fixes** that make the path correct under expert parallelism (EP) + CUDA graph:
   - **NVFP4 (Kimi-K2.5):** fix an illegal-memory-access that crashed batched serving under CUDA graph with the two-stream overlap enabled.

## Testing

Hardware: **2 nodes × 8× GB300 (TP8 / EP8, MNNVL)**, flashinfer 0.6.12.

### Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 — the crash fix
`--moe-runner-backend experimental_sgl_trtllm`, two-stream overlap **on**, CUDA graph **on**, rank-16 adapter.

- **Before:** batched `bench_one_batch_server` crashes with an illegal memory access (TMA descriptor init) during prefill.
- **After:** no crash; greedy generation coherent across diverse prompts (adapter behavior preserved). Validated bs1 prefill (the minimal repro) through bs128.
- **End-to-end overall throughput** at `input = output = 2048`, vs the no-LoRA `flashinfer_trtllm` baseline:
