title: [DSV4] Fix silent KV corruption when speculative draft tokens > 4
author: hnyls2002
body:
Supersedes #33872.

## Motivation

The compress write plan decides which tokens' raw KV get persisted into the compress-state ring for a *future* compression window to read. A speculative verify batch plans from the optimistic `seq_len = prefix_len + num_draft_tokens` but rolls back to `prefix_len + accept_len`, so every committed token must stay resident whatever the accept length turns out to be.

`c_plan.cuh` capped that pad at a hard-coded 4:

```cpp
constexpr int32_t kMaxMTPDraftTokens = 4;
const auto mtp_pad = std::min(ring_size - compress_ratio, kMaxMTPDraftTokens);
```

With `--speculative-num-draft-tokens > 4` the plan under-writes the ring, and a later compression reads stale slots. This fails silently -- no illegal access, no NaN, no assertion, just wrong compressed state. The host planner path was additionally missing the pad term entirely, so the CPU and GPU planners disagreed.

## Modifications

**The pad is a property of the ring, not of the batch.** A write at `w` aliases onto `w - ring_size`, and the earliest position a future compression can still need is `prefix_len - window_size + 2` (the next batch commits at least one token, and `run_prefill` launches the compress kernel before the write kernel, so a batch's own compressions read the pre-write ring). So the ring's capacity is `ring_size - window_size + 2`, and the plan can simply always pad that far:

```cpp
const auto mtp_pad = ring_size > window_size ? ring_size - window_size + 2 : 0;
```

Padding past a batch's own extend range is harmless -- the planner loops only span `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. A non-speculative ring is exactly one window wide, so the pad is 0 there and the write set is unchanged.

All three planner paths (both `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` branches and the C++ host loop) now share this value, fixing the CPU/GPU divergence.

**Capacity is validated at startup.** `DSV4PoolConfigurator` rejects a draft count the ring cannot serve, using `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens` since the ring is sized once and must serve the largest adaptive tier. The planner itself cannot do this -- it cannot tell an over-configured verify batch from an ordinary long prefill -- so an over-configured server now fails at startup instead of corrupting state at run time.

The current rings serve `num_draft_tokens <= 10` for c4 and `<= 130` for c128. Raising the c4 bound means growing the ring, which scales the c4 state pool; that tradeoff is left out of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_deepseek_v4_compress_plan_draft_pad.py` (kernel, ~8s in CI):

- `test_c4_ring_residency` / `test_c128_ring_residency` -- for every draft count the ring serves, crossed with residues of `seq_len % compress_ratio`, assert `plan_w` covers all of `[prefix_len, seq_len)`. This is the sufficient condition: if each step writes its whole extend range, the next compression window is resident by induction whatever the accept length. Reverting the pad turns these red for `D > 4`.
- `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` -- pins `plan_compress_prefill_kernel0` to the host-loop plan, so the fix has to hold on both paths.
- `test_plain_prefill_write_set` -- non-speculative rings produce the pre-existing write set for both ratios, i.e. no change for non-speculative serving.
- `test_over_capacity_under_writes` -- past the ring capacity the plan silently under-writes, which is why the bound is enforced at startup rather than in the planner.

`test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (CPU unit, ~1s) covers the capacity helper: 0 without speculation, 10/130 for the speculative rings, and 0 for the online-c128 ring of 1.

### The kernel test fails on the pre-fix planner

A regression test that also passes on the buggy code proves nothing, so this was checked directly — running the test file above against the pre-fix planner gives **19 failures**:

| test | failing cases before the fix |
|---|---|
| `test_c4_ring_residency` | D = 5, 9, 10 (each across 4 residues of `seq_len % 4`) |
| `test_c128_ring_residency` | D = 129, 130 |
| `test_cpu_and_gpu_planner_agree` | compress_ratio=128, D=130 |

Two things worth calling out. c4 starts losing positions at **D=5**, exactly `D > kMaxMTPDraftTokens` — the boundary is sharp, which is why an `ndt` of 4 or 2 never sees it. And c128 only breaks near the ring's capacity: its `first_w_pos = min(last_c_pos, seq_len - pad)` usually takes `last_c_pos` (as `seq_len % 128` is typically much larger than the pad), which already reaches far enough back. The exposure is concentrated in the c4 layers.

The third row is a separate defect the pre-fix code also had: the C++ host loop carried no pad term at all, only the GPU kernel did, so the two planner paths emitted different write sets.

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSPARK at `--speculative-dspark-block-size 7` (D=8, past the old cap of 4), TP=4, `--moe-runner-backend marlin`; two servers launched identically apart from the checkout.

| | GSM8K (200) | GPQA diamond (198, 5 rounds) | latency | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.990 | 0.7172 | 65.1s | 354.8 tok/s |
| after | 0.985 | 0.7374 | 64.7s | 352.7 tok/s |

Plus an opaque-id echo probe (200 requests, 4000-token prefix, greedy): 200/200 exact on both.

**These numbers show no regression; they are not evidence the fix works.** GPQA leans positive (4 of 5 rounds, +0.02 mean) but is not significant — paired t = 2.0 at df=4, p ~ 0.12. At `temperature=0` over a fixed question set the five rounds should have been identical yet spanned ~4.5pp, so concurrent-batch nondeterminism puts the noise floor above the effect size.

That the fix is not visible end-to-end is expected. The skipped positions are the head of the draft tail, and consecutive verify batches have heavily overlapping write sets, so the next step usually rewrites what the previous one skipped. Corruption needs a position to stay unwritten until a compression actually reads it, which depends on accept-length distribution, sequence length, and compression-point alignment lining up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact expected. The change replaces a compile-time constant with an expression over values the planner already receives; no extra memory traffic, no new launches, no change to the compress kernels. A speculative verify batch writes more rows than before, which is the fix, bounded by the ring capacity.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). -- no user-facing flag or behavior change; the rationale lives in the `c_plan.cuh` comment and the test module docstring.

title: [Bugfix][DSA] Fix num_splits "(b+1)" crash on prefill-CP speculative decode
author: NVShreyas
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #30296. Running a DSA model (GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2) with `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave` together with EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding crashes at warmup:

```
RuntimeError: num_splits must have shape (b+1)
```

This is a `TORCH_CHECK` inside `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fwd_kvcache_mla`, which asserts `num_splits.shape[0] == q.shape[0] + 1`.

## Root cause

`cal_padded_tokens` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/utils.py`) sizes the FlashMLA `num_splits` metadata (via `pad_dsa_cache_seqlens` → `_compute_flashmla_metadata`) and must mirror `ForwardBatch.prepare_mlp_sync_batch`, which sizes `q`. `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` applies `cp_align_size` **only when CP-v2 is disabled**, but `cal_padded_tokens` applied it **unconditionally**.

On the speculative forwards (`TARGET_VERIFY` / `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2`), `enable_cp_v2()` is `True` while `is_cp_v2_active(forward_batch)` is `False` (those modes are not `context_parallel_extend`), so `cal_padded_tokens` falls through past the CP-v2 early-return and `q` is padded to `attn_tp_size` only. The unconditional `cp_align` then over-pads the metadata to a multiple of `attn_cp_size` while `q` is not, so `len(dsa_cache_seqlens_int32)` (= `num_splits.shape[0] - 1`) exceeds `q.shape[0]` whenever `num_draft_tokens * batch_size` isn't a multiple of `attn_cp_size` → the assert fires.

This is the `attn_cp` analog of the `attn_tp` alignment fix in #30642.

## Fix

Guard the `cp_align` loop in `cal_padded_tokens` with `if not enable_cp_v2()` so the DSA metadata padding matches `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` exactly. No numeric effect — it only removes phantom metadata rows that have no corresponding `q` rows (the padded entries are zeroed and their outputs discarded).

- Legacy CP (`enable_cp_v2()` False): `cp_align` still applied — unchanged.
- Plain prefill EXTEND under CP-v2: hits the `is_cp_v2_active` early-return — unchanged.
- Only the crashing `TARGET_VERIFY` / `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` spec forwards change: metadata length now equals `q.shape[0]`.

## Test

GLM-5-FP8, tp8/ep8, `--attention-backend dsa --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --moe-a2a-backend megamoe` + EAGLE speculative decoding now serves and handles requests (previously crashed deterministically at warmup, ~175s).

title: [ROCm] Fix QuickReduce fp16 saturation corrupting bf16 all-reduces (106M non-finite -> 0, +0.3%)
author: alexnails
body:
Fixes #34473.

## Summary

QuickReduce converts BF16 inputs to FP16 before reduction for performance. GPT-OSS reaches magnitudes above FP16's maximum finite value (65,504), so the conversion could produce `inf`; quantized codecs then propagated that value through a 32-element block.

This PR:

- Enables `MODE.FP16_OVFL` on both gfx942 and gfx950 so FP16 overflow clamps instead of becoming non-finite.
- Uses a power-of-two range guard (`S = 16`) for `CodecFP`, scaling in FP32 before narrowing and restoring the scale on output.
- Emits `v_cvt_pk_f16_f32` explicitly for the scaled `CodecFP` conversion. This prevents LLVM from moving the FP16 conversion ahead of the scale.
- Keeps `CodecQ4/Q6/Q8` at `S = 1` on the existing fast FP16 path. Their block scaling already normalizes values, and a larger cast scale moves the reciprocal-scale saturation cliff into real data.
- Adds a four-GPU regression test covering low values, ordinary values, sums above FP16 range, individual inputs above FP16 range, negative overflow, and mixed blocks.

## Scope

This fixes the GPT-OSS non-finite-output failure without routing quantized codecs through native BF16 kernels. Quantized reductions may still clamp finite values when their FP16 accumulator exceeds 65,504; that is pre-existing lossy behavior and is intentionally left unchanged here. The native-BF16 alternative was numerically exact but 22–46% slower.

## Validation

- Built and passed the TP4 range regression on MI350X and MI355X with ROCm 7.2.
- `CodecFP` is bit-exact for all tested cases, including inputs and sums above FP16 range.
- Quantized codecs remain bit-exact for low and ordinary values and produce finite outputs for overflow cases.
- Captured GPT-OSS reductions went from non-finite outputs to zero non-finite outputs.
- PR-base versus final-patch latency on MI350X showed no measurable regression:
  - INT8/INT6/INT4: within 0.4% at 16 MiB and within 0.1% at 90 MiB.
  - FP: 9.6% faster at 16 MiB and 1.1% faster at 90 MiB in this run.
- Repository pre-commit checks pass.

## Test plan

- [x] Build the ROCm AOT extension on gfx950.

title: [Fix] hybrid-SSM: DP attention failures at low concurrency
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

Two failures hit a hybrid-SSM (Nemotron-H) deployment running DP attention over a
concurrency sweep (`--tp 4 --ep 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention`, one server per
concurrency level, `--max-running-requests` set to the concurrency).

**1. `--max-running-requests` smaller than `attn_dp_size` gives every worker zero slots.**

The per-DP-worker share `max_running_requests // attn_dp_size` floors to `0`
(e.g. `1 // 4`), so the server fails to launch. On hybrid models it surfaces as a
misleading mamba error, even though the mamba pool has plenty of slots
(`348 // 5 = 69` available, `0` requested):

```
RuntimeError: Hybrid (mamba/linear-attention) state cache is too small to serve any
requests. max_mamba_cache_size=348, mamba_ratio=5, resulting max_num_reqs=0.
```

**2. A decoding rank relabeled as a 1-token extend crashes on a mamba track boundary.**

For hybrid-SSM models `DpPaddingMode.get_dp_padding_mode` forces `MAX_LEN` as soon as
any DP rank is idle while another extends, and `ForwardBatch.prepare_mlp_sync_batch`
then relabels a decoding rank as `EXTEND`, padding each row to a 1-token extend so
every rank presents one shape to the collectives. The rows are still decode rows, but
the mamba metadata reads the label and builds prefill metadata for them. On a step
where one of those rows sits on a `--mamba-track-interval` boundary, the decode
batch's `mamba_track_mask` is set while `mamba_track_seqlens` — populated only by
`prepare_for_extend` — is `None`, and the scheduler dies (traceback from the
`cae69be584` run):

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 297, in _forward_metadata
  File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 399, in _init_track_conv_indices
    assert aligned_len is not None, (
AssertionError: conv-state tracking requires mamba_track_seqlens and extend_prefix_lens; this path should only run when the track mask is set on an extend batch
```

With only fix 1 applied, one DP scheduler died this way at every sweep point from
concurrency 64 up (see Testing).

By code inspection, the same relabel also sends the KDA gate preprocessing in
`kimi_linear` / `kimi_k3` down the prefill branch, handing the decode kernel a
`[1, T, H, K]` forget gate and a pre-sigmoided beta, and makes `qwen3_5` build the
strided GDN input views meant for prefill and hand them to the decode kernels.

## Modifications

**1. Per-worker request split** — floor every per-DP-worker split of the global
`--max-running-requests` at 1. Requests are load balanced across workers, so a worker
with 0 slots can never serve anything. The division itself stays floored, so every
consumer keeps sizing from the same per-worker count:

- `KVCacheConfigurator`: the request pool, the mamba pools (including the
  `disable_radix_cache` path, which produced 0-sized pools), the spec-decoding
  intermediate buffers and the GDN ReplaySSM ring reserve
- `compute_swa_request_cap` and `DSV4PoolConfigurator`
- the PD decode in-transfer reserve (`pd_disaggregation_hook`)
- the LoRA MoE CUDA graph buffers
- the MLX resolver, which returned 0 unchecked outside its hybrid branch

**2. `ForwardBatch.logical_forward_mode`** — a new property that reads back through
the decode→extend relabel.
The relabel only decouples tokens from rows for the DP collectives, so the consumers
that need the decode semantics behind the label read it instead of `forward_mode`:

- `Mamba2Metadata.prepare_mixed` builds decode metadata for relabeled rows
- `MambaAttnBackendBase._forward_metadata` builds the decode-side linear-attention
  metadata, and `HybridLinearAttnBackend.forward` dispatches linear layers to decode
- the KDA gate preprocessing in `kimi_linear` and `kimi_k3`
- the GDN input layout in `qwen3_5`, which uses the strided prefill views only for
  real extends

Full attention still runs the 1-token extend; only the state-carrying side is routed
back to decode.

## Testing

Unit tests (CPU), run on the rebased branch:
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py::TestPdDecodeExtraSlots`:
  the PD decode in-transfer reserve keeps headroom when the cap is below the DP size.
- `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py::TestPerWorkerRequestSplit`:
  with `--max-running-requests 1` on 4 attention DP workers, `resolve_max_num_reqs`
  returns 1 (was 0) and the SWA chunk cap sizes one request (was 0 tokens).
- `test/registered/unit/layers/test_mamba_prefill_track_metadata.py::TestDpDecodeRelabel`:
  a relabeled decode batch on a track boundary goes through
  `MambaAttnBackendBase._forward_metadata` as decode (was the `AssertionError` above);
  `Mamba2Metadata.prepare_mixed` builds decode metadata for relabeled rows and keeps
  real extends as prefills; idle-rank relabels are not read back as decode.

The regression cases in `TestPerWorkerRequestSplit` and `TestDpDecodeRelabel` each
fail with their fix reverted and pass with it.

The end-to-end results below were measured on one node with 4x NVIDIA GB300, with
both fixes on `cae69be584`, before the rebase onto `f3fe753475`. The rebase only
re-applied the per-worker floor where upstream renamed the divisor
(`pd_disaggregation_hook`, the MLX resolver). Nemotron-H has no GDN layers, so these
runs do not exercise the `qwen3_5` layout change.

Server cmd:
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 \
--trust-remote-code \
--tp 4 \
--ep 4 \
--dp 4 \
--enable-dp-attention \
--max-running-requests $CONCURRENCY \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
--attention-backend trtllm_mha \
--mamba-backend flashinfer \
--mamba-ssm-dtype float16 \

--reasoning-parser nemotron_3 \
--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \
--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 16}'
```
On the current base, `--dp 4 --enable-dp-attention` is spelled `--attn-dp-size 4` (#41818).

Accuracy (`--max-running-requests 64`):
```
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
--model_args base_url=http://127.0.0.1:18000/v1/completions,model=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=64

|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9386|±  |0.0066|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9356|±  |0.0068|
```

Benchmark cmd, one server and one run per concurrency point (shown for 64):
```
CONCURRENCY=64
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
--model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 \

The numbers below were collected with InferenceX's `benchmark_serving.py` using the
same settings (`--backend vllm --use-chat-template`, EOS ignored); the command above
is the `sglang.benchmark.serving` equivalent.

Before:
- without either fix, concurrency 1 fails to launch (issue 1);
- with fix 1 only, a DP scheduler crashes on issue 2 at every point from concurrency

After, the sweep completes with every request served:

title: [Fix] Fix Nemotron-H Mamba illegal memory access under DP attention with CUDA graph
author: elvischenv
body:
## Motivation

Running Nemotron-H with DP attention enabled together with a CUDA-graph runner backend (breakable CUDA graph / torch.compile piecewise) crashes at graph replay.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/nemotron_h.py`: in the `is_dp_attention_enabled()` branch of `NemotronHMambaDecoderLayer.forward`, route the mixer through the same split-op dispatch already used by the non-DP path:

- `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()` → `breakable_nemotron_mamba2_with_output(hidden_states, output, self.layer_id, False)`
- `is_in_tc_piecewise_cuda_graph()` → `nemotron_mamba2_with_output(hidden_states, output, self.layer_id, False)`
- otherwise → `self._forward_mamba(hidden_states, forward_batch)` (unchanged eager path)

`fuse_mlp_allreduce` is passed as `False` on the DP path, matching the existing behavior there (the DP path does not compute `fuse_mlp_allreduce`; the allreduce is handled by the layer communicator).

title: fix: restore VLM nightly regression coverage
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- keep single-node CUDA IPC multimodal feature transport opt-in
- preserve automatic CUDA VMM selection for validated multi-node MNNVL deployments
- refresh VLM MMMU accuracy and latency baselines for the 1024-token CoT evaluation budget

## Root cause

PR #27327 increased the MMMU CoT generation budget from 30 to 1024 tokens, but the latency thresholds still described the old 30-token workload. Nightly results moved to a new stable latency plateau immediately after that change, so the old thresholds no longer measured engine regressions.

Pixtral's score has ranged from 0.33 to 0.37 on the fixed 100-sample suite since that change. A 0.36 floor therefore flakes on normal one- or two-question variation; this PR uses 0.32 as the regression floor.

GLM-4.5V-FP8 also had a separate real regression after single-node CUDA IPC became the default. Its fixed 1 GiB feature pool reduced the GLM nightly KV cache from 25,998 to 14,088 tokens, reducing output throughput from about 687 to 549 tokens/s and increasing latency from about 107 to 131 seconds. The latest run reached 148 seconds. Restoring CPU as the single-node default recovers the KV-cache headroom while keeping CUDA IPC available through `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc`.

The GLM latency threshold is calibrated to the pre-regression 100-119 second plateau with headroom at 140 seconds, so a 208-second result still fails.

## Validation

- all changed-file pre-commit hooks pass
- Python byte compilation passes
- `git diff --check` passes
- targeted unit-test collection is blocked on the local macOS environment because its Transformers build lacks `transformers.image_processing_backends`; Linux/H100 CI is required for runtime validation

title: fix(test): stabilize nightly precision regression
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Root cause

[`test_nightly_precision_regression`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31501558607/job/94072436800) failed for `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` with TP=8 for two independent harness reasons:

1. The test skipped the remote restore when a self-hosted runner already had `.pt` files under `/tmp/sglang_precision_baselines`. A stale baseline captured replicated layer-entry tensors after FlashInfer fusion failed to initialize, while the target contained TP-partial tensors. Treating both as partial produced the approximately 8x mismatch. The historical initialization failure is tracked by [FlashInfer #3676](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3676) and [SGLang #30875](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30875), and was mitigated by [SGLang #30580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30580).
2. After a clean fused refresh, the comparator still observed rank-local BF16 buffers before fused all-reduce and residual RMSNorm. CPU-side reduction of those buffers is not the kernel's semantic output and drifted across runners.

Current H200 runs initialize TRTLLM fusion on all eight ranks. This PR keeps fusion enabled and moves the comparison to `self_attn.inputs.hidden_states`, the replicated value consumed by attention after `prepare_attn()`.

## Fix

- Always restore a signature-compatible remote baseline, atomically replace local tensors, and include the capture filters, TP size, and fusion backend in the signature.
- Compare only the replicated post-fusion attention input. Keep layer-entry captures only as a per-layer/step/rank guard that rejects fusion fallback.
- Make ordinary `/rerun-test` read-only. Add a maintainer-only, in-repo H200 refresh path:
  `/rerun-test --refresh-precision-baseline test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py`.

Serving runtime and all-reduce implementation code are unchanged.

## Verification

- [Cross-runner Nightly comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31862539092): passed all 33 post-fusion records with `max_rel_diff=0.0`.
- [Cleanup-head baseline refresh](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31893911079): fusion initialized on all eight ranks and the guarded refresh passed.
- [Cleanup-head read-only comparator](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31894139007): restored the refreshed baseline, passed a non-empty comparison, and did not publish.
- All 42 baseline-store unit tests and changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-forward changes. The registered 8-GPU H200 test exercises the actual fused path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; serving performance is unchanged.

title: [DSpark] Fix EP1 decode performance regression
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

#33465 made `DraftBlockProposer` construct a CUDA `int32` scalar on every speculative decoding step.

`num_token_non_padded` is only consumed when `enable_num_token_non_padded()` is true. For MoE EP size 1, the predicate is false, so the device allocation is unused.

## Modifications

- Return `None` instead of constructing the device scalar when token padding is disabled.
- Preserve the existing `int32` device scalar when token padding is enabled.
- Add unit coverage for both paths.

This does not change model arithmetic. The focused test verifies:

- The disabled path returns `None`.
- The enabled path preserves the existing scalar value and `torch.int32` dtype.

uv run --no-project python test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_dp_tier.py

title: [Fix] has_hf_quant_config crashes on local dirs without the config
author: gilfordting
body:
## Motivation

`has_hf_quant_config()` crashes on any **local model directory that does not contain `hf_quant_config.json`**, killing the scheduler at init.

The current code checks the positive local case first (`os.path.exists(<model_path>/hf_quant_config.json)` → `True`), but when the file is absent it falls through to `huggingface_hub.try_to_load_from_cache(model_path, ...)`, which validates its first argument as a hub repo id and raises `HFValidationError` on filesystem paths (e.g. `/models/my-draft/`). The exception escapes outside any handler.

The function can therefore say "yes" for a local directory but never "no" — it crashes instead. In practice this is hit by any **local-directory speculative draft model paired with a quantized target** (draft checkpoints don't ship `hf_quant_config.json`), which is how we found it while serving a NVFP4 target with a local draft.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: decide local paths entirely on the filesystem — if `os.path.isdir(model_path)`, return `os.path.isfile(<model_path>/hf_quant_config.json)`; only genuine repo-id strings reach the hub helpers. Behavior for hub repo ids and for local dirs containing the config is unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`: three CPU-only regression tests — local dir with config → `True`; local dir without config → `False` (previously raised); local dirs never invoke `try_to_load_from_cache`. The latter two fail on current main and pass with this fix.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — control-flow fix in a config-detection helper; no model-output changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Local directories now take one `isdir`/`isfile` pair instead of an exception-raising hub call.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix critical Ascend NPU Diffusion regression/bugs & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
author: OrangeRedeng
body:
## Motivation

Restore Ascend/NPU packed Ring Attention, 2-NPU diffusion CI suite, fix NPU correctness, runtime, and CI regressions exposed by recent Ring, SRT-CLIP, residency, and MOVA changes.

After [#35004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35004), diffusion can import SRT CLIP code and execute SRT `init_npu_backend()`. Importing `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` inside a native NPU diffusion process globally rewrites CUDA-facing APIs/device arguments and can alter runtime feature detection and kernel selection. `allow_internal_format=True` is also known to regress unquantized diffusion performance; the earlier Wan regression in [#20533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20533), fixed by [#20684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20684), increased `DecodingStage` from **6.1889 s to 11.76 s (+90.0%, 1.90x slower)**.

The packed-attention implementation is extracted from the Ascend work in [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569).

## Modifications

- **Packed varlen / Ring Attention.** [#33327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33327) extended Qwen to tail-padded Ring and fixed `u=1, r>1` replicated-token semantics, exposing the shared packed `flash_attn_varlen_func` path on NPU. Add an Ascend implementation backed by `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (`TND`) with independent Q/K packed lengths, boundary validation, empty/non-contiguous handling, LSE normalization, and `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. Unsupported FlashAttention options fail explicitly.

- **Diffusion NPU runtime isolation.** Keep the SRT CUDA-compatibility layer out of diffusion: when `sglang.multimodal_gen` is loaded, do not import `torch_npu.contrib.transfer_to_npu` and do not enable `torch_npu.npu.config.allow_internal_format`. Preserve the existing `torch.cuda.is_available=False` re-mock on the SRT path after `transfer_to_npu`. `jit_compile=False` remains unchanged.

- **MOVA 2-NPU correctness.** [#31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453) left a contiguous-layout assumption after attention. Multi-NPU attention may return a non-contiguous tensor, so use `reshape()` instead of `view()`.

- **Host-memory accounting.** [#35641](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35641) introduced storage-based module sizing for host-memory budgeting. Skip tensors whose storage access raises `RuntimeError` instead of failing memory planning; add focused unit coverage.

- **NPU CI / GT.**
  - Restore the 2-NPU diffusion suite on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16`.
  - Split both 1-NPU and 2-NPU suites into two partitions.
  - Run GT generation on the A3-800T runner families.
  - Make GT jobs check out the requested `workflow_dispatch` ref.
  - Retry transient HTTP/image-decoding failures while downloading GT.
  - Update the NPU GT revision to `8e3d717e65fb87339c2974382a092a731669f884`.

- **NPU dependencies.** Pin `sgl-kernel-npu` to `2026.8.13` and install the packaged `attentions` wheel in NPU CI/Docker; update release Docker pins accordingly.

- **Performance baselines.** Refresh affected FLUX.2 text-encoding, ERNIE timestep-preparation, and LTX-2 connector/decoding baselines plus partition-duration estimates for the current A3-800T / auto-residency environment. Related residency policy: [#34615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34615). These are CI baseline updates, not algorithmic speedups.

## Accuracy Tests

- NPU diffusion GT was regenerated successfully after the Ring semantic changes and A3-800T CI migration: [Generate Diffusion CI Ground Truth #32478548704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32478548704).
- Qwen Ring keeps the corrected semantics from #33327; no consistency thresholds are relaxed.
- Runtime isolation changes backend initialization/dispatch only; #20684 reported no accuracy impact from disabling the problematic internal-format behavior.
- The restored 2-NPU suite exercises the packed Ring path.
- Invalid-storage host-memory handling has dedicated unit coverage.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The runtime fix prevents diffusion from inheriting SRT's global CUDA-compatibility monkey patches and `allow_internal_format=True`.

title: [Quantization] Fix GPTQ scheme attachment broken by LinearBase.scheme default

body:
## Summary

#29328 added a class-level `scheme = None` to `LinearBase`, turning GPTQ's `if not hasattr(layer, "scheme")` guard into a no-op — the scheme never gets built and every GPTQ checkpoint dies on load with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'create_weights'`. title: [diffusion] Fix width/height silently dropped on multipart /v1/videos requests
author: zetyquickly
body:
## Summary
- `create_video()` declares explicit `Form(...)` parameters for `seconds`, `size`, `fps`, `num_frames`, `seed`, etc., but not for `width`/`height`. Because those two names are already declared fields on `VideoGenerationsRequest`, the generic "extra form field" fallback explicitly excludes already-declared fields, so a multipart request's `width`/`height` are never read — the pipeline's `SamplingParams` subclass default silently wins instead.
- Fix: add `width`/`height` as explicit `Form(None)` parameters, threaded through the same `form_value()` precedence already used for `fps`/`num_frames`.
- Not model-specific: any multipart `/v1/videos` request with explicit `width`/`height` hits this, for any model (surfaced here while building an image-to-video client against LTX-2.5, #35107). The JSON body path was already unaffected.

## Test plan
- [x] Before: multipart request for `width=704&height=512` produced a `960x544` video (LTX25SamplingParams' hardcoded default), confirmed via `ffprobe` on the actual output.
- [x] After: same request produces `704x512` output, confirmed via `ffprobe`.
- [x] JSON body path re-verified unaffected (worked before and after).

title: Fix: abort handling for dispatched requests after client disconnect
author: Dovis01
body:
## Summary

  This PR fixes an issue where a request could continue decoding after the client disconnected, wasting GPU resources and repeatedly logging:

```text
  Received output for rid=... but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
```

## Root Cause

When a request handler was cancelled after dispatch, TokenizerManager removed its `rid_to_state` entry immediately. The disconnect abort path checks this state before sending an AbortReq, so the abort was skipped while the request continued running in the scheduler.

 A related race also existed for chunked-prefill requests: if a request moved out of the chunked-prefill slot before its deferred abort was processed, the abort could be lost.

 ## Changes
  - Track whether each request has been dispatched to the scheduler.
  - Remove undelivered request states locally on handler failure.
  - Abort dispatched requests and retain their state until scheduler cleanup completes.
  - Deduplicate abort requests and abort metrics.
  - Preserve retry behavior when abort dispatch fails.
  - Track generated request IDs used by parallel sampling.
  - Retry deferred chunked-prefill aborts after a request moves to another scheduler queue.
  - Add regression tests for disconnect cleanup, abort deduplication, dispatch failures, parallel sampling, and chunked-prefill transitions.

## Original commits

- `f9ad78ba2471abbc9a55ff4b4b1f3fa88a798a9e`

title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
author: Deleter-D
body:
## Motivation

Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled:
1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549)
2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay.
3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`.

## Modifications
1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.)
2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why.
3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe.

Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease.

## Accuracy Tests

Server launched following the cookbook:

```bash
sglang serve \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp 4 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    --speculative-adaptive \
    --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000
```

Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook:

|          | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k |
| -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- |
| cookbook | 88.1         | 95     | 96.13 |
| before   | 88.13        | 98.33  | 96.89 |
| after    | 88.04          | 97.29  | 96.97 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache.

title: fix(disagg): PD transfer-failure injection was silently inert
author: ShangmingCai
body:
## Motivation

PD transfer-failure injection has been silently inert. `_get_failure_prob()` in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py` guarded the canonical env read with a `try/except` and fell back to a legacy `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB` name:

```python
def _get_failure_prob() -> float:
    try:
        return float(envs.SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_FAILURE_PROB.get())
    except Exception:
        # fallback to legacy env var
        return float(os.getenv("DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB", "0"))
```

But `EnvField.get()` never raises. An unset variable returns the default (`0.0`), and even an unparseable value only warns and returns the default. So the `except` branch is unreachable and the legacy name was ignored outright — with `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB=0.05` set, `_get_failure_prob()` returns `0.0`.

Two registered CI tests set exactly that variable to exercise PD transfer-failure recovery, so **both have been running with zero failure injection and their retry-path assertions have been passing vacuously**:

- `test/registered/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py`
- `test/registered/amd/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py`

## Modifications

4 files, +13 / -17. `environ.py` is deliberately untouched.

- Both failure tests now set the canonical `SGLANG_TEST_DISAGG_FAILURE_PROB` via `envs.<...>.override()` instead of mutating `os.environ`, per the env-var conventions. The override is entered before the servers launch so the subprocesses inherit it.
- The legacy name is **dropped**, not preserved behind a deprecation alias. It is a test-only knob and it has never functioned, so nothing that works today can regress: no in-repo caller sets it after this change, and any out-of-tree user setting it was already silently getting `0.0`.
- Dropping it removes the dead `try/except`, which leaves `_get_failure_prob` as a one-line wrapper over a descriptor read — so it is inlined into its single caller and deleted. `utils.py` loses its last use of `os` as a result.
- Also drops the matching legacy `os.environ.pop` from the nixl test's defensive clear, which would otherwise be a no-op naming a variable the codebase no longer honors.

After this change `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB` appears nowhere in the repo.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — no model output, kernel, or forward path is touched. The affected code is a test-only failure-injection knob.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The read gets marginally cheaper: one descriptor access inline, instead of a function call wrapping a `try/except` around the same access.

## Verification performed

**The bug was reproduced against this PR's base commit.** With `DISAGGREGATION_TEST_FAILURE_PROB=0.05` and the pre-change `_get_failure_prob()`, the result is `0.0`.

**The fix was then verified end-to-end** by executing the post-change `_poll_with_failure_injection` against 4000 pollers:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| no env set | no injection |
| legacy name set | no injection — unchanged, it was already broken |
| `override(0.05)` (what the tests now do) | **4.78% injection** (191/4000) |
| after the override context exits | injection stops |

The third row is the one that matters: it confirms the tests' new idiom actually reaches the injection path and produces the intended ~5% failure rate, which is precisely what was not happening before. The second row confirms removing the legacy name changes nothing for anyone — it was a no-op before and is a no-op now.

Also: pinned `ruff 0.15.1 --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit config) passes, plus pinned `black 26.1.0` and `isort 7.0.0`. Import survival checked in each touched test file.

The two PD tests themselves were **not** run locally — they need multi-GPU hardware.

## NOTE FOR REVIEWERS

These two tests will now genuinely inject 5% transfer failures for the first time. If the transfer-recovery path has regressed during the period when injection was inert, they may start failing. **That would be a real pre-existing defect surfacing, not a regression introduced by this PR** — and arguably the point of fixing the injection.

Part of a series of disaggregation cleanups; this is the only one that changes runtime behavior. Related: #35838, #35843, #35844, #35847, #35886.

## Motivation

### 1. Fix evalscope accuracy parsing in `python/sglang/test/ascend/e2e/test_npu_accuracy_utils.py`

evalscope 1.11+ reports accuracy as a percentage (e.g. `66.67%`), which was not matched by the existing regex patterns and was not normalized against the baseline.

### 2. Add request timeout to glm5\_1 aime26 test in `test/registered/npu/accuracy/glm5_1/test_npu_glm5_1_w4a8_1p1d_32p_in64k_out1k_50ms_aime26.py`

title: [Fix] Re-encode multimodal embeddings after cache mismatch
author: mickqian
body:
## Motivation

based on #32404

 
A compact multimodal feature-hash collision can return a cached embedding whose token count does not match the placeholder span in the request. The mismatch currently reaches `_adjust_embedding_length` and aborts prefill with `Insufficient multimodal embedding length`.

## Modifications

- Validate cached embedding token counts against the item offsets on all chunked-prefill cache-hit paths.
- Evict malformed entries and re-encode them instead of passing them to the scheduler.
- Include `(hash, token_count)` in the per-batch temporary map so colliding items with different placeholder lengths are not deduplicated.
- Add regression coverage for full, per-item, and batched cache paths.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/mm_schedule.py test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py`

title: [Kernel] Fix SM90 FP8 decode regression with benchmarked M/K/N routing
author: RunFMe
body:
## Motivation

The SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 selector introduced by #34318 can route decode GEMMs to `torch._scaled_mm` based on K/N alone. The [reported H100 W8A8 regression](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34318#issuecomment-5461656173) is:

- model: `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic`
- test: `test/registered/quant/test_w8a8_quantization.py::TestW8A8Fp8.test_throughput`
- batch size: 1
- throughput: approximately 215 tok/s before #34318, approximately 190 tok/s after it
- affected down projection: `M=1, K=14336, N=4096`

Direct profiling of that shape on both H200 and H100 showed that the AOT kernel is substantially faster at decode M, even though K and N are large.

## Modifications

Constrain Torch/NVJet routing to the benchmarked large-prefill envelope (doing m >= 6144 is not really worth the gain from my measurements):

```python
m >= 8192 and (
    (k >= 4096 and n >= 6144) or
    (k >= 7168 and n >= 5376)
)
```

This keeps the following on AOT:

- all decode and small-prefill calls with `M < 8192`
- the reported `K=14336, N=4096` Llama down projection
- narrow TP8 projections `K=5376, N=3584` and `K=3584, N=5376`
- shapes outside the measured projection envelope

Torch remains selected for stable large-prefill wins: wide QKV/gate/up projections and broad down projections.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Common software:

- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 (`70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45`)
- CUDA 13.0
- `sgl_kernel==0.4.4`
- CUDA-event timing with randomized/interleaved AOT and Torch samples

The broad grid used 11 projection families and 12 M values (132 cases): 1, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192, 8320, 12288, and 16384. Percentages below are Torch speedups over AOT.

### H200 (SM90)

Protocol:

- broad grid: 5 warmups and 15 samples per arm
- two randomized boundary confirmations: 44 cases and 33 cases, with 8–10 warmups and 30–40 samples per arm
- exact-workload conditioning before timing

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 26.50 µs | 51.12 µs | AOT is 1.93× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 1.74% | 3.30% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 0.94% | 2.14% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 2.59% | 4.64% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 2.39% | 5.17% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 2.91% | 2.62% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 1.26% | 3.29% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 1.82% | 3.25% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 1.66% | 3.09% |

Across the H200 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 2.50%, with a measured range of 0.17–5.97%. Two independent randomized boundary passes added 48 repeated routed measurements, all of which also favored Torch.

### H100 80 GB HBM3 (SM90)

Protocol:

- randomized broad grid: 5 warmups and 20 samples per arm after 0.5 s of exact-workload conditioning per case
- randomized boundary confirmation: 44 cases, with 10 warmups and 40 samples per arm after 2 s of conditioning per case

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 32.19 µs | 53.55 µs | AOT is 1.66× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K | N | Projection family | M=8192 | M=8320 |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 28672 | gate/up | 21.02% | 43.21% |
| 4096 | 6144 | QKV | 5.39% | 3.07% |
| 5376 | 21504 | QKV | 25.44% | 57.38% |
| 5376 | 28672 | gate/up | 26.58% | 52.16% |
| 5376 | 14336 | gate/up TP2 | 15.87% | 48.31% |
| 7168 | 5376 | down TP4 | 2.72% | 4.43% |
| 14336 | 5376 | down TP2 | 8.72% | 7.08% |
| 28672 | 5376 | down TP1 | 10.02% | 8.57% |

Across the H100 broad grid, every one of the 32 measurements selected by the new predicate favored Torch. Their median speedup was 19.48%, with a measured range of 1.36–56.53%. The stronger randomized boundary pass added 24 repeated routed measurements, all favoring Torch, with a 21.02% median and a 2.72–57.38% range.

On both GPUs, the excluded Llama down and narrow TP8 families had weak large-M results that were near parity or changed sign across passes, so this change deliberately leaves them on AOT rather than routing on noise.

title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
author: xiaobochen-amd
body:
## Problem

EAGLE spec-decode verify has been committing `argmax` on ROCm, ignoring
`temperature` and `top_p` entirely, with nothing in the log saying so. At
`temp > 0` it degenerates into repetition loops.

The cause is one line in `eagle_sample`:

```python
if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu:
    target_predict = torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
```

`_is_hip` sits next to `is_all_greedy`, so HIP takes the greedy path
unconditionally. It is there because the sampling branch needs
`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob` and
`top_p_renorm_prob`, all of which are CUDA/MUSA-only in `sgl_kernel`.

## Fix

Route HIP through the pure-Triton chain sampler in `reject_sampling.py` when
rejection sampling is active and the batch is not all-greedy, with a Triton
renorm (`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip`) standing in for the CUDA-only renorm ops.

The gate becomes a pure helper, `_verify_uses_greedy`. On every non-HIP platform
it reduces to the predicate it replaces: with `is_hip` False the added term drops
out and the expression is the original one.

`_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip` follows the same shape as the op it replaces — a
threshold search, matching `top_p_renorm_prob`'s ternary pivot search on
`f(x) = sum(probs[probs > x])` — so it agrees with CUDA rather than with a
sort-based nucleus. `top_p >= 1.0` short-circuits to an exact pass-through, to
stay bit-exact with CUDA's `top_p_renorm_prob(p, 1.0) == p`. top-k uses a sort,
skipped entirely when no row restricts it.

Defaulting the flag on matters: without it the fix only reaches users who pass
`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, and everyone else still silently gets
argmax verify. It flips only on HIP, for EAGLE/EAGLE3 with `topk=1`, default
accept thresholds and non-deterministic inference — the same conditions the
validation below raises on, so the flip can never turn a working config into an
error. Setting it also makes the draft worker emit the target-vocab proposal
(`draft_probs`) the Triton chain sampler consumes.

## Two shapes that come from the current tree, not from the fix

Worth pointing out so they don't read as gratuitous:

**`sampling_fn` dispatch.** It used the eager `A if cond else B` form, which
resolves `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` whether or not that branch is
taken. HIP must not import it at all, so the dispatch becomes an `if`/`else`
that imports inside the arm needing it. Non-HIP behaviour is unchanged.

**One `cfg` read becomes `resolved_view`.** `_handle_eagle_family` writes through
`declare_resolution`, whose contract is that a field it decides is *not* visible
to a later `cfg.` read. The rejection-sampling validation immediately below was
reading `cfg`, so it would have skipped every auto-enabled config — including its
own "rejection sampling is enabled" log. That read becomes
`resolved_view(server_args)`, which is what the `declare_resolution` docstring
prescribes for exactly this case.

## Test

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py` — gate truth table, CPU.
  Pins that the helper reduces to the original predicate off HIP, and that HIP
  only leaves greedy when rejection sampling is on and the batch is not
  all-greedy. 4 tests.
- `test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py` — renorm numerical
  equivalence against an independent torch reference, plus the `top_p == 1.0`
  exact-no-op and `top_p -> 0` edges. Registered for both CUDA and AMD runners;
  the kernel is device-agnostic. 5 tests.

`ruff`, `isort` and `black` clean.

title: [Scheduler] Make request-timeout aborts rank-consistent to fix TP collective hangs
author: nogumanov
body:
## Problem

`SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT` / `SGLANG_REQ_RUNNING_TIMEOUT` are enforced by a
wall-clock scan that runs independently on every TP rank. A request sitting at
the timeout boundary gets aborted on whichever rank's clock crosses the
deadline first (sub-millisecond skew), so the waiting-queue composition
diverges across ranks, the extend-vs-decode admission decision splits, ranks
enter mismatched collectives, and the server hangs until the detokenizer
heartbeat health check kills it.

Repro conditions: TP > 1, timeout enabled, queue waits longer than the timeout
(long-context traffic under saturation). We hit it reliably on GLM NVFP4,
B200 TP4, 60k-300k token prompts, `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT=45`.

Evidence from per-rank scheduler tracing (identical recv/token/kv state on all
ranks up to the divergence): one run split 2+2 (two ranks admitted a chunked
prefill, two stayed in decode), another split 1+3 — in both, one rank had
dropped a timed-out request from its queue one iteration earlier than the
others. Setting the timeout to 0 on the same image eliminated the hang; with
this fix and the timeout re-enabled we saw 0 hangs over 21.6h of saturated
long-context benchmarks (vs. reproducible hangs within 16-90 min before).

## Fix

- The timeout scan runs only on the request-pulling rank
  (`Scheduler._poll_timeout_aborts`, invoked from
  `SchedulerRequestReceiver.recv_requests` before
  `_broadcast_reqs_across_ranks`). It only emits `AbortReq`s — no local
  deletion.
- The emitted `AbortReq`s join the recv stream and ride the existing
  broadcast, so every rank removes the same requests in the same scheduler
  iteration through the deterministic `abort_request()` path (waiting queue:
  pop; running batch: `to_finish`). No new collectives.
- `abort_request()` now propagates the initiator's `finished_reason` /
  `abort_message`, so clients still receive
  503 "Request waiting/running timeout reached." (previously the reason was
  dropped on the waiting-queue echo path).

## Notes

- Timeout semantics and env defaults are unchanged; only the enforcement
  mechanism moved.
- Routing through `abort_request()` also picks up its fuller cleanup
  (disaggregation KV / metadata / beam retire) that the old per-rank scan
  skipped.
- With PP > 1 the injected aborts follow the same path as tokenizer-initiated
  `AbortReq`s; tested on pp_size=1 only.
- Unit tests adapted: `test_scheduler_timeouts.py` now drives
  `_poll_timeout_aborts` (plus a dedup case for a request present in both
  running and last batch).

title: fix: resolve remaining GLM-5.3 rebase regressions
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes for deterministic CI regressions found after #37235 was merged into #36507:

- honor Helion KDA prefill `beta_is_raw` and cover the raw-beta contract
- make GLM5 hybrid-config detection tolerate minimal and non-GLM fixtures
- update the DSA CP unit test for the generalized DCP LSE helper name
- align adaptive-spec expectations with the current GLM-5.3 defaults
- restore plan-stream handoff initialization and verify-event publication for Frozen-KV MTP

The fused sigmoid-gating split-grid fix originally carried here is now present in the base branch through #37250, so it no longer appears in this PR diff.

## Root causes

- Helion KDA accepted `beta_is_raw` only through `**kwargs`, silently ignoring it.
- `glm5_next_config` assumed every model/config fixture exposed `model_type` and `is_draft_model`.
- Tests retained a private helper name and GLM-5.3 adaptive defaults from before the rebase.
- Plan-stream handoff support initialized its event state only in the regular EAGLE worker. Frozen-KV MTP inherited code that consumed `_pending_verify_handoff_event` without ever creating or publishing it.
- The first raw-beta fixture used a mathematically expansive unnormalized recurrence, which amplified ordinary BF16 differences and produced a false failure. The final fixture keeps the no-QK-L2 path while using contractive keys and deterministic raw beta spanning `[-2, 2]`.

No full CI was requested for this PR. Validation used dedicated devboxes and precise `/rerun-test` jobs only; queued reruns were cancelled after equivalent devbox coverage completed.

title: [Fix] DP attention: correct the decode->extend prefix off-by-one
author: mmangkad
body:
## Motivation

Under `--enable-dp-attention`, a decode step can compute its token at a RoPE position one past the row's own KV slot, with a causal window one token too wide. This corrupts generation for every request in flight on an affected step. Bisected to #36288 (`ff5578eb4e`), which added the DP decode->extend conversion.

`convert_decode_to_extend` derived the extend prefix from the request's token list:

```python
delta = 0 if self.enable_overlap else -1
self.prefix_lens = [len(r.origin_input_ids) + len(r.output_ids) + delta for r in self.reqs]
```

That assumes `output_ids` always trails `seq_lens` by one step under overlap. It doesn't: `seq_lens` advances only on an iteration that runs `prepare_for_decode`, while a pending result lands regardless, so an iteration that runs prefill instead of decode drains the lag. Extend positions are `arange(prefix_len, prefix_len + extend_len)`, so a 1-token extend needs `prefix_len == seq_len - 1`; with the lag drained the old formula gives `prefix_len == seq_len`.

How often that fires is a property of the traffic: it takes an iteration that runs prefill while a request is mid-decode, so it is common under concurrent load with continuous arrivals and rare on an otherwise idle server. Instrumentation at 512-way concurrency caught it on ~31% of converted requests (1226 / 3986).

The DP-padding decode->extend path already encodes the right invariant (`extend_prefix_lens = self.seq_lens - 1`); this makes the scheduler side agree.

## Modifications

1. **`convert_decode_to_extend`**: derive `prefix_lens` and `extend_range` from `seq_lens_cpu`. Also removes a contradiction the two carried by construction (`prefix_lens` said the prefix was `full_len`, `extend_range` put the new token at `full_len - 1`). Sliced to `bs` because `append_beam_tail` adds rows without reqs, and `zip(strict=True)` so any other divergence raises.
2. **`_local_prefill_cuda_graph_vote`**: reject beam requests. Two hazards — member rows have no req for the reqs-aligned lists, and `process_batch_result` dispatches on `forward_mode`, so a converted batch commits beam requests via `commit_prefill` instead of the batch-level `commit_decode` fold. The second applies whenever `beam_group` is set, so the predicate is the scan, not `beam_tail`.
3. **`mix_with_running`**: same convention, same point in the loop, same contradiction — derive it the same way. **Hardening, not a measured fix**: gsm8k over `--enable-mixed-chunk` shows no delta (94.47/94.16 before, 94.24/94.54 after), since that workload never blocks the mix so the lag never drains. Spec branch is bit-for-bit the old `delta = -1`. Happy to drop this hunk if reviewers prefer a minimal PR.

Tests: new registered CPU test pinning both halves of the geometry in the lag-present and lag-drained states plus beam alignment and the strict-zip failure (all four fail pre-fix); both directions of the beam gate in `test_dp_attn.py`; and a fixture fix in `test_schedule_batch_out_of_place.py`, whose `seq_lens_cpu` was left at the auto-filled `arange(1)` and never read by the old code. Nothing in `test/` covered `convert_decode_to_extend` before.

## Accuracy Tests

gsm8k, 1319 examples, temperature 0, `--num-threads 512 --max-tokens 512`. `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, 4x GB300, `--tp-size 4`. DP adds `--dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention`.

| Build | TP only | DP attention |
|---|---|---|
| main | 94.24 / 94.39 / 94.24 | **71.34 / 70.20 / 70.43** |
| main + this PR | — | **94.24 / 94.47 / 94.39** |
| conversion gated off | — | 94.47 / 94.01 / 94.16 |
| #36288 reverted | 94.09 / 94.24 | 94.16 / 94.01 / 94.09 |
| `ff5578eb4e~1` | 94.31 / 94.24 | 94.16 / 94.24 |

Reverting, gating off, and fixing all recover the same ~94.2, so the conversion is the sole source. `test/registered/unit/managers/`: 630 passed, 4 skipped, 610 subtests.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same runs as above; completion-token counts are within 0.5% across variants (~293k), so latency is comparable.

| DP attention | latency | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 15.1 / 15.1 / 15.2 s | 19323 / 19452 / 19253 |
| conversion gated off | 34.2 / 33.2 / 34.0 s | 8550 / 8873 / 8634 |
| #36288 reverted | 33.4 / 34.2 / 32.0 s | 8793 / 8611 / 9200 |

The conversion is worth ~2.2x, so fixing the geometry beats reverting: a revert is correct but drops DP attention below plain TP (15.1 s). Against the broken build (20.4k tok/s) this is ~5% slower, but that build produces wrong output and is not doing the same work.

author: BBuf
body:
## Problem
MiniCPM-V-4.6 fails to serve on SGLang with a Triton compile error in the GDN prefill conv1d kernel:

```
AssertionError: Mismatched type for col0 between then block (<['256'], bf16>) and else block (<['256'], fp16>)
```

Root cause: MiniCPM-V-4.6 runs a Qwen3.5 LLM (bf16 conv-state cache) but its vision resampler emits **fp16** activations, so the GDN prefill mixes an fp16 `x` stream with a bf16 conv-state cache. The `col0..col3` sliding-window registers then disagree on dtype across the kernel — the `chunk_offset==0` branch loads them from the bf16 conv-state cache while the `chunk_offset>0` branch and the per-token sliding-window reassignment produce fp16 — and Triton's if/else phi type check aborts.

## Fix
Cast the conv-state loads to `x_ptr.dtype.element_ty` (and keep the zero-init on the same x dtype) so `col*` have a single dtype across the whole kernel. Zero-cost when the dtypes already match (the common case).

## Validation
- MiniCPM-V-4.6 now loads, captures decode CUDA graphs, and serves on RTX 5090 (bf16). Paired throughput 591/1885/5608/8013 tok/s at bs=1/4/16/32. (vLLM 0.28 cannot load this model at all — unrelated `k_proj` vs `qkv_proj` weight-mapping bug — so SGLang is the only working engine.)
- No change for models where x and the conv-state cache already share a dtype (the cast is a no-op).

title: [AMD] Fix EAGLE crash when no kv_index_translator is bound on the DSA fp8 read door
author: jiaryang
body:
## Motivation

`_get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa` translates its read ids through the attention backend's `kv_index_translator` unconditionally:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py#L659

But only the FlashAttention and FlashInfer backends bind a translator. `BaseAttentionBackend` documents its `None` default as meaning "no translate":

```python
# The runner's KVIndexTranslator; backends that read through it set the
# instance attribute in __init__. None means "no translate" -- a backend
# that never set it cannot serve the unified pool, which the server-args
# allow-list enforces.
kv_index_translator = None
```

The DSA backend keeps that default. Under EAGLE the draft model runs on the DSA backend and reaches this door, so on gfx950 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` every TP rank dies on the first request:

```
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha_rocm.py", line 211, in forward_normal_rocm_prepare
    kv_a, k_pe = self._get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa(forward_batch)
  File "python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py", line 659, in _get_mla_kv_buffer_from_fp8_for_dsa
    kv_indices = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'translate_dcp_read_ids'
```

The server comes up fine and dies the moment the first request arrives, taking down all four ranks. A target-only (non-speculative) run has no draft model and never reaches this door, which is why the crash is specific to speculative decoding.

Repro (crashes on current `main`, serves normally with this PR):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1
```

## Modifications

Honor the documented contract at the read door: skip the translation when no translator is bound. With no translator the ids were never widened to VIRTUAL, so there is nothing to collapse. Behavior for the backends that do bind a translator is unchanged.

```python
translator = get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator
if translator is not None:
    kv_indices = translator.translate_dcp_read_ids(kv_indices)
```

One file, guard only, no functional change on any path that previously worked.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GSM8K, three runs. Before the fix the speculative server could not serve a single request, so there was no MTP result to compare against.

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EAGLE (this PR) | 0.941 | 0.932 | 0.927 |
| target-only, same build | 0.929 | 0.932 | 0.932 |

Speculative decoding lands in the same band as the target-only reference, as expected.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a single `None` check and leaves every previously working path byte-for-byte identical.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [AMD][Fix] Fix regression in jit build error with FLUX.2-dev on gfx1250
author: sogalin
body:
## Motivation
FLUX.2-dev fails on gfx1250 as soon as denoising starts:
```
Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_flux2_gated_resnorm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:57:9: error: invalid output constraint '=&f' in asm
flux2_gated_resnorm.cuh:64:43: error: invalid output constraint '=f' in asm
amd_warp_sync_functions.h:297:62: error: static assertion failed due to requirement
    'sizeof(unsigned int) == 8': The mask must be a 64-bit integer.
3 errors generated when compiling for gfx1250.
```
The kernel added in #37112 is CUDA-only — it uses PTX inline asm with
float-register operand constraints and `__shfl_down_sync` with a 32-bit mask,
and AMDGPU has neither.
It gets selected because `_blackwell_or_newer()` only tests the device
capability. On ROCm that capability is derived from the gfx number, so gfx1250
reports `(12, 5)` and clears the `major >= 10` test, with
`torch.cuda.is_available()` already true under HIP.
Same class of issue as #34481, for a kernel added after it.
## Modifications
Require a CUDA build in `_blackwell_or_newer()`, matching the guard
`rope/qwen_qkv_epilogue_jit.py` already applies to the same capability test:
```python
 def _blackwell_or_newer(device: torch.device) -> bool:
     return (
-        torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
+        torch.version.cuda is not None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] >= 10
     )
```
Both entry points, `can_defer_flux2_gated_residual()` and
`can_use_flux2_gated_resnorm()`, route through the guard, so ROCm now takes the
`residual_gate_add` + eager norm path for both. CUDA is unaffected.
## Accuracy Tests
ROCm falls back to the same unfused path it used before #37112, so there is no
new numerical behavior to validate on either platform.


## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
