title: [Fix] sampling: deterministic top-p / top-k renorm when tp_size > 1 (TP rank divergence in DFlash/DSpark)
author: gilfordting
body:
## Summary

flashinfer's default top-p / top-k renorm kernels are non-deterministic (float `atomicAdd`); because of this, TP ranks that renormalize the same logits can produce different results. Every consumer of this output (plain sampler, spec-verify) samples against a deterministic coin and commits the result to per-rank KV/radix state. A coin that lands in between the cross-rank gap causes divergence across ranks, and NCCL collectives hang.

Previous PRs (#33549, #33289; #33614) work around this issue by broadcasting rank 0's decision. This PR addresses the root cause and avoids an extra collective, by routing the renorm through flashinfer's `is_deterministic=True` variants. This is turned on where it matters:

| configuration                         | renorm kernels  | why                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| single rank                           | fast            | nothing to agree with                                          |
| `attn_tp_size > 1`                    | deterministic   | each rank computes the same result; bit-identical across ranks |
| `--enable-deterministic-inference`    | deterministic   | self-explanatory                                               |
| `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1` / `0` | forced on / off | explicit override                                              |

Repro + results are below. With all relevant broadcasts turned off, the fast kernels reproduce the hang on H100 and B200 in every run. The deterministic kernels never diverge, and the end-to-end cost to TPOT is marginal.

## Root cause

- `sgl_kernel.top_p_renorm_prob` and `top_k_renorm_prob` forward to flashinfer.
    - Top-p on rows longer than 2048 uses the AIR radix kernel (>= 0.6.7, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2752) whose default histogram is a float atomic.
    - Top-k (`RadixTopKRenormProbMultiCTA`) pools the kept mass with a float atomic.
    - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4831 (0.7.x, sglang pins 0.7.2) added a fixed-point `is_deterministic=True` at unchanged latency.
- In non-greedy verification, each rank compares its own `target_probs` (top-p/top-k output) against a shared coin and samples the bonus token from `relu(q - p)`.
    - If ranks differ slightly, the coin might cross the acceptance or bonus thresholds on some ranks and not others; this will cause KV state to drift and a later prefix match will cause NCCL collectives to hang.
- The sampler's `min_p` path calls the same kernels with no broadcast (`SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is off by default).
- Earlier synthetic repros were clean because they used `top_p=1.0`, which skips the kernel entirely.

## Repro

**Setup**

- Image: current main (nightly `ed8c3139`, flashinfer 0.7.1, sgl_kernel 0.4.10) with this PR applied.
- Model, config, workload: TP=2 DFlash, Llama-3.1-8B + `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.9`, 32 concurrent multi-turn streams, fp8 KV.
- Broadcast collectives off:
    - Hard-coded broadcast is only on for the EAGLE path. We use DFlash.
    - `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=off` turns off #33614's broadcasts.
    - `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` are off by default.
- Deterministic renorm kernels on using a new environment variable, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
- A probe all-gathers per-verify-step fingerprints of `{rng state, prefix_lens, draft_tokens, target_logits, target_probs, accept_len, bonus, commit_lens, out_tokens}` and reports the first field that differs.
    - It also calls `top_p_renorm_prob` twice on the same input on one rank, counting mismatches after.

**Results**

"knob" below refers to the new env-var, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
| broadcast | renorm | runs | requests per run | first cross-rank `target_probs` difference | rank-local mismatches (top-p calls) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | fast (knob=0, same kernels as main) | 4 x H100, 2 x B200 | 1.4k to 6.5k | 1 to 22 s | 0.4 to 0.9 % | **all 6 hung**, at 190 to 610 s |
| off | deterministic (knob=1) | 3 x H100, 2 x B200 | 22.6k to 35.4k | never | 0 of 276,000 | all 5 clean, full 30 min |
| all (#33614) | fast (knob=0) | 1 x H100 | 25.2k | 14 s | 0.9 % | clean: 436 `target_probs` divergences, none reaches a token |
| all (#33614) | deterministic (knob=1) | 1 x H100 | 24.4k | never | 0 of 46,000 | clean, 0 divergences |

Every fast-kernel run with the broadcast off hung, with the same recorded chain each time:

- `target_probs` differs between ranks while logits, `prefix_lens` and RNG are identical.
- `bonus` / `out_tokens` differ on one rank.
- Next step's `draft_tokens` differ.
- Hang.

Toggling only the knob to 1 on the same image, model, load and probe consistently results in zero divergences, zero rank-local mismatches, and no hang.

## Kernel measurements

We perform 99 repeated calls on byte-identical input. Settings: flashinfer 0.7.1, vocab 128256, H100. B200 and B300 give the same results.

`nondet` refers to calls that differ from call 0.

| rows | input distribution | kernel | current default        | `is_deterministic=True` |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 32   | flat               | top-p  | 0.136 ms, nondet 99/99 | 0.169 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-p  | 0.127 ms, 0/99         | 0.149 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | flat               | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 99/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 77/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-p  | 0.603 ms, 98/99        | 0.815 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-k  | 0.288 ms, 99/99        | 0.289 ms, 0/99          |

We observe the following:

- Top-k performs near-identical between both fast and deterministic arms.
- Top-p adds 20 to 45% to a 0.1 to 0.8 ms kernel. We measure how much this matters in the next section.
- The deterministic wrapper adds no host sync and no `cudaMalloc`, so there is no overhead.

## End-to-end speed

**Setup**

- Workload: `sglang.bench_serving`, random 512-in / 256-out, 400 prompts, concurrency 32.
- Model, config: Llama-3.1-8B, fp8 KV, triton attention, H100.
- One container boots four servers in sequence with the knob 1 / 0 / 1 / 0, two trials each, so both arms share a host and an image.
- We look at TPOT, since this code change is exercised during decode. The first trial (warmup) is dropped, and we calculate mean TPOT. We see that differences are on the order of 0.01 ms.

| config                                                                           | knob=1   | knob=0   | delta  | accept len    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ------------- |
| plain TP2 `min_p=0.05` (the path the default policy makes deterministic), host A | 4.974 ms | 4.976 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| same, host B, order 0 / 1 / 0 / 1                                                | 5.058 ms | 5.062 ms | -0.1 % |               |
| plain TP1 `min_p=0.05`                                                           | 8.065 ms | 8.067 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| DFlash TP2 `top_p=0.9` (knob=1 forces the verify path deterministic too)         | 3.992 ms | 3.983 ms | +0.2 % | 4.563 / 4.564 |
| EAGLE3 TP2 `top_p=0.9`                                                           | 7.191 ms | 7.175 ms | +0.2 % | 1.929 / 1.930 |

Thus, we see that there is no measureable end-to-end cost, including the forced-deterministic verify path; the accept length is also unchanged.

The renorm kernel runs once per step over `batch_size` rows (sampler) or `batch_size x draft_tokens` rows (verify), so deterministic top-p adds ~0.03 ms at 32 rows and ~0.2 ms at 256 rows, which is small compared to a step of several ms.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py` (new):
    - `renorm_deterministic(ranks_agree)` policy.
    - `top_p_renorm_prob` / `top_k_renorm_prob` for the sampler and `spec_top_p_renorm_prob` / `spec_top_k_renorm_prob` for verify, calling flashinfer with `is_deterministic=True` when appropriate (`sgl_kernel` as before otherwise).
    - The flag's presence is checked once at import (`inspect.signature`), so an older flashinfer degrades to the fast kernel rather than failing on the first sampled request.
    - Without flashinfer (MUSA, XPU) `sgl_kernel`'s own single-CTA kernel is already deterministic; no int32-sensitive code is added there.
- `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `speculative/eagle_utils.py` are the only renorm call sites, and now they import from the module above.
    - The `_sync_token_ids_across_tp` and `spec_tp_sync.py` comments name the renorm kernels as a known source of nondeterminism and point at the knob.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC` next to the other determinism knobs.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_renorm.py`: existing correctness tests run through the new module; regression tests call each deterministic renorm 30 times on a flat 256 x 128256 input and assert bit-identical output (the default kernels fail this 30 of 30); scoped runtime-context fixture.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_renorm_policy.py` (CPU): single rank fast; TP=2 sampler deterministic and verify fast; `--enable-deterministic-inference` forces on; env overrides both ways.

The fix lives in `sglang` rather than the `sgl_kernel` wrappers, because `sglang-kernel` ships as a pinned prebuilt wheel. A wrapper change there is not testable in CI, and is not delivered until the next kernel release.

This fix is Complementary to #33614: the broadcast keeps replicated state safe against any future non-deterministic operator. This removes the one we found, so rank 0's own output and every other consumer of `target_probs` (logprobs, sampling masks) become reproducible too.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Fix] moe: Preserve FP32 router precision across model gates
author: seongyun1104
body:
## Motivation

Addresses the independent model fixes called out in #38695.

Several MoE models still discard router precision at model-specific boundaries:

- MiMo-V2, Ernie4, and Kimi Linear can construct the checkpoint correction bias in bf16, even though expert selection consumes it in fp32-sensitive score arithmetic.
- Bailing MoE and Bailing MoE Linear compute with fp32 router weights when configured, then cast the logits back to the hidden-state dtype before top-k.

These paths either collapse checkpoint bias values or throw away the fp32 router output immediately before expert selection.

LLaDA2 originally had the same router-output downcast, but #31768 fixed that path independently. The current PR therefore leaves LLaDA2 untouched.

## Modifications

- Keep `e_score_correction_bias` parameters in fp32 for MiMo-V2, Ernie4, and Kimi Linear.
- Return the gate GEMM output at the router-weight dtype for Bailing MoE and Bailing MoE Linear.

The patch is limited to five model files. It does not introduce a shared `RouterGate`, add a kernel, or change expert computation.

## Accuracy Tests

No new unit test is included, following the maintainer guidance in #38695 that these model-file fixes do not require one. The changes only preserve the dtype already selected for the correction bias or router GEMM output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. No kernel is added. The Bailing paths remove a dtype-conversion operation when the router is configured for fp32.

## Test Plan

- [x] Rebased onto current `main` (`961bcf481d`).
- [x] Python bytecode compilation for all five changed files.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files <all changed files>`.
- [x] `git diff --check`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the contribution guide.
- [x] Follow the requested model-file-only scope.

title: Fix: post-load staging regression breaks offload meta/sharded_gpu modes
author: Hide-on-bushsh
body: ## Motivation The offloader (V2, `--offload-group-size`) intentionally parks offloaded parameters on the meta device through weight post-processing: - `--offload-mode=meta`: all offloaded params become meta at build time (weight loading is a no-op via a replaced `weight_loader`). - `--offload-mode=sharded_gpu` / `shm_cpu`: non-rank-0 DP ranks park params on meta during loading (rank 0 owns the real data). This is by design: device kernels skip meta params (e.g. `npu_format_cast` has an explicit meta skip), and the old `device_loading_context` passed meta tensors through untouched. Since #35180, `process_weights_after_loading` hits the new upfront check and the scheduler dies during startup: RuntimeError: Cannot post-process meta tensor FusedMoE.w13_weight The bug is device-agnostic (same code path on CUDA/NPU); it was caught by the NPU offload CI suites (`test_npu_offload_modes.py`, `test_npu_offload_group_size.py`). ## Modifications In `stage_module_for_post_load()`, record tensors that are already meta at context entry and pass them through untouched — no staging, no restore — restoring the pre-#35180 behavior for offloader-parked params. The original guard is preserved: tensors that *become* meta during post-load processing still raise, so genuine kernel bugs keep failing fast. for test_npu_offload_modes.py before after ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. title: [Fix] Disable NCCL graph buffer registration for the TP LM-head all-to-all (pure-DP decode hang under request bursts)
author: hanming-lu
body:
## Motivation

Pure-DP PD decode nodes (`tp_size == dp_size` with DP attention) auto-enable the TP LM-head all-to-all (`_tp_lm_head_all_to_all_default`), a PyNccl send/recv captured in the decode CUDA graphs. With NCCL's default graph-capture buffer registration (`NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=1`) that exchange deadlocks the first time a burst of new requests ramps the DP ranks at different rates: one rank leaves the step while the others spin in `ncclDevKernel_SendRecv` forever, the scheduler watchdog fires on every rank, and the whole gang restarts.

Reproduced deterministically on a tp4/dp4/ep4 unified launch with `--enable-tp-lm-head-all-to-all` (hang on the first ~240-request burst from idle, every launch) and on a multi-node tp16/dp16/ep16 PD decode deployment. `--enable-dp-lm-head`, which avoids the all-to-all, does not hang.

Experiment matrix on the tp4/dp4/ep4 repro:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| baseline | hang on round 0 |
| different MoE backend | hang on round 0 |
| dedicated non-pool all-to-all buffers (no env change) | hang on round 0 |
| `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0 NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | 4/4 rounds pass |
| `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` only | 5/5 rounds pass |
| plain gather path (all-to-all off), default env | 5/5 rounds pass |
| this PR, default env | 10/10 rounds pass |

At the hang, cuda-gdb showed three ranks resident in `ncclDevKernel_SendRecv` and the fourth already in the next step's first cross-rank MoE kernel; per-rank Python-level decisions (forward mode, graph replay, LM-head branch) were identical across ranks, so the divergence is inside the registered exchange. The exact NCCL-side mechanism (registration of graph-pool temporaries whose addresses the pool reuses) is inferred from the experiment matrix, not from NCCL internals.

## Modifications

- `handle_data_parallelism` now sets `NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER=0` in the server environment whenever the TP LM-head all-to-all resolves to enabled, so the schedulers' NCCL communicators inherit it. An explicit user setting is kept and a warning is logged.
- Scope: only the all-to-all path. `attn_tp > 1` shapes never enable the all-to-all (it requires `tp_size == dp_size`), and `--enable-dp-lm-head` is mutually exclusive with it, so neither changes behavior. Eager NCCL ops are unaffected; only the two collectives captured in the decode graphs (the LM-head all-to-all and the DP gather feeding it) go through NCCL's staging buffers instead of registered zero-copy.
- Unit tests cover: pure-DP decode node sets the env, an explicit value is preserved with a warning, and unified serving / decode with `--enable-dp-lm-head` leave the env untouched.

## Original commits

- `53b0218449`
- `ca3830e652`

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (no numerics change).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Verified on an internal tp4/dp4/ep4 setup: without this change every launch hung on the first burst of ~240 concurrent requests from idle; with it, 10 burst rounds (240-256 concurrent requests, 250-1000 input tokens, 20-400 output tokens) all completed with health 200 throughout and no watchdog. A tp4/dp2/ep4 scoping check resolves `enable_tp_lm_head_all_to_all=False`, leaves the environment untouched, and completes 10/10 rounds, i.e. no behavior change there.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).
- [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging.
- [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss your PR.

title: [NPU] Fix device mismatch in SWA mask for DSpark verify graph capture
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

DSpark verify reuses `DFlashVerifyInput`, so `_is_dflash_verify()` routes it into the `seq_lens_cpu` branch of the SWA mask update in the NPU attention backend. Unlike DFlash (whose target verify graph runs through the NPU graph runner with on-device `seq_lens`), DSpark's verify graph goes through `decode_cuda_graph_runner`, which passes a CPU tensor (`forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` during capture, `buffers.seq_lens_cpu` on replay). Comparing it against the on-device `swa_indices` buffer raised:

```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device. Expected NPU tensor, please check whether the input tensor device is correct.
```

This crashes the target model at graph capture time, so DSpark cannot run on Ascend NPU with hybrid SWA layers.

## Modifications

One-line fix in `ascend_backend.py` (`_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`): move `seq_lens_int` to the backend device before the SWA mask comparison:

```python
seq_lens_int = seq_lens_cpu[:bs].int().to(self.device)
```

- No-op for the DFlash path (its `seq_lens_cpu` is already on-device).
- Side benefit: DSpark now also gets the correct SWA mask window (`seq_lens_cpu` = prefix + block_size), so draft KV positions stay unmasked instead of being masked out by the prefix-only `seq_lens`.
- The copy runs in replay prep (outside the captured graph) and moves `bs × 4` bytes, so the performance impact is negligible.

## Accuracy Tests

No impact — this change only fixes a crash at graph capture time (device placement of metadata tensors); it does not alter any compute logic. On devices where capture previously succeeded (DFlash path), `.to(self.device)` is a no-op.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No impact — the added transfer is a host-side `bs × 4` byte copy executed outside the captured graph (~µs level), and it is a no-op when the tensor is already on-device.

title: [NPU][Bugfix] Disable pinned memory to fix DeepSeek-V2 DP-attention hang
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

#36472 introduced the in-tree `NPUSRTPlatform` and made NPU machines resolve to it instead of the base `SRTPlatform`. Unlike the base default (`is_pin_memory_available=False`), the new class returns `True`, silently switching hot paths such as the next-token-logits copies and the xgrammar bitmask allocation to pinned memory with `non_blocking` H2D copies.

torch_npu's pinned-memory + async-copy semantics are not verified against CANN on this stack. The correctness of `non_blocking` H2D depends on a stream-ordering guarantee that has not been established for NPU, and under DP attention — where compute, copy, and HCCL communication streams run concurrently — inference intermittently hangs (deadlock) with DeepSeek-V2.

Two independent reproductions confirm this:

- The #36472 author observed DeepSeek-V2 hanging during normal DP-attention inference with pin_memory enabled.
- We reproduced the same hang on Ascend 910C under DP-attention retraction stress (`TestDPRetract`, i.e. `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1` + a small KV budget).

Both hang and disappear with `is_pin_memory_available=False`. Since the per-step benefit of pinning is limited to KB-scale decode-path buffers, disabling it is the safe choice until the async-copy stream semantics are validated.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/platforms/npu.py`: force `is_pin_memory_available` to return `False`, restoring the pre-#36472 behavior. Re-enable only after the pinned-memory async-copy semantics are validated against CANN (optionally behind a debug env var first).
- `test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py`: align the NPU pin-memory unit test with the restored behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Reran the `TestDPRetract` stress repro (DP attention + 4500-token KV budget + radix retract stress + regex/JSON constrained generation) multiple times on NPU: all passed with this change, while the server previously hung intermittently during DP-attention inference.

title: Fix corrupted chat prompts on mistral_common tokenizers (tool_choice auto never fires)
author: alisonshao
body:
On Mistral3 models, `tool_choice: "auto"` never produces a tool call — the model emits one token, EOS, and returns empty content. `tool_choice: "required"` works, which makes it look like a tool-calling bug. It isn't: the prompt is corrupted for every request.

`_render_and_encode_chat_template` renders the chat template to a string and re-encodes it. mistral_common tokenizers emit control tokens that have no text form, so that round-trip destroys them. Comparing the server's prompt token ids against `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)` for the same request:

```
server:   ['<s>', '<', 's', '>[', 'A', 'VAIL', 'ABLE', '_TO', 'OL', 'S', '][', ...]   103 tokens
template: ['<s>', '[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]', '[', ...]                                       82 tokens
```

`[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]` (control token id 5) comes back as the letters `A`,`VAIL`,`ABLE`,`_TO`,`OL`,`S`, and a second BOS is prepended. The model never sees the tool block as a control structure. transformers warns about exactly this: `MistralCommonBackend.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=False)` is unsafe and may lead to unexpected behavior. Please consider using `tokenize=True` instead and don't encode the output manually.

The margin is thin, which is why it reads as arbitrary: the first sampled token is `</s>` at logprob -1.413 with ` [` right behind at -1.476. `required` hides it by constraining the output.

Every request takes the text path because `_engine_prompt` sends text whenever the model `is_multimodal`, and Mistral3 carries a `vision_config`.

This patch probes once at startup whether the render-then-encode round-trip reproduces `tokenize=True`, and when it does not, encodes straight to ids and sends those. Requests carrying media keep the text path, since the multimodal processor still has to tokenize it to expand placeholders.

Verified on Ministral-3-3B (same `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` class and tekken tokenizer as Mistral Medium 3.5):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tool_choice: "auto"` | no tool call, 1 token generated | `get_weather{"location": "Paris, France"}` |
| prompt | 103 tokens, doubled BOS | 82 tokens, control tokens intact |
| plain chat, no tools | 21 tokens, reply began `<s>[EVAL]` | 12 tokens, clean reply |

The last row is the wider point: this degraded ordinary chat too, not only tool calls.

The probe discriminates correctly — Ministral-3-3B renders to 12 junk tokens against 4 correct ones (`<s>[INST]x[/INST]`) and is flagged lossy; Qwen3-0.6B round-trips to identical ids and keeps the existing path.

title: [Moe] Fix flashinfer_trtllm silently dropping swiglu_limit clamped SwiGLU activation
author: Dovis01
body:
## Motivation

Models with a clamped SwiGLU activation (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM-5-Next, Qwen3-Next style) plumb the clamp limit through `FusedMoE(swiglu_limit=...)` -> `MoeRunnerConfig.swiglu_limit`. All MoE runner backends are supposed to honor it: `triton` passes it into the fused kernel, `deep_gemm` applies it via `silu_and_mul_clamp` / `_apply_swiglu_limit`, but `flashinfer_trtllm` **silently ignores it**.

The flashinfer_trtllm FP8 path only materializes `gemm1_clamp_limit` (the TRT-LLM kernel parameter), which stays `None` for models that use the `swiglu_limit` field. With no error and no warning, the expert activation degrades from the trained `silu(clamp(gate, max=L)) * clamp(up, -L, L)` (with L = 10.0) to a plain `silu(gate) * up`, which measurably hurts accuracy.

On GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (blockwise 128x128 FP8, 288 routed experts, top-8, 1 shared expert, `swiglu_limit=10.0`), GSM8K 5-shot with only `--moe-runner-backend` varying:

| moe_runner_backend | GSM8K strict-match (runs) | mean |
|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.9356 / 0.9363 | 0.9360 |
| deep_gemm | 0.9249 / 0.9287 / 0.9295 / 0.9310 / 0.9340 / 0.9348 | 0.9305 |
| flashinfer_trtllm (before) | 0.9265 / 0.9280 / 0.9287 | 0.9277 |
| **flashinfer_trtllm (this fix)** | **0.9348 / 0.9371** | **0.9360** |

Before/after ranges do not overlap (within-group variance is ~0.2pp); after the fix flashinfer_trtllm matches the triton baseline exactly. fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39797. Thx for finding this issue. @NolenLiang

## Modifications

Single-file change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod._prepare_flashinfer_trtllm_activation_params()`: when `gemm1_clamp_limit` is not explicitly set, fall back to `swiglu_limit`.

Why here and not in the model code: this function is the only consumer that builds the TRT-LLM SwiGLU parameters (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`), so the two naming pipelines (`gemm1_clamp_limit` used by gpt_oss / bailing_moe_v3, `swiglu_limit` used by DeepseekV2MoE-family models) converge at a single point; `triton` consumes both fields independently (`gemm1_limit` and `swiglu_limit`), so setting both at the model level would change behavior of unrelated backends, while this fallback is scoped to the flashinfer_trtllm preparation only. Models that already set `gemm1_clamp_limit` explicitly (gpt_oss, bailing_moe_v3) are unaffected, and the same silent drop is fixed for every other model that routes the clamp through `swiglu_limit` (e.g. Qwen3-Next) whenever flashinfer_trtllm is used.

The TRT-LLM kernel natively supports the clamp: with `ActivationType.Swiglu`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=L` computes `X2 = clamp(X2, max=L)`, `X1 = clamp(X1, -L, L)`, `out = X2 * sigmoid(alpha * X2) * (X1 + beta)` (alpha defaults to 1.0, beta to 0.0), which matches the reference `swiglu_clamped` in `models/glm5_next.py` exactly. Verified against flashinfer 0.6.18 (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe`, `Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8`).

## Accuracy Tests

Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, blockwise 128x128), 4x B200, TP=4/EP=4. Launch (only `--moe-runner-backend` varies between runs):

```bash
 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --context-length 16384 --disable-radix-cache \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --served-model-name glm-5-next-fp8
```

Eval (lm-evaluation-harness, `local-completions`):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=glm-5-next-fp8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 --seed 1234 --log_samples
```

Results (exact_match, strict-match):

| config | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flashinfer_trtllm before | 0.9287 | 0.9265 | 0.9280 | 0.9277 |
| flashinfer_trtllm **after** | 0.9371 | 0.9348 | – | **0.9360** |
| triton (baseline) | 0.9363 | 0.9356 | – | 0.9360 |

Fixed server sanity-checked with deterministic generation (temperature=0) on GSM8K-style prompts before running the evals.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected. The change only materializes one extra per-expert fp32 tensor (`[num_local_experts]`, 288 bytes here) once at weight-load time; the hot kernel call is unchanged (the `gemm1_clamp_limit` argument was already being passed, as `None`). No throughput regression expected or observed.

title: [HiCache] fix: bound the controller reset join so a stalled storage thread cannot hang the scheduler
author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`HiCacheController.reset()` previously set `storage_stop_event` and called
untimed `join()` on four storage threads. If a thread does not exit, reset can
wait indefinitely and block the scheduler. This change hardens the reset
teardown by reusing the existing detach helper, `_stop_storage_threads()`.

## Modifications

`reset()` now uses the helper's queue wakeup sentinels, bounded joins, and final
thread-liveness check before clearing shared state and restarting storage threads.
Sentinels can wake threads waiting on queues; they cannot interrupt an in-progress
`all_reduce()`. Likewise, a join timeout only bounds the caller's wait and does
not terminate the worker or cancel its collective.

The helper joins four threads sequentially, with `timeout=10` for each, so the
combined join wait can reach approximately 40 seconds, not 10 seconds total.
After all joins, it raises `RuntimeError` if any thread remains alive. This prevents
reset from clearing shared state and starting replacement threads while an old
thread is still running. The queue clearing, stop-event clearing, and thread
re-creation after a successful stop remain unchanged.

A prefetch thread blocked in a cross-rank collective is a possible stalled-thread
scenario inferred from the source, not a reproduced failure. This PR bounds the
reset wait; it does not resolve the underlying collective stall. Treat it as a
hardening change pending validation of that scenario's reachability.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` + `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`:
  1278 passed, 1436 skipped, 70 subtests.
- `test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py`, `test_unified_cache_linker.py`,
  `test_radix_cache_unit.py`: 95 passed, 71 subtests.

title: [AMD][Fix] AgentX HIP TPOT regression when SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN is set
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes an AgentX TPOT regression on HIP after [#37134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37134).

Agent mode (InferenceMax AgentX) sets `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.39` for Qwen3.5 (`match-expected` / `real-draft-token`). The server still runs a full EAGLE verify, then overwrites accept length. #37134 auto-enables `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` on HIP, so every decode step also runs the Triton chain sampler; that result is then thrown away. Extra verify work shows up as ~14% worse AgentX TPOT (TP4 conc=4) vs pre-#37134 / a 0915 baseline.

Fixed-length MTP does not set `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, and the client is greedy (`temperature=0`), so verify stays on `argmax` and does not hit this regression.

Skip the HIP auto-enable when `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN > 0`. Real eval / serving (env unset or `< 0`) still auto-enables as in #37134.

## Modifications

- `_should_auto_enable_hip_rejection_sampling` now takes `simulate_acc_len` and returns false when `simulate_acc_len > 0`.
- `_handle_eagle_family` passes `envs.SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` into that gate.
- Explicit `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is unchanged (the helper already no-ops when the flag is already on).
- Unit test `test_simulate_acc_len_stays_off` in `test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No new EVAL_ONLY / quality run. The `EVAL_ONLY=true` AgentX path does not set `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, so HIP still auto-enables rejection sampling as in #37134. This change only affects the simulated-accept throughput path, whose accept length is overwritten after verify. The new unit test covers the auto-enable predicate for `simulate_acc_len=3.39` vs `-1.0`.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

InferenceX arm `qwen3.5-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp`, recipe `benchmarks/single_node/agentic/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`, TP4, conc=4, `DURATION=1200`. Same container (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260915`), weights, GPUs, and recipe; only the SGLang SHA / this patch changes.

| SGLang | TPOT mean (ms) | Interactivity mean (tok/s/user) | total tok/s | requests ok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `832ec39cc` (pre-#37134-era good) | 3.1 | 317.9 | 21163.7 | 350/357 |
| `8d08dfdab` (main, #37134 in tree) | 3.6 | 277.5 | 19124.3 | 334/341 |
| `8d08dfdab` + this patch | 3.2 | 315.6 | 21158.2 | 350/357 |

First-bad commit for the AgentX drop was `7eedd57ab` (#37134). Parent `2f7d04da5` was still good.

title: [Fix] [NPU] qwen3_6: Set accuracy cases to greedy decoding and tune retries
author: pllimax
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Two changes to the NPU test suite:

- Four Qwen3.6 accuracy cases used non-zero sampling temperatures (0.2 / 0.6 / 1.0), which makes their accuracy results depend on sampling. Switch them to greedy decoding so the runs are reproducible, and bound how many evaluations each case may consume.
- The DP attention basic-function case was temporarily disabled for DTS2026091464350. Re-enable it now that the issue is resolved.

Note: the removal of the LLaDA2.0-mini basic-function case that this PR originally carried is no longer part of the change set. Upstream renamed that file to `test_npu_llada2_mini_fdfo.py`, so the old path is already gone from `main` and there is nothing left to delete.

## Modifications

### 1. Set `temperature=0` for four Qwen3.6 accuracy cases

All four are `nightly-acc-2-npu-a3` cases.

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_1p_gpqa.py` | 1.0 | 0 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_w8a8_1p_in3k5_out1k5_50ms_gpqa.py` | 1.0 | 0 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_35b_a3b/test_npu_qwen3_6_35b_a3b_1p_aime26.py` | 0.6 | 0 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_35b_a3b/test_npu_qwen3_6_35b_a3b_1p_in64k_out1k_prefix90_50ms_aime26.py` | 0.2 | 0 |

### 2. Adjust `max_retries` of the affected accuracy cases

`max_retries` is the number of evalscope evaluations a case performs, not the number of extra retries: the case passes as soon as one evaluation reaches the threshold, and fails after the last one. When it is left unset it defaults to 3 for the datasets listed in `DATASET_FLUCTUATION` (`gpqa_diamond`, `aime25`, `aime26`, `gsm8k`) and to 1 otherwise.

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_1p_gpqa.py` | 1 | 2 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_w8a8_1p_in3k5_out1k5_50ms_gpqa.py` | 1 | 2 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_35b_a3b/test_npu_qwen3_6_35b_a3b_1p_aime26.py` | unset (3) | 2 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_35b_a3b/test_npu_qwen3_6_35b_a3b_1p_in64k_out1k_prefix90_50ms_aime26.py` | unset (3) | 2 |
| `test/registered/npu/accuracy/kimi_k3/test_npu_kimi_k3_w4a8_32p_gpqa.py` | unset (3) | 1 |

The four Qwen3.6 cases are capped at 2 evaluations so a single unlucky evaluation can still be absorbed without letting the worst case grow; the Kimi-K3 case (32 devices, ~3600 s) is pinned to 1 so it fails fast instead of running the default three evaluations.

### 3. Re-enable the DP attention basic-function case

Remove `disabled="Temporarily disable this test case due to DTS2026091464350"` from the `base-b-test-4-npu-a3` registration in `test/registered/npu/basic_function/dp_attn/test_npu_dp_attention.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

These changes touch accuracy test configurations only - no model, kernel or runtime code is modified.

title: [KDA] Fix ptx_kda prefill NaN without a gate lower bound and workspace growth
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

Validating `--linear-attn-prefill-backend ptx_kda` end to end on B200 turned up two problems in the PTX prefill path. Neither depends on the arch: both exist on SM103, where ptx_kda runs today.

1. **Models without a gate lower bound get NaN.** On Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, ptx_kda scored GSM8K 0.000 against 0.902 for Triton, every prompt logprob of a 6K-token prefill was NaN, and nothing was logged. The kernel only handles the safe gate (`lower_bound` set, as in Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3-Flash).
2. **The workspace cache grows with every batch shape until the process runs out of memory.** A GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 server on ptx_kda hit CUDA OOM about 20 s into GSM8K, while Triton on the same args ran the full eval.

## Modifications

- `srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_ptx.py`: batches from a model without a gate lower bound take the wrapper's existing Triton fallback, the same path as spec draft-extend, track-state snapshots and unsupported shapes. It logs one warning.
- `kernels/jit/csrc/attention/kda_prefill.cu`: `get_workspace` clears its cache once it holds 4 entries. The device code is unchanged.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill.py`, one regression case per fix. Like the existing ptx cases they run on SM103 (GB300 CI).
  - `test_ptx_without_lower_bound_matches_triton`: with no lower bound and `exp(A_log)` near 200, the output must be finite and match Triton.
  - `test_ptx_workspace_memory_is_bounded`: 16 new batch shapes must not keep one workspace each.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests on B200, with the companion PR's SM100 enablement applied so the ptx cases run there (on this branch alone they run on SM103 only):

```
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_nvidia_prefill PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_padded_raw_beta PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_prefill PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_without_lower_bound_matches_triton PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_workspace_memory_is_bounded PASSED
5 passed in 152.71s
```

Both new cases fail on the code before this change: the output has NaN, and 16 shapes keep 107.6 MB against a 37.9 MB bound.

End-to-end on B200, same setup:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi-Linear-48B, TP2, ptx_kda: GSM8K | 0.000 (Triton 0.902; 500 questions, 5-shot) | 0.93 (200 questions, 5-shot) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4, ptx_kda: GSM8K, 500 questions, 20-shot | CUDA OOM during the eval | 0.932 (Triton 0.924) |

- Kimi-Linear now runs its prefill on Triton, and the server logs the fallback once per rank.
- GLM-5.3-Flash uses the cookbook Blackwell recipe plus `--disable-radix-cache`, which keeps its tracked batches off the Triton fallback. Its prompt logprobs on a 2040-token prefill are bit-identical with and without the cache bound.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The bound can make a cache hit into a miss, so this measures what a miss costs: the latency of the first call of a batch shape against a repeat of it. B200, 16 heads, safe gate, 16K tokens, CUDA events:

| batch | new shape (miss) | repeated shape (hit) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 sequence (fused route) | 895–939 µs | 764–798 µs |
| 2–9 sequences (builder + chain) | 573 µs | 532 µs |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format are clean on the changed Python files).
- [x] Add unit tests (a regression case for each fix).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

title: [Fix] sampling: Make top-k/top-p filtering consistent across sampling paths
author: alvion427
body:
Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct dense/sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Fuse CUDA unseeded top-p rescaling by reusing the retained top-k maximum, avoiding a full-vocabulary maximum reduction and exponential intermediate.
- Preserve logsumexp for seeded/non-CUDA callers; UNO rejects deterministic inference.
- Document that fused FP32 rounding can change cutoff membership, without promising bitwise identity or trainer alignment.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

`TestSamplingMaskCapture` and `test_speculative_sampling.py`: **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, no failures/errors/skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed with pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The same tests exercised pre-fix filtering from public base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd`; EAGLE retained the extracted helper signature for testability.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, syntax, whitespace, and registry checks passed. The H200 results above apply to `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f`, not current-head CI.

[Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39500026515) passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03`; Extra/AMD had failures. CI States below tracks newer runs.

<!-- lint: profile=evidence-heavy -->

### Historical HTTP validation at `f0c0a64`

All 10 HTTP checks passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` on H200 using `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`, Transformers 5.19.0, and the runtime below.

NGRAM accepted `min_p=0`. With `min_p=0.1`, non-streaming requests returned HTTP 400; streaming requests emitted `abort`, embedded status 400, and `[DONE]`. Each rejection mode ran twice; all four following valid requests succeeded. Ordinary sampling accepted `min_p=0.1`. Both servers remained healthy before teardown. Other speculative modes and PD deployment were not exercised. Source Rust extensions used `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

These measurements predate fusion in `b94a95d5e805e0ee214c6d355a3a6cc79dd5e073`; see the [fused-helper validation summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41916#issuecomment-6328764169) for results and limitations.

Historical head `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` versus base `f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38`:

| Setup | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware/runtime | H200; driver 595.71.05; Python 3.12.15; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.2; Triton 3.8.0 |
| Functions | Production head functions and exact base definitions with unchanged dependencies; UNO retains `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` |
| Inputs | Seed 41916; FP32 normal logits, std=2; temperature=0.8; top-k=50; top-p=0.9; draft width=6 |
| Timing | Median microseconds/call; five alternating base/head samples; 200 CUDA Graph replays/sample; compilation and warmup excluded |
| Shape order | Vocabulary 32,768 then 128,256; batch 1, 16, 64 for each |

Outputs were finite and normalized; base/head sampling semantics intentionally differ.

| Path | Batch | Vocabulary | Base (us) | Head (us) | Added (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 32,768 | 79.85 | 99.50 | 19.65 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 32,768 | 28.75 | 38.01 | 9.26 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 32,768 | 130.29 | 158.38 | 28.09 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 32,768 | 30.45 | 48.85 | 18.40 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 32,768 | 373.87 | 437.04 | 63.17 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 32,768 | 61.63 | 119.92 | 58.30 |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 128,256 | 101.42 | 139.81 | 38.40 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 128,256 | 49.55 | 70.68 | 21.13 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 128,256 | 320.54 | 442.95 | 122.41 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 128,256 | 59.51 | 116.82 | 57.31 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 128,256 | 896.05 | 1211.86 | 315.81 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 128,256 | 163.58 | 369.16 | 205.58 |

With top-p disabled at batch=16, vocabulary=128,256, DFlash measured 300.17 -> 300.31 us; UNO measured 57.71 -> 56.90 us. Costs increased 17-38% for DFlash and 32-126% for UNO in this sweep. End-to-end serving throughput and latency remain unmeasured.

`torch.profiler` CPU/CUDA traces used ten graph replays and three ordinary calls, after warmup. At batch=64, vocabulary=128,256:

| Path | Additional full-vocabulary work | Profile attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash sparse | Eager `logsumexp`: max, subtract, exp, sum, final normalization | 9 kernels, ~350 us; ~188 MiB temporary tensor. Total kernel count: 30 -> 52. Unprofiled rerun: 886 -> 1199 us. |
| UNO compact | Compiled full-vocabulary max and exp-sum reductions | 4 kernels, ~206 us; two scans dominate. Total kernel count: 6 -> 10. Unprofiled rerun: 163 -> 369 us. |

DFlash's top-p kernel fell from ~53 to 5 us; kernel durations attribute costs but do not replace unprofiled timings.

UNO depends on shape warmup order. Starting with vocabulary=128,256 and batch 1 then 64 generated a single full-vocabulary reduction kernel (~113 us), with unprofiled timings 161 -> 275 us. Repeating the sweep restored 163 -> 369 us; the percentage is not universal.

import ast
import gc
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import subprocess
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_utils as dflash
from sglang.srt.speculative import uno_utils as uno

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'benchmark-results.json'


def source_node(path, name):
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    node = next(n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
    return source, node


def load_base(path, names, module):
    namespace = dict(vars(module))
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    nodes = [n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names]
    assert len(nodes) == len(names)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), 'exec'), namespace)
    return namespace


def capture(fn):
    # Compilation and allocator warmup are outside the measured region.
    for _ in range(4):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        output = fn()
    for _ in range(10):
        graph.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    tensors = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)
    assert all(torch.isfinite(t).all().item() for t in tensors)
    probs = tensors[-1]
    assert torch.allclose(probs.sum(-1), torch.ones_like(probs.sum(-1)), atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
    return graph, output


def measure(graph, repetitions=200):
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(repetitions):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    end.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / repetitions


def main():
    base_dflash = load_base(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', {'build_speculative_verify_target_probs'}, dflash)
    base_uno = load_base(ROOT / 'base_uno_utils.py', {'_normalize_sparse_topk_probs', '_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'}, uno)
    for helper in ('_dflash_top_p_renorm_prob', '_dflash_top_k_renorm_prob'):
        _, before = source_node(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', helper)
        _, after = source_node(dflash.__file__, helper)
        assert ast.dump(before) == ast.dump(after), f'Dependency changed: {helper}'
    metadata = {
        'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03',
        'base': 'f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38',
        'torch': torch.__version__, 'cuda': torch.version.cuda,
        'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        'driver': subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi', '--query-gpu=driver_version', '--format=csv,noheader'], text=True).strip(),
        'packages': {p: importlib.metadata.version(p) for p in ('flashinfer-python', 'triton', 'transformers')},
        'method': 'Production head functions, exact base function ASTs with unchanged production dependencies; UNO torch.compile(dynamic=True) retained. CUDA Graph replay, warmup and compilation excluded, 5 paired samples alternating order, 200 replays/sample. Synthetic fixed-seed float32 logits, std=2; temperature=.8; top_k=50; draft_width=6.',
        'scope': 'Sampling function microbenchmark only. No model inference or end-to-end latency claim. Base/head intentionally implement different distributions.',
        'source_sha256': {str(p.name): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (ROOT/'base_dflash_utils.py', ROOT/'base_uno_utils.py', Path(dflash.__file__), Path(uno.__file__), Path(__file__))},
    }
    results = []
    cases = [(b, v, True) for v in (32768, 128256) for b in (1, 16, 64)] + [(16, 128256, False)]
    for bs, vocab, enabled in cases:
        torch.manual_seed(41916)
        width, k = 6, 50
        logits = torch.randn(bs * width, vocab, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32) * 2
        temperatures = torch.full((bs, 1), .8, device='cuda')
        top_ks = torch.full((bs,), k, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
        top_ps = torch.full((bs,), .9 if enabled else 1.0, device='cuda')
        info = SimpleNamespace(temperatures=temperatures, top_ks=top_ks, top_ps=top_ps, need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=enabled)
        for path in ('dflash_sparse', 'uno_compact'):
            print(json.dumps({'starting': path, 'batch': bs, 'vocab': vocab, 'top_p_enabled': enabled}), flush=True)
            if path == 'dflash_sparse':
                args = dict(next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=info, draft_token_num=width, bs=bs, max_top_k=k, uniform_top_k_value=k, use_sparse_topk=True)
                before = lambda: base_dflash['build_speculative_verify_target_probs'](**args)
                after = lambda: dflash.build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**args)
            else:
                args = (logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps, bs, width, k)
                before = lambda: base_uno['_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'](*args)
                after = lambda: uno._build_sparse_target_support_tensors(logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps if enabled else None, bs, width, k)
            bg, bo = capture(before)
            hg, ho = capture(after)
            samples = {'base': [], 'head': []}
            for round_id in range(5):
                pairs = [('base', bg), ('head', hg)] if round_id % 2 == 0 else [('head', hg), ('base', bg)]

            bm, hm = statistics.median(samples['base']), statistics.median(samples['head'])
            row = dict(path=path, batch=bs, vocab=vocab, top_p_enabled=enabled, base_us=bm, head_us=hm, delta_us=hm-bm, ratio=hm/bm, samples_us=samples)
            results.append(row)
            OUT.write_text(json.dumps({'metadata': metadata, 'results': results}, indent=2)+'\n')
            print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
            del bg, bo, hg, ho, before, after
            gc.collect()
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    print('BENCHMARK_COMPLETE', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import psutil
import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:31916'
RESULT = {'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03', 'model': json.loads((ROOT/'model.json').read_text()), 'checks': [], 'launches': []}


def save():
    (ROOT/'http-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(RESULT, indent=2)+'\n')


def request(min_p, stream, expected_rejection, label):
    payload = {'text': 'The capital of France is', 'sampling_params': {'temperature': .7, 'top_k': 50, 'top_p': .9, 'min_p': min_p, 'max_new_tokens': 8}, 'stream': stream}
    start = time.monotonic()
    response = requests.post(BASE_URL+'/generate', json=payload, timeout=(10, 60))
    duration = time.monotonic()-start
    body = response.text
    if expected_rejection:
        assert 'min_p is not supported with NGRAM speculative decoding' in body, (response.status_code, body)
        assert response.status_code in (200, 400, 422), response.status_code
        if stream:
            assert 'data:' in body or response.status_code != 200, body
    else:
        assert response.status_code == 200, (response.status_code, body)
        parsed = response.json()
        assert isinstance(parsed.get('text'), str), parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['completion_tokens'] > 0, parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['finish_reason']['type'] != 'abort', parsed
    RESULT['checks'].append({'label': label, 'request': payload, 'status_code': response.status_code, 'elapsed_seconds': duration, 'response': body, 'passed': True})
    save()
    print(json.dumps({'label':label, 'status':response.status_code, 'seconds':duration, 'passed':True}), flush=True)


def stop_server(process):
    try:
        children = psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True)
    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
        children = []
    try:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
    try:
        process.wait(timeout=45)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        process.wait(timeout=15)
    for child in children:
        try:
            if child.is_running(): child.terminate()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
            pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=15)
    for child in alive:
        try: child.kill()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess: pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(alive, timeout=15)
    assert not [p.pid for p in alive if p.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE], 'server children survived'


def run_server(speculative):
    label = 'ngram' if speculative else 'ordinary'
    cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'sglang.launch_server', '--model-path', str(ROOT/'model'), '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '31916', '--attention-backend', 'flashinfer', '--dtype', 'bfloat16', '--mem-fraction-static', '.5', '--max-running-requests', '8', '--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode', '8', '--context-length', '2048']
    if speculative:
        cmd += ['--speculative-algorithm', 'NGRAM', '--speculative-num-draft-tokens', '16']
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(ROOT/'source/python'), HF_HOME=str(ROOT/'hf'), HF_HUB_CACHE=str(ROOT/'hf/hub'), TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'inductor'), TRITON_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'triton'), SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE='0', SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE='auto', SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'sglang-cache'))
    with open(ROOT/f'server-{label}.log', 'w') as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, env=env, cwd=ROOT/'source', stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
        RESULT['launches'].append({'mode':label, 'command':cmd, 'pid':process.pid})
        save()
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic()+600
            while time.monotonic()<deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError(f'{label} server exited: {process.returncode}; see server-{label}.log')
                try:
                    if requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=2).status_code == 200:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    pass
                time.sleep(2)
            else:
                raise TimeoutError(f'{label} server startup exceeded 600 seconds')
            print(f'SERVER_READY {label}',flush=True)
            if speculative:
                request(0, False, False, 'ngram valid initial control')
                for iteration in range(2):
                    for stream in (False, True):
                        request(.1, stream, True, f'ngram reject min_p=.1 stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
                        request(0, False, False, f'ngram valid after rejection stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
            else:
                request(.1, False, False, 'ordinary accepts min_p=.1')
            assert requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=10).status_code == 200
            assert process.poll() is None
        finally:
            stop_server(process)
            RESULT['launches'][-1]['stopped'] = True
            save()


try:
    run_server(True)
    run_server(False)
    RESULT['complete'] = True
    print('HTTP_CHECK_COMPLETE',flush=True)
except Exception as exc:
    RESULT['error'] = repr(exc)
    raise
finally:
    save()

title: [PD] Fix crash for allocation when mamba + pd + decode radix cache
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

With Mamba/KDA, PD decode, and decode radix cache, [PD admission on `main`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py#L1373-L1387) checks whether **zero** Mamba slots are free. It does not evict cached states when one slot is free, even though a fresh request needs **three** slots with overlap scheduling: one live state and [two tracking buffers](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1450-L1471). The [buffer allocation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1599-L1613) then asserts and exits the decode worker.

```text
Fresh request: 1 free slot, cached states are evictable
  -> PD admission sees free > 0 and skips eviction
  -> request row and live Mamba state allocate (1 -> 0 free)
  -> two tracking buffers cannot allocate
  -> AssertionError: Not enough space for mamba ping pong idx
```

## What?

- Extract `ensure_mamba_capacity` from the [combined-engine allocation logic on `main`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a9c97c9f6973c03e778d1fe1e63a6b9f58a55012/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocation.py#L300-L323). It counts the live state and tracking slots each request still needs, evicts enough cached states to cover any shortfall, then rechecks capacity.
- Use that check before PD decode preallocation and before resuming a retracted request. If capacity is still short, leave the request queued rather than partially allocating it.
- Keep combined serving's existing behavior: attempt eviction, then let its allocator run. Only PD uses the capacity check to defer a request.

## Verification?

On one H200 node, two GPUs ran the tiny Kimi Linear model with real weights, NIXL PD, decode radix cache, overlap scheduling, and 16 sequential distinct requests (257 input / 256 output tokens each):

```text
Unpatched, 5 Mamba slots: 3 requests complete; request 4 crashes
                         at 2 free + 3 evictable slots
Patched,   5 Mamba slots: all 16 complete
Unpatched, 128 slots:     all 16 complete (capacity control)
Patched, repeated prompt: request completes with 256 cached tokens
```

Relevant traceback, with framework wrappers omitted:

```text
DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated
  -> DecodePreallocQueue._pre_alloc          (decode.py:2075)
  -> HybridReqToTokenPool.alloc              (memory_pool.py:1471)
  -> HybridReqToTokenPool._alloc_ping_pong_buffer
  -> AssertionError: Not enough space for mamba ping pong idx
```

## Test?

- On the current source tree, pinned isort `7.0.0`, Ruff `0.15.1` selected checks and formatter, Python syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass.
- On the original pinned source (`7b079c9c26`), the Mamba-capacity and decode-queue tests passed: **13 passed, 3 subtests passed** on H200. The end-to-end H200 comparison above also used that source, before the per-request sizing refinement.

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] Fix shared-expert fusion accuracy and speed up MoE routing on ROCm
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Two MoE fixes for DSV4.1-Flash When running it with `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` on ROCm.
1) Issue: Resolve the shared-expert requant accuracy lost
2) Perf opt: Fused decode routing kernels into one.

## Modifications

- On ROCm, requantize the FP8 shared expert to MXFP4 with round-to-nearest-even (aiter `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` scaling). The old cast rounded midpoints toward zero, which shrank the shared expert by ~5%. Other platforms keep the existing requant (output unchanged).
- `rocm_router_gate` now writes the fused shared-expert columns in the same launch, so decode no longer falls back to reduce + topk + append.
- Use aiter's multi-phase MoE sorting for small batches via `SGLANG_AITER_MOE_SORTING_DISPATCH_POLICY` (default 2; 0 restores aiter's auto policy).
- Update the requant unit test and add `test_rocm_router_gate.py` cases.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K 1319 5-shot, TP2 with fusion: 0.891 -> 0.906 (3 runs), matching unfused (0.904 / 0.905). With the router change: 0.897 / 0.901 / 0.900.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X TP2 + DSpark, per decode step: router -0.41 ms, sorting -0.13 ms.
AgentX: c1 11,371.9 tok/s/GPU, P90 349.5 (+2.6% / +4.8%); c2 11,819.8, P90 324.6 (+2.8% / +10.7%).

title: [Spec] Fix wrong tokens from compact-verify CUDA graphs when a token tier is captured more than once
author: ormandj
body:
## Motivation

With compact ragged verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`), `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` captures a token tier more than once when there are several attention graph variants (for example the DSv4.1 candidate graphs `candidate_unfiltered` / `candidate_filtered`) or several PD-mux streams. Each capture calls `_capture_ragged_verify_layout`, which allocated a new `RaggedVerifyLayout` and replaced `_captured_ragged_layouts[num_tokens]`. At replay, `_stage_ragged_verify_layout` copies the live `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` only into that registered layout, which belongs to the last capture. Graphs from the earlier captures still read the layout they were captured with. That layout holds synthetic capture offsets, and replay no longer refreshes it.

A graph that reads an earlier capture's layout tensors directly computes with the wrong offsets whenever the live layout differs from the capture-time one. On current main, PD-mux with the TRT-LLM MLA backend is exposed: its ragged verify path pads and unpads queries with the captured `verify_lens` / `qo_indptr` inside the graph. For DSv4.1 target verify on current main the defect is latent, because its backend copies the live layout into its own buffers outside the graph. The ragged Engram hashing and `token_req_indices` in #40567 read `qo_indptr` inside the DSv4.1 verify graph; with them, the `candidate_unfiltered` graphs map tokens to the wrong requests.

I measured an A/B on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, DSpark gamma 5, compact verify, #40567 applied) with an earlier revision of this fix, which copied the live layout into each capture instead of sharing one layout per tier. I compared the log-prob of each generated token with a plain prefill of the same text:

- Without the fix, per-token differences reached 14.4 nats. At temperature 1, 9 of 32 streams looped to the length cap.
- With the fix, the maximum difference was 0.79-0.86 nats, and none of the 32 streams looped or hit the cap.

Eager verify was correct in both builds.

## Modifications

`_capture_ragged_verify_layout` creates the layout once per token tier and returns the same object for later captures of that tier. Every graph of the tier now captures the tensors that replay refreshes.

## Accuracy Tests

- `TestRaggedVerifyLayoutPerTier` (CPU, `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) calls the capture-layout helper twice for tier 24 with two variant labels, stages a live layout, and checks both returned layouts' `qo_indptr_device` / `verify_lens` against the live padded layout. On main the first layout keeps its synthetic offsets (7 of 9 `qo_indptr` entries differ).
- The end-to-end A/B in Motivation (earlier revision of the fix).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The replay staging code is unchanged; capture reuses one registered layout per token tier across attention variants and PD-mux streams.

title: [Fix] model_loader: Avoid unsafe pickle fallback when loading PyTorch checkpoints
author: nguyendvk
body:
## Motivation

`torch.load(weights_only=False)` deserializes with pickle, so a crafted checkpoint can execute code when it is loaded. `_load_pt_file` fell back to it for legacy tar checkpoints, and several loaders called `torch.load` on model files without `weights_only=True`. This is the same class of issue as #35653 (RIFE) and is consistent with the contribution guide's rule against unpickling untrusted data.

## Modifications

- Remove the `weights_only=False` fallback in `_load_pt_file` (`srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py` and `multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/weight_utils.py`). Legacy tar checkpoints now fail with torch's own error and should be converted to safetensors or a zip-format `.pt` offline.
- Pass `weights_only=True` to `torch.load` in `deepseek_ocr.py` (x2), `roberta.py` and `rife_interpolator.py`.
- Add unit tests for `_load_pt_file`: a tensor state dict still loads, and a pickle payload is not executed.
- `srt/debug_utils` is unchanged: it reads developer-written tensor dumps, not model weights.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: only the checkpoint deserialization path changes; no model forward code is touched.

title: [AMD][Fix] Saturate FP8 KV commits instead of reproducing e4m3fnuz NaN overflow
author: michaelzhang-ai
body:
## Motivation

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` has been red on `main` since #40785 merged. Every run that has executed the job since has failed identically — #40785's own run, two on #34537, and one on an unrelated branch, all reporting `30732 / 65536` mismatched elements at the same index. The job only runs when a PR touches `python/sglang/kernels/`, so most PRs skip it and it went unnoticed.

Full evidence in #42981.

## Modifications

torch's `float8_e4m3fn` cast saturates to its max finite value. `float8_e4m3fnuz` has no infinity, so `fp8e4m3fnuz_from_fp32_value` returns NaN (`0x80`) for every magnitude at or above 256.0. Triton's cast saturates on both types, so the fused commit kernel from #40785 matches eager on CUDA and diverges on gfx94x.

This is not only a test problem. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` has a fused path and an eager fallback, and on ROCm they now write different bytes for the same input — the fallback writes NaN into a committed KV slot, which poisons attention for that slot on every later read.

Rather than have the test chase whichever cast runs, this makes saturation the defined contract and clamps before the FP8 cast in all three places:

- `cache_move.py` — the kernel clamps, with the limit passed as a `tl.constexpr`; NaN falls through both `tl.where` arms. Two vector ops added to a memory-bound kernel.
- `memory_pool.py` — the eager fallback clamps identically, so the two production paths agree.
- `test/kernels/prefix_valid.py` — the shared oracle clamps identically.

The limit is `torch.finfo(fp8).max`, not the conservative `fp8_max` constant (224.0 on fnuz): clamping at 224.0 would pull values that eager rounds to 240.0 down a step.

All three are no-ops on CUDA, where the eager cast already saturates to 448.

## Test plan

`jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` on MI300 / ROCm 10: **42/42 files passed** ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37648241557/job/113082433719)), including `test_prefix_valid_fp8.py` and `test_prefix_valid_fp8_pool.py`. For reference, the same job on current `main` fails at 6/42 with 30732/65536 mismatched elements.

An earlier revision of this branch clamped in FP32, which turned the `bf16/fp16 -> fp8` cast into `fp32 -> fp8`; those lower to different conversions and left 2/65536 elements off by one FP8 subnormal step at fp16 with a host scalar scale. Clamping in the source dtype restores the original lowering, and that is the version here.

Still red on this PR, all reproducing on #40785 or unrelated to this path:

- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd (7)` — MiniMax sparse decode kernel requests 128 KiB LDS against a 64 KiB limit (`OutOfResources`), same partition red on #40785.
- `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (1)` — red on #40785.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` — `test_e2e_spec_eagle.py`; the server stops responding mid-stream (`RemoteDisconnected`), with no CUDA/HIP fault, scheduler exception or OOM in the log. That test runs `kv_cache_dtype=auto`, so `self.dtype` is not FP8 and neither the fused branch nor the eager clamp in this PR is reached — the non-FP8 commit path goes through `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled`, which is untouched here. The same job is also red on #40785, on a different test.
- NPU jobs — `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` returns early for non-CUDA/non-HIP before reaching any line this PR touches.

If you would rather the kernel reproduce eager's `e4m3fnuz` NaN-on-overflow instead of saturating, I can invert the patch — but that writes NaN into the KV cache on AMD and diverges from the CUDA path, so saturation looks like the better contract.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] Fix DP attention + TP MoE decode NaN and support bounded replay
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

With DP attention and a TP MoE, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode on MI355X produced NaN in the MoE output under CUDA graph and crashed after a few minutes, and decoder SWA bounded replay was rejected for every DP attention layout. This PR fixes the crash and enables bounded replay for DP attention + TP MoE.

## Modifications

- Stage the aiter custom all-gather / reduce-scatter inputs through the pre-registered IPC pool during CUDA graph capture, so peers no longer read stale graph-pool data on replay (`SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN`, default 0; set 1 for DSv4.1 DP attention + TP MoE).
- For DP attention + TP MoE, write the real per-rank token count before every decode replay and zero the pad rows before the DP gather (`SGLANG_DP_MASK_PAD_ROWS`, default true, ROCm only).
- On ROCm, allow `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` with DP attention when the MoE is TP (`moe_a2a_backend none`) and attention TP is 1. Eager forwards all-gather each rank's late-layer row count and switch the DP gather sizes to it for the late layers.
- CUDA behaviour is unchanged: all of the above is gated to ROCm.

GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, DSv4.1-Flash TP2 DP2 TP-MoE + DSpark: 0.896 (TP2 without DP attention: 0.894-0.906).
