title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output for non-sliding-window models on the vectorized_5d KV layout
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

On the AITER backend, the SHUFFLE 5D KV layout (`SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) silently produces garbage output for every model without sliding-window attention: decode reads the wrong KV pages and nothing reports an error. GSM8K on Qwen3-14B-FP8 drops from 0.885 to 0.000 on MI325X. This has been the case since the layout was added in #27063. Setting `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` works around it today.

Root cause: `forward_decode_vectorized_5d` passes `forward_metadata.kv_indices` to `pa_decode_gluon` as its `block_tables`, a 2-D `(bs, max_num_blocks_per_seq)` table of page ids, and its docstring says the same ("Full-attn → `kv_indices` page table"). But the decode metadata only builds that table on the unified-attention branch:

```python
if not self.use_triton_unified_attention:
    # flat per-token kv_indices, addressed through kv_indptr
    create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton[(bs,)](...)
else:
    # 2-D page table
    ...
```

`use_triton_unified_attention` is forced on for sliding-window models, which is why gpt-oss (the model the 5D path was added for in #27063) is unaffected. Every other model leaves it off by default, so `pa_decode_gluon` reads token ids as page ids with a row stride of 1. The eager path, the CUDA-graph page-table buffer and CUDA-graph capture/replay all make the same choice.

## Modifications

The decode metadata format and the decode kernel are separate choices, so this PR names the former explicitly:

```python
self.decode_uses_page_table = (
    self.use_triton_unified_attention or self.kv_cache_is_vectorized_5d
)
```

and uses it at the five sites that decide between the flat indices and the page table: the eager decode path (plain and speculative), the CUDA-graph page-table buffer allocation, and both checks in `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` (shared by capture and replay).

`use_triton_unified_attention` itself is unchanged. The 5D layout already has dedicated KV-write, extend and decode branches, so the only things the flag still controls for it are the metadata format and the target-verify kernel choice (`_use_unified_verify`). Forcing the flag on would also switch the verify kernel, which is outside this fix. The NHD layout is unaffected: `decode_uses_page_table` equals `use_triton_unified_attention` there.

Tests: `test/registered/amd/test_aiter_vectorized_5d_decode.py` launches the CI default model (`meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, dense, no sliding window) with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the 5D layout and `--page-size 64`, and runs GSM8K. Registered in `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`.

The branch is rebased onto `main` @ `e45cbce599` without conflicts.

## Accuracy Tests

### MI325X (gfx942)

MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.7.0, AITER `c16d44b93`. This image ships a `sgl-kernel` that current `main` does not run against, so these runs use the image's sglang (`dc6b5d1f5a`, 2026-09-04), with and without this patch, which applies to it unchanged.

Qwen3-14B-FP8, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, CUDA graph on, GSM8K 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy, one server at a time:

| Config | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| NHD layout, `--page-size 1` | 0.870 |
| NHD layout, `--page-size 64` | 0.885 |
| 5D layout | **0.000** |
| This PR, 5D layout | 0.890 |
| 5D layout + `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` | 0.890 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change on the NHD layout. On the 5D layout the fixed path builds the same page table as the unified-attention path.

Long-context serving on MI325X, same setup as the gfx942 accuracy table: `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, 3 × concurrency prompts after a warmup of one concurrency's worth:

| Config | c=64 output tok/s | c=64 mean TPOT (ms) | c=128 output tok/s | c=128 mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NHD layout, `--page-size 1` | 351.9 | 133.0 | 389.2 | 190.7 |
| NHD layout, `--page-size 64` | 349.0 | 133.3 | 383.6 | 194.5 |
| This PR, 5D layout | 358.9 | 128.6 | 395.2 | 186.2 |
| 5D layout + `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` | 358.0 | 128.9 | 392.1 | 187.4 |

At the same page size, the 5D layout lowers mean TPOT by 3.5% (c=64) and 4.3% (c=128) on this dense model. The runs are prefill-heavy (mean TTFT is about 50 s at c=64 and 110 s at c=128 for every config), so these numbers are about the decode side only.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Scheduler] Fix the deterministic-inference hang when a prefill chunk is shorter than its alignment
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Deterministic inference truncates each prefill chunk to a multiple of an alignment (4096 by default). A per-rank chunk below it, from `--chunked-prefill-size` < 4096 or from DP attention splitting the chunk across ranks, truncated every chunk to zero tokens, so a prompt longer than the chunk waited in the queue forever
- Triton: drop the alignment; `align_window_kv_to_tiles` pads each sliding-window KV list to an absolute multiple of 128, so a chunked prefill sums keys in the same tiles as an unchunked one (built once per forward, deterministic inference only; the attention kernel is unchanged)
- Flashinfer and the DSA kpool alignment: a per-rank chunk shorter than the alignment fails at startup instead of hanging; decode servers are exempt
- Deprecate `SGLANG_TRITON_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_ALIGN_SIZE`
- Add `test_deterministic_chunk_align.py` and a chunked-vs-unchunked sliding-window case in `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`

No behavior change without deterministic inference. With it, triton prefill chunks are no longer aligned (chunked and unchunked outputs stay bitwise equal), and flashinfer configurations that used to hang now fail at startup.

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Prevent scheduler crash and has_audio_understanding misreport for audio-declaring models without an audio tower
author: enternal111
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43864

An audio request sent to a model whose multimodal processor defines an audio token but has no audio tower - e.g. `gemma-4-31B-it`, a non-audio variant of the Gemma 4 family whose `config.json` ships `audio_config: null` - is not rejected at the API layer. It reaches the scheduler, where `get_audio_feature()` raises inside `model.forward`, and the whole scheduler process dies.

Two underlying problems, both fixed here:

1. Request validation only checks `is_multimodal`, not per-modality capability, so the audio request passes tokenization/dispatch and fails deep in the scheduler, killing the scheduler process.
2. `ModelConfig.is_audio_understandable_model` used `hasattr(hf_config, "audio_config")`. Because the config key is present with a `null` value, `hasattr` is `True` even though no audio tower exists, and the model is misreported as audio-capable (`/get_model_info`: `has_audio_understanding: true` for `gemma-4-31B-it`).

Scope:

- The crash (problem 1) affects only models whose processor defines an audio token while the model has no audio tower. For all other models the audio never reaches the scheduler: models whose processor defines no audio token drop it in the processor, and text-only LLMs have no multimodal processor at all.
- The misreport (problem 2) is a config-level issue: it affects any model whose `config.json` carries `audio_config` with a `null` value.
- Existing behavior is otherwise unchanged: for models whose processor defines no audio token, requests are handled exactly as before (verified on `glm-5.3-flash`, see Production verification). The only intentional exception is the corner case noted under Limitations.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`: `is_audio_understandable_model` now requires `audio_config` to be present and non-`None` (top-level and under `thinker_config`) instead of `hasattr`. This makes the capability flag - and the `/get_model_info` report - correct for models with a `null` audio config.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py` (`_tokenize_one_request`): reject with a per-request error when a request carries audio data, the model's multimodal processor defines an audio token, and the top-level audio_config is present but explicitly None (audio tower disabled), return 400 with :

  ```
  Audio inputs are not supported by <served_model_name>
  ```
  Limitations:
  - Audio only; the same shape of problem could exist for other modalities but is out of scope here.
  - Corner case : on the native `/generate` path, a request that passes valid `audio_data` for a model whose processor defines an audio token but which has no audio tower, while the prompt carries no audio placeholder, used to succeed (the base processor drops the surplus audio with a warning); it is now rejected with the same 400 error. The OpenAI path is unaffected - it always inserts the placeholder, and those requests previously crashed the scheduler. We keep the broader guard because an explicit error is preferable to silently discarding user-provided audio.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output path is changed (the guard rejects requests that would otherwise crash the engine; the config-flag change only corrects a misreported capability), and existing behavior for models whose processor defines no audio token is preserved. 

Verified on `gemma-4-31B-it` (4x H20): an audio request now returns a clean per-request error instead of killing the scheduler, and the engine keeps serving:

```json
{"object":"error","message":"Audio inputs are not supported by gemma-4-31B-it","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

Existing behavior also verified on `glm-5.3-flash` (whose processor defines no audio token): an audio request still returns 200 exactly as before this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - no change to the forward path; the only addition is a lightweight per-request validation at tokenization time.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) - N/A: the Gemma 4 cookbook page already documents which variants support audio; no doc change needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) - N/A: no model-output or performance change (see above).

title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort held decode requests, and read live requests from the lists
author: hnyls2002
body:
With every live request in a list (`Scheduler.request_lists()`), a few places that walk their own subset of queues and batches either miss requests or repeat the list of holders. This makes them read the lists, and lets an abort reach the one list it skipped.

- `abort_request` also aborts a PD decode request held for rebootstrap while generation is paused (`DecodePreallocQueue.held_rebootstrap_reqs`). Such a request holds no KV and no step uses it, so it finishes and is released at once. `DecodePreallocQueue.take_aborted` now removes the retracted and held requests an abort matches; the scheduler only releases them.
- `_has_active_sampling_mask_request` reads every list instead of its own set of batches and queues. It now also sees requests in the PD prefill bootstrap and transfer queues, launched prefills, the dLLM queue, PD decode requests releasing their KV, HiSparse staging and parked uOCR windows.
- `is_fully_idle` reads the request part of each variant (default, health check, `ignore_waiting`) from the lists. Its result is unchanged: the default counts every list except the ones counted elsewhere or deliberately left out (running and launched prefills through the batches, dLLM through its staging check, held decode requests, parked uOCR windows through `blocks_flush`, finished deferred responses); the health check counts chunked, waiting and, unless paused, retracted decode requests, as before.

Behavior changes: the held-request abort, and the sampling-mask check covering more lists.

## Test plan
- A held-request abort during a retract pause finishes only the matching request, and resume enqueues the rest.
- The unit tests this PR touches pass locally with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1`, apart from failures main has too.

title: [Fix] hisparse: Release HiSparse rows on the KV checksum mismatch and chunked abort exits
author: hnyls2002
body:
Two exits free a request's KV with `release_kv_cache` without releasing its HiSparse state first, so the rows leak. Both now call `hisparse_coordinator.request_finished` before the KV free, under the same `enable_hisparse` guard as the other exits.

- PD decode KV checksum mismatch (`_handle_kv_checksum_mismatch`): the transfer has already admitted the request into HiSparse, so its host pages and device buffer were never returned.
- Chunked prefill abort (`process_pending_chunked_abort`): a request aborted between chunks holds only the spec scratch row its extend allocated; `request_finished` frees exactly that (its no-device-buffer branch), and the prefill KV is still freed by `release_kv_cache`.

No change without `--enable-hisparse`. No stream wait is added or moved; `request_finished` keeps its own wait on the forward stream, as at the other exits.

## Test plan
- One unit test per exit checks that the HiSparse release runs, and runs before the KV free; both fail without the fix.
- `/rerun-test` on this head:
  - `test_hisparse_unit.py` (1-gpu-5090): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746839763)
  - `test_disaggregation_hisparse.py` (8-gpu-h200, PD + HiSparse, DeepSeek-V4-Flash): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746854792)
  - `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` (8-gpu-b200, HiSparse + speculative decoding): passed, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746870316)
  - `test_kv_checksum.py` (1-gpu-h100): queued, [run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41746823280)

title: [Fix] srt: Apply --gc-threshold in every server process and freeze every tokenizer worker
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

`--gc-threshold` is applied with `gc.set_threshold` in the launching process only. The scheduler and detokenizer subprocesses keep Python's default thresholds, so a deployment that raised the gen2 threshold to stop periodic full collections still sees them in the scheduler, where they cost the most.

The post-warmup `/freeze_gc` request freezes the scheduler and detokenizer, but with `--tokenizer-worker-num` greater than one it is served by whichever tokenizer worker receives it, so only that worker's interpreter is frozen. The other workers keep scanning their long-lived heap on every collection.

Defaults are unchanged: with no `--gc-threshold` nothing new is set, and the single-tokenizer path still freezes exactly where it did.

## Modifications

- `freeze_gc` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) takes an optional `gc_threshold` and applies it with `gc.set_threshold` before `gc.freeze()`; `None` leaves the thresholds alone.
- `FreezeGCReq` carries `gc_threshold: Optional[List[int]] = None`. `TokenizerManager.freeze_gc` reads the configured threshold off the device args, sends it with the request, and passes it to its own local freeze; the scheduler and detokenizer handlers pass `recv_req.gc_threshold` through.
- `_wait_and_warmup` (`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`) gains `post_warmup_callback`, run after warmup and before the routed `/freeze_gc` request. In multi-tokenizer mode each worker's warmup thread gets a callback that freezes that worker's interpreter with the configured threshold, so every worker freezes locally and the routed request still covers the scheduler and detokenizer.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution or outputs. Only garbage-collector thresholds and freeze points move, and only in the processes that were previously skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable as a benchmark: the change removes recurring gen2 collections from the scheduler and the extra tokenizer workers when a threshold is configured, and is a no-op otherwise.

Unit tests on this head (CPU, `pytest`): `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py` and `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`, 37 passed. New cases: `freeze_gc` preserves the thresholds without a configuration and applies a configured one; each tokenizer worker freezes locally with the configured threshold after warmup and before the routed request.

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Fix the first-step denoise regression from compiling ENABLE_CK=0 BF16 attention
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
With `ENABLE_CK=0`, `AITerImpl.forward` calls `aiter.flash_attn_func` inside `torch.compile`. That dispatch opens a Triton config JSON and builds a Triton kernel Dynamo cannot reconstruct. The graph break is inside the DiT block loop, so Dynamo skips `Flux2Transformer2DModel.forward` on the first real step.

**Where it shows up**
gfx1250 already takes `AITerImpl._forward_bf16_eager`, which is `@torch.compiler.disable`, because FlyDSL's Python JIT is not traceable. gfx950 with CK enabled stays on `FlashAttnFunc` and is unchanged. The failure shows up on MI355 when the process sets `ENABLE_CK=0`, including the FLUX.2 720p run: the scored denoise's first step takes 11.8s retracing, then the rest of the steps run at 2.02 it/s. The profiled CK GEMMs and the Triton attention kernel match the previous image.

**Why #44671 did not cover it**
#44671 split the BF16 call into `_forward_bf16` (compiled) and `_forward_bf16_eager` (`@torch.compiler.disable`), and sent only `USE_AITER_GFX1250` to the eager helper. It kept gfx942/gfx950 compiled on the grounds that FlyDSL returns `None` there and the call falls through to the CK `@compile_ops` kernels, which Dynamo records as opaque graph nodes. That holds only while `ENABLE_CK=1`. With `ENABLE_CK=0`, gfx950 falls through FlyDSL into `aiter.ops.triton.attention.mha.flash_attn_func` instead, which Dynamo cannot trace, and `_forward_bf16` still calls it inside the compiled graph.

**How to fix**
Call `_forward_bf16_eager` whenever `ENABLE_CK` is off, so the untraceable Triton attention stays outside Dynamo and the rest of the compiled forward remains.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: `AITerImpl.forward` uses the eager BF16 path when `USE_AITER_GFX1250` is true or `aiter.jit.core.ENABLE_CK` is false. `ENABLE_CK=1` on gfx950 still calls `_forward_bf16` from inside the compiled graph.
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py`: compile `AITerImpl.forward` and assert `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` is false for gfx1250 and for `ENABLE_CK=0`, and true for the CK path.

## Accuracy Tests

The eager path calls the same `aiter.flash_attn_func` with the same arguments. The unit test checks that the compiled forward returns the attention output unchanged (`torch.testing.assert_close` against the fake kernel's `q.clone()`). No weight, scale, or kernel-config change.

`PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_aiter_attention_impl.py` — 8 passed.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Kernel time for the profiled FLUX.2 transformer forwards is not the regression. Oct 6 image total kernel time 1.512s, Oct 21 image 1.481s. The two largest CK GEMMs stay on the same tiles (`MT192x320` ~628ms, `MT256x208` ~310ms, 288 calls each).

The denoise wall gap is the first scored step. After that step the Oct 21 run holds 2.02 it/s, in line with the Oct 6 steady rate. This change removes that retrace. An after-fix end-to-end FLUX.2 number is not in this branch yet.

title: [Fix] logits: Preserve lm_head precision with shared buffers
author: YAMY1234
body:
A matching FP32 logits buffer currently makes the ordinary FP16/BF16 lm_head produce FP32 GEMM output even when FP32 lm_head is disabled. Introduced by #45631, this skips the rounding used by the unbuffered prefill-scoring path and LoRA-wrapped heads.

Restrict the direct FP32 buffer write to heads that explicitly enable FP32. Default heads again compute in their original dtype before copying into the shared buffer. Explicit FP32 and MuseSpark's existing FP32 override retain direct buffer writes.

Add buffered/unbuffered equality coverage for FP16 and BF16, check direct writes for explicit FP32, and exercise CUDA graph replay with FP32 enabled and disabled. Low-precision test references now use the normal dtype GEMM instead of an FP64 result rounded afterward, which can differ by one output ULP. Existing tolerances are unchanged.

Related: #45846. This is intended to address the DSpark decode/prefill logprob mismatch and the contemporaneous LoRA/UNO parity failures; end-to-end confirmation is pending.

Validation:
- Changed-file Ruff, Ruff format, isort, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` pass.
- A local CPU control-flow check with emulated CUDA FP32 output reproduces the buffer-dependent rounding change before the fix and removes it afterward. This does not validate CUDA kernels or graph replay.
- GPU validation submitted for `9a9c369051`: [lm_head / RTX 5090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39822486281) and [DSpark logprob, dynamic LoRA update, UNO parity / H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39822512516). Results pending; keeping this PR as a draft.

title: [Fix] comfyui: Reject conditioning kwargs the SGLD adapters silently drop
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Summary

ComfyUI's native `QwenImageTransformer2DModel.forward` passes `attention_mask`, `additional_t_cond` and (via `**kwargs`) `ref_latents_method`. `QwenImageEditAdapter.pack()` in `apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/executors/qwen_image.py` caught all three in `**kwargs` and never forwarded them: the request sent to the SGLD worker was identical whether or not these were set, so a workflow using them silently ran with the worker's hardcoded defaults instead (the worker's `QwenImagePipeline` fixes `zero_cond_t` per checkpoint at load, and always applies reference latents the way native ComfyUI's default `ref_latents_method="index"` does).

`ZImageAdapter.pack()` (Lumina2 / Z-Image) has the same gap for Z-Image Omni's `siglip_feats` / `ref_contexts` (multi-reference conditioning): the worker's `ZImagePipeline` has no path for either, so a reference-image workflow would silently produce a plain text-to-image result.

This is the same failure mode #43404 fixed for `FluxAdapter`'s `ref_latents`/`control`: instead of a silent wrong result, both `pack()` methods now raise a clear `ValueError`.

I checked native ComfyUI source (`comfy/ldm/qwen_image/model.py`, `comfy/ldm/lumina/model.py`, `comfy/model_base.py`) before picking which kwargs to reject:
- `ref_latents_method` defaults to `"index"` (`self.default_ref_method`); the worker only supports that mode, so only a non-default value (`"index_timestep_zero"`, `"negative_index"`) is rejected.
- `attention_mask` / `additional_t_cond` for Qwen-Image are both genuinely conditional in `QwenImage.extra_conds` (only set when meaningful), so rejecting any non-`None` value cannot false-positive on an ordinary workflow.
- For Z-Image, I deliberately did **not** reject `num_tokens` or `attention_mask`: `Lumina2.extra_conds` sends `num_tokens` on every call (derived from the text context length), and native ComfyUI's own `patchify_and_embed` discards `attention_mask`'s effect regardless, so dropping either already matches native behavior exactly. Only `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts` (confirmed to arrive only when a reference image is actually wired in) are a real silent-drop bug there.

## Test plan

Extended `test/unit/test_comfyui_adapters.py` (reusing its existing `_qwen_image_edit_adapter()` ComfyUI-stub helper):
- `test_qwen_image_edit_pack_rejects_unsupported_kwargs`: asserts `ValueError` for `attention_mask`, `additional_t_cond`, and `ref_latents_method="negative_index"`; asserts the default method and no extra kwargs still pack successfully.
- `test_zimage_pack_rejects_omni_reference_conditioning`: asserts `ValueError` for `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts`; asserts `num_tokens`/`attention_mask` (sent on every real call) and absent `siglip_feats`/`ref_contexts` still pack successfully.

The full `sglang` package is too heavy to install for a CPU-only check of this isolated fix, so I verified the exact same logic against the modified source files directly (stubbing only the ComfyUI-side imports, the same technique the existing test file already uses) on Modal CPU: 9/9 checks pass, including regression checks that unchanged default-arg behavior (no new kwargs passed) is unaffected for both adapters.

No GPU run: this is pure Python kwarg validation in `pack()`, no model weights or worker round-trip involved.

title: [Fix] rust-server: End a native /generate stream on a scheduler abort frame, as Python does
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

When the scheduler aborts a request with an error status (a disaggregated decode whose KV transfer failed, a request whose `logprob_start_len` lies past the prompt, ...), the Python server and the Rust frontend answer a native `/generate` **stream** differently.

Python's `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason` yields the abort as a normal terminal frame: the output so far, the request's counts, `e2e_latency`, and `meta_info.finish_reason` `{type: "abort", message, status_code, err_type}`, followed by `[DONE]`. Only a non-streaming request turns that abort into an HTTP status.

The Rust frontend turned the same scheduler frame into a bare `{"error": {"message", "code"}}` item on the stream and dropped the frame. A client, router or proxy that classifies an in-band error item by its code then reads a 429/503 abort as "overloaded" in Rust mode where Python reports a finished request with an abort reason. The abort message also named the request by the suffixed rid this server hands the scheduler (`Rid::from_client`), not by the rid the client sent, so the message leaked a request-id suffix the client never saw.

This PR makes a native Rust stream end on the abort's frame, as Python's does, and names the request in the abort message by the client's own rid. Non-streaming responses are unchanged.

## Modifications

- **`core/error.rs`**: `CoreError::RuntimeRejected` now carries the request's terminal `CoreOutput` (boxed; finish reason and counts included). `from_runtime_rejection` takes it, and a new `into_rejected_output` hands it back for the one surface that reports the abort as an output: a native `/generate` stream. Any other `CoreError` comes back as is.
- **`core/handle.rs`**: `generation_event` passes the scheduler's terminal output into the rejection. `RuntimeCall::recv` / `try_recv` run the terminal item through a new `name_client_rid`, which strips this server's rid suffix from the abort message so the message names the request as the client does. The message may hold the rid raw (`{rid}`) or as Python's `repr` (`{rid=}`, `{rid!r}`); the suffix is ASCII hex after `#`, so dropping it leaves the client's rid in whatever form the scheduler wrote, including `repr`'s escaping and quoting.
- **`http/native_api.rs`**: `generation_event_stream` maps every event through `stream_event`, which turns a `Failed` whose error is a scheduler rejection back into `Finished(output)`. The stream then ends on the usual terminal frame (`meta_info.finish_reason` is the abort, `e2e_latency` is set) and `[DONE]`. Unary responses, batch unary items, the OpenAI surfaces and gRPC still answer with the abort's status and message, matching Python's unary path and its OpenAI stream.
- **`message/finish_reason.rs`**: `FinishReason::replace_in_abort_message` rewrites a substring of an abort's message and leaves any other reason alone.
- **`grpc/native_api.rs`**: the error-mapping test fixtures gain the new field.

This deliberately replaces `scheduler_rejection_preserves_legacy_http_status`, which pinned the error-item shape on a native stream, with `scheduler_abort_ends_a_stream_on_a_frame_and_fails_unary`: Python is the reference for the native `/generate` surface, and Python has always ended a stream on the abort frame (see `_handle_abort_finish_reason`, which only raises when `is_stream` is false). The legacy status is still preserved; it now reaches a unary client as a status and a streaming client inside `finish_reason.status_code`, as it does from Python.

Tests:

- `scheduler_abort_ends_a_stream_on_a_frame_and_fails_unary` (`http/native_api.rs`): a stream that already sent a frame ends on the abort frame (`text` so far, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, the abort as `finish_reason`, `e2e_latency` set, no `error` item), then `[DONE]`; the same abort on a unary call answers the abort's status with `error.code` and `error.message`.
- `status_abort_names_the_client_rid` (`core/handle.rs`): a status abort fails the call with that status and keeps the terminal output, and the message names the client's rid for raw and `repr` forms, including rids with backslashes, newlines and quotes.
- `from_runtime_rejection` status mapping and the gRPC code mapping tests updated for the new field.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes; generated tokens are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The change adds one boxed output to a rejection error and one substring check per terminal item.

## Testing

- `rust/`: `cargo fmt -p sglang-server -- --check` passes; `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` passes, including the two tests above; `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage output with an fp8 KV cache and calibrated KV scales
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

With `--attention-backend aiter` (the default for MHA models on ROCm) and an fp8 KV cache, a checkpoint that ships calibrated KV scales produces garbage output: GSM8K drops to 0.

No flag is needed to hit it. With the default `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `configure_kv_cache_dtype` turns on the fp8 KV cache whenever the checkpoint's quant config declares one (compressed-tensors `kv_cache_scheme`, ModelOpt `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`) and loads its scales, e.g. `nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV`. Checkpoints that do not declare it, such as `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` (per-layer `kv_scale` ≈ 0.025) or the Quark `amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8`, hit it with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, which is how they are meant to be served.

The KV cache itself is written correctly (`K / k_scale`); three attention call sites misuse the scales:

- **default decode (`paged_attention_ragged`)**, the decode kernel for MHA models without a sliding window: the backend-wide unit scales are passed instead of the layer's k/v scales, so the cache is never dequantized.
- **unified-attention decode (`unified_attention`)**, used for sliding-window models such as gpt-oss and with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`: q is quantized with `k_scale`, a scale calibrated for K, not q.
- **NHD prefill (`mha_batch_prefill_func`)**, used on gfx942, and on gfx950 where the HD128 ASM prefill does not apply (e.g. head_dim 64): q is cast to fp8 unscaled, but the KV cache `k_scale` is passed as q's descale, so every logit is multiplied by `k_scale` a second time.

Models without KV scales run with `k_scale == 1`, where all three mistakes are invisible.

## Modifications

- `AiterAttnBackend._quantize_q_fp8`: quantizes q with a static unit scale (sglang does not load checkpoint q scales) and returns that scale as `q_descale`. Used by the NHD prefill and the unified-attention decode. This is the convention the gfx950 HD128 ASM prefill already follows ("Q is cast at unit scale"). For checkpoints without KV scales (`k_scale == 1`) the numerics are unchanged, except that the quant kernel saturates where the previous `.to(fp8)` cast produced NaN for |q| > 240 on e4m3fnuz; the FP8-Q unified-attention decode from sgl-project/sglang#31856 keeps the same kernel and cost.
  - The input is made contiguous because q is a strided view into the fused qkv output and aiter's per-tensor quant kernels read their input as contiguous rows (with a strided q they silently read the wrong elements).
- `paged_attention_ragged` decode receives the layer's `k_descale` / `v_descale`, falling back to the unit scales.
- New AMD unit test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py`: runs the default paged decode and the NHD prefill with the real aiter kernels on an fp8 cache whose k/v scales are far from 1, and compares with fp32 attention over the dequantized cache. No model download, about 10 s.
- `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py`: the unified branch now expects the unit q scale instead of `layer.k_scale`.

Not changed: the gfx950 head_dim-256 fp8 prefill paths (`flash_attn_varlen_fp8_pertensor_func`) pass `k_scale` as q's descale in the same way and are left to a follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

**MI355X (gfx950)**, main `fd5c52588f` vs. this PR on top of it. Single GPU, `--attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on, GSM8K 200 questions, 5-shot completion (`sglang.test.run_eval` with the `GSM8KMixin` settings), 3 runs each:

| Model | KV cache | Path exercised | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | default decode (prefill on the HD128 ASM kernel) | 0.005 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.755 / 0.760 / 0.760 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | unified-attention decode, page size 16 | 0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.780 / 0.775 / 0.755 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | bf16 (reference) | — | — | 0.765 / 0.760 / 0.770 |
| nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV | `auto` (resolves to fp8) | default decode, NHD prefill | 0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000 | 0.310 / 0.310 / 0.305 |
| nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV | bf16 (reference) | — | 0.320 / 0.305 / 0.320 | — |
| amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8 | fp8_e4m3 | unified-attention decode (sliding-window pool) | 0.005 / 0.005 / 0.020 | 0.510 / 0.575 / 0.565 |
| amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8 | bf16 (reference) | — | 0.510 / 0.555 / 0.500 | — |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B (no KV scales) | fp8_e4m3 | default decode | 0.915 / 0.935 / 0.935 | 0.925 / 0.925 / 0.935 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B (no KV scales) | fp8_e4m3 | unified-attention decode, page size 16 | 0.945 / 0.955 / 0.950 | 0.950 / 0.935 / 0.945 |

The gpt-oss scores are low in absolute terms because the 5-shot completion prompt does not use its chat format; the bf16 reference uses the same harness.

Tests on MI355X:

- `test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py` (new): both cases pass with a relative L2 error of 0.04 against the reference (threshold 0.15); on main both fail, with errors of 285 for the paged decode and 0.91 for the NHD prefill.
- `test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` passes; on main its unified-attention case fails because q is quantized with `k_scale`.

**MI325X (gfx942)**, single GPU, `--attention-backend aiter`, GSM8K 200 questions, CUDA graph on. These runs use the image's sglang (`dc6b5d1f5a`) with the identical patch applied, because main did not start in that image (sgl-kernel mismatch); the diff of `aiter_backend.py` is the same line for line.

| Model | KV cache | Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | default | 0.000 | 0.755–0.770 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | unified attention, page size 16 | 0.000 | 0.780–0.795 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | bf16 (reference) | default | 0.770–0.795 | — |
| Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (no KV scales) | fp8_e4m3 | default | 0.755–0.790 | 0.760–0.795 |

`test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` passes on the patched build.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, single GPU.

**MI355X (gfx950)**, main `fd5c52588f` vs. this PR, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (no KV scales) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, 8 × concurrency prompts (at least 32):

| Path | Concurrency | TTFT main / PR (ms) | TPOT main / PR (ms) | Output tok/s main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 1 | 38.14 / 37.97 | 4.57 / 4.64 | 212.4 / 209.4 |
| default | 32 | 498.66 / 499.30 | 6.90 / 6.92 | 3619.8 / 3610.1 |
| default | 128 | 1602.91 / 1611.36 | 16.76 / 16.83 | 5563.8 / 5539.3 |
| unified attention, page size 16 | 1 | 38.35 / 38.11 | 4.58 / 4.59 | 212.3 / 211.5 |
| unified attention, page size 16 | 32 | 505.11 / 500.43 | 6.95 / 6.99 | 3587.9 / 3581.8 |
| unified attention, page size 16 | 128 | 1612.80 / 1611.78 | 15.08 / 15.10 | 5988.8 / 5986.0 |

On gfx950 the default path does no extra work (the HD128 prefill runs on the ASM kernel, which this PR does not touch, and the decode only receives different scale tensors), so its differences of up to 1.5% are run-to-run noise. The unified path, which adds the q quantization copy, stays within 0.6%.

MI355X, `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` with this PR, fp8 KV cache vs. bf16 KV cache:

| KV cache | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp8_e4m3 | 1 | 37.48 | 3.36 | 285.8 |
| bf16 | 1 | 50.10 | 3.45 | 275.2 |
| fp8_e4m3 | 32 | 485.96 | 5.73 | 4198.6 |
| bf16 | 32 | 519.16 | 6.18 | 3902.2 |
| fp8_e4m3 | 128 | 1211.95 | 16.29 | 6093.5 |
| bf16 | 128 | 1307.39 | 19.25 | 5263.1 |

**MI325X (gfx942)**:

| Model | KV cache | Build | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | fp8_e4m3 | before | 1 | 57.98 | 5.73 | 168.3 |
| Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | fp8_e4m3 | after | 1 | 57.67 | 5.65 | 170.7 |
| Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | fp8_e4m3 | before | 32 | 875.88 | 10.55 | 2294.6 |
| Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | fp8_e4m3 | after | 32 | 880.15 | 10.55 | 2292.0 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | after | 1 | 42.04 | 4.63 | 209.2 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | bf16 | — | 1 | 44.73 | 4.73 | 204.1 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | fp8_e4m3 | after | 32 | 586.98 | 8.18 | 3060.1 |
| amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV | bf16 | — | 32 | 598.13 | 8.61 | 2927.1 |

No measurable overhead for models without KV scales.

## Reproduce

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently.

In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy.
- New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` with unified attention at page size 1 (threshold 0.65).

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, with and without this patch, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 --attention-backend aiter`, CUDA graph on. GSM8K uses the same settings as the new CI test (200 questions, 5-shot, completion API, `max_tokens=512`), 3 runs each.

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| unified attention, page size 1 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.755 / 0.755 / 0.765 |
| unified attention, page size 16 (reference) | — | 0.765 |

A second dense model gives the same picture: Qwen3-8B scores 0.00 before and 0.95 after, the same as page size 16 (0.95).

The new CI test fails on `main` (`np.float64(0.0) not greater than or equal to 0.65`) and passes with this patch: 0.765 on MI355X, and 0.765 on MI300X (gfx942) in this PR's CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for configurations other than unified attention at page size 1, which was producing wrong output before. With the patch, page size 1 output throughput is within 2% of page size 16.

MI355X, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, `sglang.bench_serving`, random input 2048 / output 256, CUDA graph on, unified attention, patched build:

| Page size | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 58.79 | 4.24 | 224.5 |
| 16 | 1 | 61.89 | 4.25 | 223.4 |
| 1 | 32 | 572.97 | 7.48 | 3294.8 |
| 16 | 32 | 621.54 | 7.15 | 3342.5 |

## Reproduce

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --port 30000

python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 --num-shots 5

python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --seed 1
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Fix] [AMD] docker: Remove implicit INT8 QuickReduce default as it causes accuracy issues in 800k+ long context evals
author: functionstackx
body:
## Human

QUICK REDUCE QUANTIZATION has been reported by multiple community maintainers & folks deploying in production an signficiant  drop in quality for end-user production workloads in addition to their private & public 800k+ long context evals.  On 1 eval, community maintainers and us ran, it drops the 800k+ long context eval by over relatively 10% from 34% baseline to 30.4%.

this shouldn't be an surprise to AMD as AMD has noted the accuracy effect of this option too in vllm recipes https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blame/e38b528a540f3bf79674960cae78173e775e7fdc/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml#L710

since this is an accuracy effecting flag, it shouldnt be set as default

## Motivation

The ROCm image currently sets `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8` for every workload. Remove this image-level override so deployments opt into INT8 QuickReduce explicitly.

## Modifications

Delete `ENV ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8` from `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`. No other defaults or runtime code change.

When the variable is unset, `QuickAllReduce.init_quick_all_reduce()` defaults to `NONE` and disables QuickReduce. Users can still enable it explicitly at container launch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Verified that the diff contains only the requested ENV deletion.
- Verified that the runtime fallback remains `NONE`.
- No image build or GPU accuracy tests were run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Removing the implicit INT8 QuickReduce setting may affect collective performance for workloads that previously inherited it.

title: [Fix] rust-server: End an /abort_request-ed request on the scheduler's abort finish reason, as Python does
author: metamergebot
body:
Based on #46961, now merged: the frontend abort output repeats the request's `cached_tokens_details`, which that change introduced. This branch sits directly on `main`.

## Motivation

Python's `POST /abort_request` does not fail the request it names. `TokenizerManager.abort_request` forwards an `AbortReq` to the scheduler and leaves the request's response state in place, so the scheduler's next step ends the request with its terminal output: the partial generation produced so far, the request's token counts, and `finish_reason` `{"type": "abort", "message": "Aborted"}`. A streaming client sees a final chunk whose `finish_reason` is `abort`, then `[DONE]`; a unary `/generate` gets a 200 with the partial text.

The Rust frontend's `/abort_request` (#45888) reused the gRPC `Abort` path, which cancels the request at once and ends the client's call with a cancelled error. Clients that abort through the HTTP route therefore got an error body and no partial output where Python's server gives them a completed-with-abort response.

## Modifications

- `handlers/generate.rs`: `CoreHandle::abort` takes an `AbortEnding`. `CancelledError` keeps the gRPC `Abort` behaviour. `AbortFinishReason` is what `/abort_request` uses: a request Intake has not claimed yet is cancelled before it starts and its call finishes on a frontend abort output; an accepted request is handed to the scheduler as an `AbortSource::Request` and its call keeps waiting for the scheduler's terminal output. The cancellation a `Generation` observes is now a `Cancellation` (`Error`, `Unstarted`, `Scheduler`) rather than a unit, and is remembered once observed so preparation, submission and the response stream can all read it.
- `handlers/handle.rs`: a `RuntimeCall` records the counts and cache split of the request's latest output. When a scheduler-handed abort gets no answer, because Intake closed the sink or the scheduler stayed silent for 30 s, the call ends on a frontend abort output that repeats those counts, is marked `abort_output`, and (on the deadline) tells the runtime to drop the request as a dropped call would.
- `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler.rs`, `wiring.rs`: `AbortSource::Request` keeps the detokenizer entry so the scheduler's terminal output still reaches the client, and queues the `AbortReq` behind the request on the request ring, so the reserved control lane cannot overtake a request the scheduler has not yet seen. On a full ring it falls back to the existing abort path. `RequestAdmission` gains `cancel_if_pending` and `is_accepted` for the two endings.
- `http/info.rs`: `/abort_request` aborts with `AbortFinishReason`. `grpc/service.rs`: the `Abort` RPC keeps `CancelledError`.
- `Cargo.toml`: tokio `test-util` as a dev-dependency, for the paused-time deadline test.
- Tests: `abort_request_ends_requests_on_the_schedulers_abort` (native stream, unary `/generate`, and `/v1/completions` stream each end on the scheduler's abort output), `scheduler_abort_without_an_answer_ends_on_a_frontend_abort_output`, `unstarted_abort_request_records_no_finished_request`, `explicit_abort_ends_the_call_before_its_sink_closes`, `request_abort_keeps_the_sink_and_queues_behind_the_request`, and both endings in `explicit_abort_wakes_a_submission_blocked_on_admission`.

## Lines that exist only to fit the `handlers/` layout

Beyond the behaviour change itself, this pull request carries 14 lines whose only purpose is to fit the `handlers/` split from #46181 (the code this change touches used to be one `core/handle.rs`). None of them changes behaviour or a test body:

1. `handlers.rs`: `pub(crate) use generate::{AbortEnding, CoreCall, recv_indexed};` re-exports `AbortEnding` from `generate.rs`.
2. `grpc/service.rs`: `AbortEnding` added to the existing `use crate::api_server::handlers::{...}` import.
3. `http/info.rs`: `AbortEnding` added to the existing `use crate::api_server::handlers::{...}` import.
4. `handlers/generate.rs`: `enum Cancellation` is `pub(super)`, because `RuntimeCall` in `handlers/handle.rs` matches on it.
5. `handlers/generate.rs`: `Generation::cancelled` keeps the `pub(super)` the split gave it while its return type changes to `Cancellation`.
6. `handlers/generate.rs`: `Generation::try_cancelled`, which replaces `is_cancelled`, keeps that function's `pub(super)`.
7. `handlers/generate.rs`: `LastOutput` added to the `use super::handle::{...}` import (rustfmt wraps it to three lines).
8. `handlers/handle.rs`: `Cancellation` added to the `use super::generate::{...}` import.
9. `handlers/handle.rs`: `use std::time::Duration;` for `SCHEDULER_ABORT_DEADLINE`.
10. `handlers/handle.rs`: `RuntimeCall.last_output` and `RuntimeCall.abort_deadline` are `pub(super)` like the struct's other fields, since `generate.rs` constructs it.
11. `handlers/handle.rs`: `struct LastOutput` is `pub(super)`, as the type of a `pub(super)` field.
12. `handlers/generate.rs` tests: imports for `CachedTokensDetails` and `ChunkExtras`, which the new tests use and which no longer live in the same file.
13. `handlers/generate.rs` test `unstarted_abort_request_records_no_finished_request`: `peer_endpoints: Vec::new()` in the `CoreConfig` literal, a field #46181 added.
14. `handlers/health.rs`: `use crate::api_server::handlers::AbortEnding::CancelledError;` for the two `abort(None, CancelledError)` asserts in the health-probe and warmup tests that now live there.

Placement only: `SCHEDULER_ABORT_DEADLINE` sits in `handlers/handle.rs` next to `RuntimeCall::recv`, its only user.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: control-plane behaviour of one endpoint.

## Test plan

- `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cd rust && cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cd rust && cargo test -p sglang-server`: 434 passed, 0 failed (includes the new tests above).
- Not run: a live server. The change composes the existing core cancellation registry, `Intake::on_abort` and the response path, which the unit tests drive end to end from the HTTP routes.

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Fix the EP>1 crash in the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE path and restrict it to gfx1151
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
Serving a Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoint with `--ep-size` > 1 on the W4A16 path added in #41389 aborts the GPU with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016`. Under expert parallelism the standard dispatcher hands each rank `topk_ids` where experts owned by other ranks are `-1`, and `_apply_triton_w4a16` feeds those ids straight into `counts.scatter_add_(...)`, which writes out of bounds.

**Where it shows up**
Every GPU that takes the W4A16 path with EP > 1. It was reported on #41389 for both gfx1151 and gfx942, and reproduced here on gfx1151. The path was also enabled on every HIP GPU that is not gfx95x or gfx1250 (so gfx942/MI300X as well), although it was written and validated for gfx1151.

**How to fix**
Send `-1` ids to an extra bucket that sorts last, is left out of the ragged expert counts, and is zeroed before the top-k reduction, and enable the path only on gfx1151.

This PR also addresses the review comments on #41389 that were still open at merge time: log once when the W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16, register the opt-out env var in `environ.py`, and reject SwiGLU variants the path cannot compute (`gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_beta`, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `swiglu_limit`, e.g. gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4, MiniMax-M3), which previously passed the `activation == "silu"` check and produced silently wrong output.

## Modifications

All runtime changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` and only take effect on gfx1151.

- Gate: `_use_triton_w4a16` is now `gfx1151 and SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` instead of "HIP and not gfx95x and not gfx1250". gfx942 and other AMD GPUs go back to the AITER path.
- EP fix in `_apply_triton_w4a16`: `-1` ids are mapped to bucket `num_experts`, `counts` gets one extra slot that is dropped before `make_ragged_tensor_metadata`, and the scattered rows of non-local slots are zeroed with `masked_fill` before the sum over `top_k`. Everything stays on device, so CUDA graph capture still works.
- Env var: `SGLANG_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` becomes `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16 = EnvBool(True)` in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (AMD section), read via `envs.....get()`. The name gains the `ENABLE_` verb required by the env-var conventions; it was only on the #41389 branch, never in a release.
- `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` raises `NotImplementedError` listing the unsupported SwiGLU parameters instead of running plain SwiGLU.
- `logger.info_once` reports that the W4A4 MXFP4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 and how to disable it.
- New `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_w4a16.py` (stdlib `unittest`, `register_amd_ci(est_time=40, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")`), entering through `create_moe_runner` / `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply_weights`:
  - `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path`, `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path`, `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` (gate, by reloading the module with a mocked `gcnArchName`)
  - `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` (ep=2 outputs summed over ranks equal the ep=1 output)
  - `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output`
  - `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected`

## Accuracy Tests

Setup for all tables: 1x gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, 96 GB VRAM carve-out), tp=1, `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, `--attention-backend triton --context-length 8192`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-gfx1151-20260923`. Before = #41389 as merged; After = this PR.

**EP crash (kernel level).** This GPU has a single device, so EP > 1 was exercised by calling `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` / `_apply_triton_w4a16` with the `topk_ids` the dispatcher produces under EP (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MoE shapes: 256 experts, top-k 8, hidden 2048, intermediate 512; random MXFP4 weights).

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ep=1 | runs | runs |
| ep=2, rank 0 / rank 1 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION` (code 0x1016) | runs |
| ep=2 rank outputs summed vs ep=1 output, N = 1 / 7 / 16 / 128 / 512 tokens | n/a | rel. error 2.26e-3 to 2.36e-3 (bf16 rounding of each rank's output) |
| CUDA graph capture + replay with `-1` ids | n/a | bit-identical to eager |

**New unit tests** (6 tests, 3.6 s, 29 s wall including import, on gfx1151):

| Test | Before (#41389 code) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path` | pass | pass |
| `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected` | FAIL (`NotImplementedError` not raised) | pass |

**GSM8K at ep=1** (regression check for the default path). sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 questions, thinking off (`enable_thinking=false`), `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `seed=0`, 16 concurrent requests.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K score | 63.0% | 60.0% |

The 3-point gap is sampling noise, not a numerical change: at ep=1 the MoE output of `_apply_triton_w4a16` is bit-identical before and after (`torch.equal` on N = 1 / 16 / 27 / 512 tokens, max abs diff 0), because every id is valid and the new ops are identities. The end-to-end runs differ only through temperature-1.0 sampling with nondeterministic batching (200 questions give a standard error of about 3.4 points). With thinking off the model answers with `\boxed{N}` and little or no reasoning, so this run checks before/after equivalence, not the model's best score. For reference, before with thinking on scored 82.0%, but 31% of answers were truncated by the 8192-token context.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, input 512 / output 256 tokens, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `num_prompts` = 10 x concurrency, `--seed 0`, one run per row.

| Concurrency | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Output throughput (tok/s) | 8.45 | 8.34 | -1.3% |
| 1 | Median TPOT (ms) | 117.00 | 117.98 | +0.8% |
| 1 | Median TTFT (ms) | 458.8 | 491.2 | +7.1% |

| 16 | Median TPOT (ms) | 154.05 | 156.35 | +1.5% |

title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort retracted requests whose KV the recompute cannot rebuild
author: hnyls2002
body:
- **Abort a retracted request when the recompute cannot rebuild its KV.** `release_req` now returns whether the request can be resumed, and is the single decision point for every retract:
  - **PD decode rebootstrap** (`pause_generation(mode="retract")`, and the DeepSeek-V4 retract through `backup_kv_cache`): `Req.build_rebootstrap_payload` carries token ids only, so multimodal, `input_embeds` and `positional_embed_overrides` requests were recomputed with wrong KV and produced wrong output without an error. They are now aborted (`Req.resumable_by_rebootstrap`). `backup_kv_cache` already did this for multimodal requests under DeepSeek-V4; it now uses the same property.
  - **Local re-prefill** (non-disaggregated retract): multimodal inputs and embed overrides are applied again by `prepare_for_extend`, so those requests are fine. `input_embeds` cover only the prompt, so `reset_for_retract` restarts their generation. That restart is invisible until output has been sent downstream; once it has (a streamed token, or a non-stream request past the `SGLANG_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL` flush), the restarted tokens were spliced after the stale `send_token_offset`. Such a request is now aborted instead (`Req.resumable_by_reprefill`); one that has sent nothing still restarts.
  - `retract_all` returns the requests that cannot be resumed, and `pause_generation` aborts them with a 503. `retract_decode` already aborts when `release_req` returns False.
  - Every PD rebootstrap now has at least one output id, so the transfer commit's `resumes_output` is `decode_req.is_rebootstrap` with an assert.
- **One PD fill-length formula.** `len(origin_input_ids) + max(len(output_ids) - 1, 0)` was written in `DecodePreallocQueue._pre_alloc_fill_len` and again for the prebuilt `seq_len`; both use `pre_alloc_fill_len` in `disaggregation/utils.py` now. No behavior change.
- **`/detokenize` rejects out-of-vocabulary ids with 400.** A negative id or one above u32 returned 500, and an id at or above the vocab size was silently dropped with a 200. Ids outside `[0, model vocab_size)` now get a 400, as `_validate_token_ids_logprob` reports invalid ids.

Behavior changes: the aborts above replace silently wrong output (PD decode) or a garbled restarted generation (local `input_embeds` retract after output was sent), and `/detokenize` returns 400 where it returned 500 or dropped ids. Priority preemption still re-prefills a preempted `input_embeds` request from the prompt; that path is unchanged here.

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Do not dispatch a request whose abort was already sent
author: metamergebot
body:
## Motivation

If a request is aborted while the tokenizer manager is still preparing it (for example while it fetches an image or publishes multimodal features), the `AbortReq` reaches the scheduler before the request itself. The scheduler drops an abort for a rid it has not received and keeps no record of it, and `abort_request` never resends one because `state.abort_sent` is already set. The request is then dispatched anyway and runs to completion while its caller waits. A plain server shows it with a slow image URL and a client disconnect: the request runs to `max_new_tokens`. In PD disaggregation a decode request in this state holds its KV until the transfer timeout.

The ordering:
1. The rid is registered and preprocessing is in progress.
2. `abort_request` sets `state.abort_sent` and sends `AbortReq`. The scheduler has no request with that rid yet, so it drops the abort.
3. Preprocessing finishes and `_send_one_request` dispatches the request.
4. Every later `abort_request` call returns early at `if state.abort_sent`, including the disconnect watcher's.

## Modifications

- `_send_one_request` and `_send_batch_request` check `abort_sent` after their last `await` and skip dispatch for such requests. Everything after the check is synchronous, so no abort can land between the check and the dispatch. The prepared transport features of a skipped request are released the same way a failed dispatch releases them: CUDA VMM items through `cancel_for_dispatch`, and CUDA IPC feature proxies (`feature` and `precomputed_embeddings`) through the pool's `cancel_proxy`, since no scheduler would ever acknowledge them. A batch still dispatches its other requests. The batch path is factored into `_drop_aborted_before_dispatch`.
- `_wait_one_response` finishes a skipped request through `_handle_abort_req`. That produces the same output the scheduler sends when it pops an aborted request from its waiting queue (finish reason `abort`, "Abort in waiting queue") and removes the rid from `rid_to_state`. It runs in the waiter rather than at the send site because the waiter looks its state up by rid and finishing the request removes that entry.
- `abort_request(abort_all=True)` marks every undispatched request `abort_sent`, so an abort-all (`/abort_request`, weight updates with `abort_all_requests`, pause with abort) also keeps requests still preprocessing from running. Requests held at `generate_request`'s pause gate are left alone (new `ReqState.waiting_at_pause_gate`): a pause holds them and they run after `continue_generation`.

Not covered: multi-tokenizer mode (`tokenizer_worker_num > 1`). If `/abort_request` lands on a worker that does not own the rid, that worker forwards it to the scheduler without touching the owning worker's state; covering that needs a record on the scheduler side.

## Tests

New tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestAbortBeforeDispatch`; each fails without the fix (the waiter never finishes, `TimeoutError`):
- `test_abort_during_preprocessing_is_not_dispatched` aborts a request through `generate_request` while tokenization (subtest `tokenize`) or feature publication (subtest `publish`) is blocked, then lets it finish. Only the `AbortReq` reaches the scheduler, the caller gets an `abort` finish reason, the prepared features and CUDA IPC proxies are cancelled, and the rid is freed.
- `test_abort_all_skips_preprocessing_requests_but_not_paused_ones`: an abort-all finishes the request that was preprocessing and leaves the one held at the pause gate, which is dispatched after the pause is lifted.
- `test_batch_dispatches_only_requests_not_aborted` aborts one request of a batch during the batch's feature publication. The other request is dispatched alone, only the aborted request's multimodal items and proxies are cancelled, and its waiter gets an `abort` finish reason.

`test_request_class_override_points.py`: the stub request state gains an `abort_sent` field, which the dispatch path now reads.

Run locally on a CPU-only environment: `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py` and `test_request_class_override_points.py`, 55 passed; `test_multimodal_abort_cleanup.py`, `test_gpu_feature_transport.py` and `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` also pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model execution or numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a dictionary lookup per dispatched request.

title: [Fix] PP: record received proxy tensors on the forward stream
author: Phoenix3334
body:
<!-- editorial-summary-20261107 -->
## Summary

**Fixes #47613.** In asynchronous PP decode, proxy tensors received on a communication stream may be consumed later on the forward stream. When the previous Python reference is dropped before the queued forward uses the data, the CUDA caching allocator can reuse the receive storage and corrupt model outputs. This was observed as long token-0 runs at `--pp-async-batch-depth > pp_size / 2`.

## Changes

- In `_pp_launch_batch`, call `record_stream(self.forward_stream)` for each non-CPU proxy tensor before `run_batch`, protecting storage until the forward stream has finished using it.
- Update the existing idle-counter fixture to return `None` for the simulated first PP stage.
- No global synchronization or new execution-order barrier is introduced: **`record_stream` records allocator lifetime, not stream ordering**.

## Validation

Kimi-K3, 8×B300, fake PD transfer; affected requests were identified by ≥20 consecutive token-0 outputs.

| PP/TP shape | Async depth | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 51/192 | **0/192** |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 98/192 | **0/192** |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 59/192 | **0/192** |
| PP4 × TP2 | 3 | 6/192 | **0/192** |
| PP4 × TP2 | 4 | 19/192 | **0/192** |

Receive-vs-forward checksums mismatched in the unfixed runs (76 and 378 of ~7,500 comparisons), but not in the fixed runs. A later reported exact-fix comparison and dedicated-communication-stream experiments are documented in the archive below; those evidence groups are **not interchangeable**.

Existing 4×H100 PP GPU tests (2 compatibility + 6 speculative tests), and prior-head Base/AMD CI passed. The mocked-only `record_stream` unit test was removed in review because it could not reproduce allocator reuse.

## Scope and limitations

This is a correctness/lifetime fix, **not a performance optimization**. Historical 8×B300 experiments used v0.5.22 and fake transfer; real two-node PD, all PP event-loop combinations, and full post-merge GPU runtime coverage were not established. Historical CI passes are explicitly scoped to the corresponding tested heads.

Evidence: [Issue #47613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/47613), [review discussion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47614#issuecomment-6567604516), and the archived runs below.

<details>
<summary>Historical experiment matrices, CI runs and investigation notes (original PR body)</summary>

**Archive notice:** The sections below preserve the original investigation record, including earlier intermediate findings and CI statuses. The concise summary above states the final interpretation and validation boundaries.

---

## Motivation

Fixes #47613. With `--pp-async-batch-depth > pp_size / 2`, the PD decode loop returns runs of token 0 for many requests (Kimi-K3 PP2 × TP4 depth 2: 51–98 of 192).

A downstream stage gets its proxy tensors from `recv_tensor_dict`, which allocates them on another stream; the forward stream reads them later. `event_loop_pp_disagg_decode` drops the previous reference before posting the next recv. When enough forwards are queued, the allocator gives the next recv the same block and it overwrites data a queued forward has not read yet. Checksums taken right after the recv and right before the forward differ in 76 and 378 of ~7500 comparisons on two runs; with this change they never differ.

## Modifications

- `_pp_launch_batch`: before `run_batch`, call `record_stream(self.forward_stream)` on each non-CPU tensor in `pp_proxy_tensors`. Every PP event loop goes through `_pp_launch_batch`, so they share this fix location; runtime validation did not exercise every loop configuration; the first stage passes `None` and is unchanged.
- Existing idle-counter test: make the mocked proxy receive return `None` for the simulated rank-zero scheduler, matching the real receive path. A bare `Mock()` previously reached the new tensor iteration and caused a fixture `TypeError`.

- The earlier DCP CI fixture correction from mickqian’s [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736), source commit `be43d568ca8115e173bd4b9f5d106a3060ae1f8b`, is now included in main and is no longer part of this PR's cumulative diff.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3, 8 × B300, fake transfer, C64 N=192, requests with ≥20 consecutive token 0:

| shape | depth | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 51 | 0 |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 98 | 0 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 59 | 0 |
| PP4 × TP2 | 3 | 6 | 0 |
| PP4 × TP2 | 4 | 19 | 0 |

A later validation report for this exact fix recorded PP2 × TP4 depth 2 and PP4 × TP2 depth 4 both 0/192, with 0 checksum mismatches in 7498 and 14499 comparisons, and PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 depth 2 at C384 N=3840 at 0/3840. The raw logs for that exact-fix rerun are not in the current local bundle; these figures are reported results, not independently rechecked here. The earlier fix runs and checksum comparisons above have retained local logs.

GSM8K (5-shot, 200 questions, non-PD, PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 depth 2): 0.985 before, 0.980 after.

### Additional validation: dedicated PP communication stream

Follow-up runs on 2026-10-31 used `SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP=1` on v0.5.22, Kimi-K3, 8 × B300, and fake PD. The server log confirmed `PP tensor communication overlap enabled on a dedicated CUDA stream`. Synthetic random-token prompts targeted 64,000 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens, with random range ratio 0. C is maximum request concurrency; N is the number of requests. The output check counted requests containing at least 20 consecutive token 0 (`!` for this tokenizer).

| shape | depth | C | N | affected requests, original | affected requests, fixed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PP2 × TP4 | 2 | 64 | 192 | 73/192 | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 | 3 | 64 | 192 | 109/192 | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 64 | 192 | not run | 0/192 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 256 | 2560 | not run | 0/2560 |
| PP2 × TP4 + DCP4 | 2 | 384 | 3840 | not run | 0/3840 |

These runs used the earlier CUDA-equivalent fix: `record_stream(current_stream())` inside `forward_stream_ctx`, guarded by `tensor.is_cuda`. The submitted diff uses `self.forward_stream` and a non-CPU guard. This extends the output-level evidence to the dedicated communication-stream configuration; it is not an exact-diff rerun, a main runtime test, or real two-node PD validation. Checksum instrumentation was not enabled in these runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

PP2 × TP4 + DCP4, depth 0, fake transfer, C384 N=3840, same node and session, runs in order:

| run | output tok/s | median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 3525.5 | 103.41 ms |
| after | 3507.0 | 104.04 ms |
| before | 3539.8 | 103.79 ms |

The patched run was 0.52–0.93% slower than the two baseline runs. This small sample does not establish statistical equivalence or zero overhead. With depth 2, the throughput reported before this change was inflated by the corrupted outputs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (all applicable hooks passed on both final PR files; repository-wide Ruff lint and formatting checks also passed on the updated base).
- [x] Validate with existing PP integration tests and B300 experiments; remove the mock-only CPU test as requested in review.
- [ ] Update documentation (N/A).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.

## Applicability to main

The lifetime-critical logic is the same in `release/v0.5.22` and main at `2f6e7f347526034a173424cad0e7a72a5fb61ad2`: the disaggregated decode loop clears `pp_proxy_tensors` before the next receive; `_pp_recv_proxy_tensors` wraps the received tensors without recording the forward stream; and `_pp_launch_batch` submits `run_batch` on the forward stream without recording those inputs. Main is therefore expected to be affected by the same allocator-lifetime race based on source comparison. The B300 runtime reproduction and fix validation were completed on v0.5.22; that B300 reproduction was not separately repeated on main. Upstream CPU and PP integration results are listed below. This comparison concerns the bug-relevant lifetime logic, not byte-for-byte identity of the entire scheduler file.

## Validation limits

The B300 GPU results above are historical reports from v0.5.22; upstream main-based CI results are listed below. PD tests used fake transfer; real two-node PD and ordinary PP at queue depths ≥3 remain untested. The token-0 feedback experiment does not independently exclude recurrent-state corruption.

Current preparation base: `768e56202b0ef523227fe8dc375937083194eccc`. Updated on 2026-11-02 in current head `9effc87527556ad4e8697b2e1de91bd2312d15c4`, merging main while preserving the PR commit history. The PP lifetime fix is unchanged; its explanatory comment is shortened to two lines. The DCP fixture correction from [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736) is already present upstream and is no longer part of the cumulative PR diff.

On the previous head `6745437`, [Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41301682406) passed, including all 20 CPU shards and the GB300/B300 jobs; [AMD CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41301682373) also passed. Both requested PP GPU test files (`test_pp_parallel_compat.py`, 2 cases; `test_pp_spec.py`, 6 cases) [passed on 4×H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41291896395) at `1bd623e`. The production fix is unchanged from that run.

### Review cleanup (2026-11-02)

Per [BBuf’s request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47614#issuecomment-6567604516), commit `b15b09e` deletes `test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_proxy_record_stream.py`. It only checked mocked `record_stream` calls and ordering, and could not reproduce allocator reuse. The production fix, existing idle-counter fixture correction, and documented GPU evidence remain unchanged. The cleanup commit changes only that deletion (112 lines); no additional local CPU/GPU runs were performed.

The passing Base/AMD results above apply to the previous head, before the test deletion. [CI on the cleanup head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41378151982) was triggered but stopped at the 120-minute per-user cooldown gate before tests executed. The logged previous accepted trigger is 2026-11-02 02:18:01 UTC; earliest retry under that cooldown is 04:18:01 UTC / 12:18:01 UTC+8. BBuf confirmed the opt-in extra workflows are not needed for this production fix. Code-owner approval is still pending.

### Latest reviewer follow-up (2026-11-02)

Addressed [ShangmingCai’s review](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47614#pullrequestreview-5732492693) in [`9effc87`](https://github.com/Phoenix3334/sglang/commit/9effc87527556ad4e8697b2e1de91bd2312d15c4): shortened the lifetime comment from five lines to two, and merged main at `768e562`, which already removes the duplicate `tree_cache` keyword that caused the previous Ruff failure in `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`.
