title: [Fix] moe: Revert the JIT rewrite of `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` (#47784)
author: hnyls2002
body:
- Revert #47784 (`ca819c11cd`), the JIT rewrite of `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`: restore `moe_finalize_fuse_shared.cu` and its Python wrapper byte for byte, and drop the new `.cuh` kernel with its unit test and benchmark.
- Keep the `fma_f32x2` / `mul_f32x2` / `add_f32x2` helpers #47784 added to `sgl_kernel/math.cuh`; `kimi_k3/attn_res/fused_tma.cuh` uses them now.
- #47784 drops GSM8K of `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 1P1D, HiSparse + MTP) on 8-gpu-b200 from ~0.95 to ~0.90, below its 0.935 threshold. The test is nightly-only, so the PR's CI did not run it.
- The failure reproduces on 8-gpu-b200 only; on 8x B300 the same commits pass (0.942-0.950).

No behavior change other than going back to the pre-#47784 finalize kernel.

## Suspected cause

cc @DarkSharpness @BBuf. This is our reading of the code, not yet confirmed by a targeted run.

- With `routing_ready=True`, the default and what `finalize_flashinfer_trtllm_deferred_output` passes, the new kernel loads the routing tensors **and the `shared_output` row** before `PDLWaitPrimary` (`moe_finalize_fuse_shared.cuh`, `Token::load` and `finalize_kernel`).
- The old kernel also staged the routing tensors before `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()`, but read `shared_output` only after it. The early `shared_output` load is the one ordering change #47784 makes.
- In `DeepseekV2MoE`, `shared_output` is produced by the shared expert on `alt_stream`, and the main stream joins it with `wait_stream` right before the finalize launch. The `routing_ready` docstring requires the inputs to be complete when the kernel launches. We suspect that under CUDA graph capture with PDL, the dependency on the shared expert's last kernel is relaxed too, so finalize can read rows that are not written yet. The routing tensors come from an earlier kernel on the same stream, which is why reading them early was safe before.
- That fits the symptom: no crash, a few points of accuracy lost, and only on one GPU type, where the timing exposes the race.

## Relanding

- Keep the routing prefetch, and move the `shared_output` row load after `PDLWaitPrimary`, as the old kernel did. Or pass `routing_ready=False` whenever `shared_output` is given, at some cost in latency.
- Add a test that produces `shared_output` on a side stream inside a CUDA graph with PDL on. The current unit test builds every input before the launch, so the early read is always safe there.
- Run `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200 before merging; it is nightly-only, so PR CI does not cover it.

## Bisect

`test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200, threshold 0.935; two scores are the first try and the automatic retry. In commit order:

title: [Fix] rust-server: Freeze the scheduler's garbage collector after the startup warmup
author: metamergebot
body:
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:start -->
**CI status (oncall, 2026-11-06 21:40 PST):** this PR is in GitHub stack #48459, the Rust-server stack: #48455 → #48457 → #48512 → #48515 → #48518 → #48523 → #48572 → #48753 → #48797 → #48798 → #48818 → #48815 (top). Each PR keeps its own diff (parent branches and `main` were merged in, no rebase). The merge commit that took main into this branch also adds one line to upstream's new test `drain_end_release_is_latched` (#48492): it takes the post-startup `FreezeGCReq` first, as this branch's other runtime tests do. The CI bar for the whole stack is `pr-test.yml` with `pr-test-finish` green on the top #48815 (run 42341406709). Once that is green, approve and use **Merge stack** to land the chain in one atomic step.
<!-- oss-sync ci-note:end -->

Stacked on #48512 (rust-server startup guards): this PR targets that branch, so its diff is the one commit on top; it rebases onto main once #48512 lands.

## Motivation

In Python-frontend mode the launcher posts `/freeze_gc` once the startup warmup finishes (or at once when `--skip-server-warmup` is set): the tokenizer manager turns it into a `FreezeGCReq` carrying `--gc-threshold`, and every scheduler rank applies the thresholds and calls `gc.freeze()`, so the objects allocated during startup stay out of every later full collection.

The Rust frontend never ran that step. `--gc-threshold` reaches the scheduler only through `FreezeGCReq`, so in Rust mode the flag was silently ignored and every full collection in the scheduler walked the whole startup heap.

## Modifications

- `ServerArgs` (Rust) gains `gc_threshold`, filled from `--gc-threshold` by `_build_server_args`.
- Each listener's `startup_warmup` sends `FreezeGCReq` once its warmup generation succeeds, immediately when the warmup is skipped, and after the disaggregation exception that keeps the server up on a failed warmup. A failed or timed-out warmup sends nothing, as in Python.
- The scheduler sends no reply to `FreezeGCReq`, so it leaves through a new one-way intake event (`TmEvent::OneWay`) instead of the awaited control path, which would hang. The intake pushes it on the reserved lane that aborts already use, so a full request ring cannot drop it, and reports back whether it was queued; a failure is logged as an error.
- `Scheduler.handle_freeze_gc` forwards the request to the detokenizer socket only when no Rust server is embedded: in Rust mode the detokenizer runs inside the scheduler process, which the freeze already covers, and nothing reads that socket.
- Propagation follows Python: without local control broadcast, the DP0 listener's message is broadcast to the TP group and the other listeners' copies are dropped; with `--enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast` each DP group freezes its own ranks; PP stages receive it through the normal forwarding.

No `/freeze_gc` HTTP route is added to the Rust server: in Python mode its only production caller is the launcher's own post-warmup request, which the Rust server now makes internally.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no change to model execution).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable here; the effect is the one `/freeze_gc` already has in Python mode (startup objects excluded from later full collections, `--gc-threshold` applied in the scheduler).

## Checklist

- `app.rs::startup_warmup_freezes_gc_once_warm`: skipped warmup, successful warmup (nothing frozen until the warmup reply arrives), failed warmup (nothing frozen, failure reported), failed warmup in disaggregation mode (server stays up and freezes); checks the exact `FreezeGCReq` wire array.
- `to_scheduler_tests.rs::one_way_control_bypasses_request_ring_capacity`: a full one-slot request ring still takes the message.
- `test_rust_server_extension.py::test_freeze_gc_skips_the_detokenizer_socket_in_rust_mode`.
- The `runtime.rs` tests that boot a real runtime with the warmup skipped, and `test_rust_server_crash_dump.py`, now take the startup `FreezeGCReq` off the ring before their own requests.
- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server --all-features` and the registered unit tests above pass locally on this branch.
- Beyond the change itself: one `assertEqual` in `test_rust_server_crash_dump.py` is joined onto a single line, the ruff-format form that upstream `lint` requires; no other line differs from the behaviour change.

title: [Fix] scheduler: Abort beam groups on a retract pause and close three request-drop gaps
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Summary

Four small fixes for requests that a pause, a memory release, an abort, or a PD role switch could leave in a broken state.

## Changes

- **Beam groups on a retract pause.** `pause_generation(mode="retract")` now aborts live beam groups instead of requeueing their leaders. `retract_all` frees each leader's member rows before its KV is released and records the abort reason, which is the same path `ScheduleBatch.retract_decode` takes under KV pressure. The running batch is now emptied through `filter_batch`, so its beam tail is stripped with the requests. Before this change, the stale tail tripped `reqs changed while a beam tail was attached` on the first `filter_batch` after resume. A pause-retracted beam leader that could not resume also leaked its member rows.
- **`release_memory_occupation` on a busy scheduler.** The idle check was a bare `assert`, which crashed the scheduler, or was skipped under `python -O`. The scheduler now returns a refusal instead: `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput` carries `success` and `message`, and the check runs before any memory is paused. A refused release must not be silent for callers that ignore return values, so `TokenizerManager.release_memory_occupation` raises `RuntimeError` with the merged message, and `Engine.release_memory_occupation` raises with it. `/release_memory_occupation` turns the error into a 400 through its existing error path. The later `flush_cache()` cannot be refused, because its idle gate is the same check.
- **Abort of a HiSparse-staged request.** After prefill, a HiSparse request waits in the staging list until its host copy lands, and it is in no batch while it waits. An abort that arrived after the prefill batch had moved on matched nothing, so the request ran to completion. `collect_inflight_reqs` now includes staged requests. The abort marks them, and they finish at their first decode step, as a running request does.
- **PD role switch with held requests.** `is_fully_idle` deliberately skips requests held by a retract pause (`PD_HELD`), so that a weight update can flush the cache. The role switch used the same check, so it tore down the decode queues and dropped the held requests without answering them. The switch now rejects with `safe_to_restore=True` while any request is held.

## Behavior changes

- During a retract pause, a beam-search request is aborted with 503 and is not resumed after the pause.
- `release_memory_occupation` on a busy scheduler no longer crashes the scheduler. `Engine.release_memory_occupation` raises `RuntimeError`, and `/release_memory_occupation` returns 400 with the message. A successful release returns what it returned before.
- An abort sent while a request is in HiSparse staging now finishes it.
- A PD role switch during a retract pause that holds requests is rejected until generation resumes and the held requests drain.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py::test_retract_aborts_beam_groups_and_drops_the_beam_tail`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] `test_scheduler_timeouts.py::test_hisparse_staged_request_is_finished_at_its_next_step`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] `test_pd_role_switch.py::test_rejected_while_a_retract_pause_holds_requests`: fails before the fix and passes after.
- [x] The existing CPU unit tests for the touched paths pass when each file runs on its own: beam search, pause, timeouts, weight updater, flush cache, io_struct and msgpack round trip, HiSparse, abort cleanup, PD role switch, decode queue cleanup, and the MLX scheduler mixin. The MLX mixin test's batch mock now applies `filter_batch`.
- [ ] GPU: a beam-search run with a retract pause and resume.

title: [Fix] test: Keep a passed precision baseline row pointing at its own tensors
author: hnyls2002
body:
## Why the test broke

`test/registered/debug_utils/test_nightly_precision_regression.py` failed in the Nov 7 nightly (attempt 1) with `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8: FAILED - tensor=...model.layers.56.self_attn.inputs.hidden_states rel_diff=0.00117`, and passed on the rerun on the same commit.

- **The failure itself is a runner, not code.** On healthy hardware the dumped tensors are bit-reproducible: 16 fresh launches on one commit on a separate 8x H200 machine were bit-identical to each other and to the stored baseline, and passing CI runs report `max_rel_diff=0.0`. The failing attempt ran on one specific `8-gpu-h200` runner whose deviation (starting at layer 48, prefill tokens 11-16, largest on TP rank 1, growing to ~1.4e-2 by layer 77) is bit-identical across a month of nightlies on different commits; every comparison from that runner against a baseline from another runner has failed. That runner needs to be drained and checked; no threshold can separate it, since its deviation is as large as a real numerics change.
- **The rerun then poisoned the baseline store.** `push_run` skips the tensor upload when the same model + date + sha path is already in the manifest. Attempt 1 pushed its tensors with `pass_label="failed"`; attempt 2 passed and only refreshed meta and appended a `passed` manifest row, so that row now serves attempt 1's deviating tensors as the next baseline (`fetch` takes the newest non-failed row). The next nightly on a healthy runner will compare against them. The same reuse turned an earlier deviation into the baseline in October.

## Changes

- `push_run` skips the tensor upload only for a `failed` push. A passed push at an existing path uploads its own tensors, so a `passed` row always points at tensors from a passing run; a failed push still leaves the earlier tensors in place.
- The CI context records `RUNNER_NAME` as `ci_runner`, promoted to the manifest, so a deviation that follows one machine is visible from the manifest.

The baseline the store holds right now still needs one refresh from a healthy runner (`SGLANG_PRECISION_FORCE_UPDATE=1`); this PR does not write to the store.

## Verification

- Checked locally against a fake `HfApi`: a passed push after a failed one at the same path uploads its own tensors here and skips them on main; a failed push still skips them.
- The nightly test itself is not rerun from this PR: it writes to the shared baseline store.
